requirement: AgentView SHALL expose plan chip and prompt auto-flag visibility from independent plan and permission state, with plan chip visibility requiring usable preview content.
contract: auto_flag_visible SHALL return true only for session auto permission mode without AlwaysApprove, ignoring effective_plan because plan behavior does not hide permission state. should_show_plan_chip SHALL return true only when plan_mode_active or appearance.show_plan_chip is enabled and plan_preview_available is true; exiting plan mode hides the chip by default and a config override cannot show it without content.
scenarios: Auto permission
session permission mode is Auto and AlwaysApprove is inactive
the auto flag is visible regardless of effective plan state.
Always approve
AlwaysApprove is active
the auto flag is hidden even if plan mode is effective.
Plan mode
plan mode is active but no usable plan body exists
the plan chip remains hidden.
Configured chip
show_plan_chip is true but no usable plan body exists
the chip remains hidden rather than showing an empty action.
Input mode evidence
persisted simple/vim mode or pane transitions are exercised by this module's tests
the tests assert mode/pane routing separately from the plan chip predicate.

requirement: AgentView SHALL open a fullscreen plan line viewer from available inline or file content, configure action/feedback controls by approval context, rebuild visible comments, and restore approval focus when reopening.
contract: show_plan_preview_if_available SHALL call show_plan_preview only when plan_preview_available. show_plan_preview SHALL open markdown content or the plan path, toast No plan written yet. when neither is possible, mark the viewer PlanPreview, title it plan.md, make it fullscreen, enable action buttons only outside approval and feedback controls only inside approval, and rebuild approval comments or casual plan_comments when present. reopen_plan_approval SHALL stash the prompt, clear prompt text, focus Preview, reopen the viewer, and if the viewer cannot open focus Prompt; an opened viewer receives feedback_active=true.
scenarios: Available preview
inline approval content or a readable plan artifact exists
a fullscreen plan.md viewer opens in PlanPreview mode.
Unavailable preview
no content and no session path are available
the agent stays without a viewer and shows No plan written yet.
Approval controls
the viewer opens during plan approval
action buttons are disabled and feedback_active is enabled.
Casual controls
the viewer opens without plan approval
plan action buttons are enabled and existing casual comments are overlaid.
Reopen
plan approval is reopened after prompt input
the prompt is stashed, preview focus/viewer is restored when possible, and prompt focus is used when it is not.

requirement: Plan approval actions SHALL send approved, abandoned, or revision feedback responses while restoring the stashed prompt and clearing transient viewer/comment state.
contract: approve_plan and abandon_plan SHALL no-op with Changed when no approval view exists; otherwise they take the view, serialize nonblank formatted comments for approval when present, send the appropriate response, update next_comment_id, restore stashed_prompt, clear line_viewer and casual comment state, log PlanSubmit build/abandon, and return Changed. send_plan_feedback SHALL format supplied feedback with comments, fall back to raw nonblank feedback if formatted text is empty, add a minimal-mode user prompt row for nonblank sent text, send cancellation feedback, restore prompt, clear viewer/undo state, show Plan revision sent., log PlanSubmit revise and return Changed.
scenarios: Approve without comments
approval exists and no comments/feedback require revision
Approved is sent, prompt/viewer state is restored/cleared and build telemetry is logged.
Approve with comments
approval has comments and the user approves
feedback is included in the typed approval response.
Abandon
approval exists and abandon is selected
Abandoned is sent and approval transient state is cleaned.
Revision
nonblank revision text or formatted comments are submitted
cancelled/revision response carries feedback and Plan revision sent. is shown.
Empty revision
prompt is empty and there are no comments
approval remains open and an actionable toast asks for revision notes or a to approve.

requirement: The plan approval key handler SHALL prioritize file-search dismissal, focus navigation, comment save/cancel, direct approval, revision submission, and prompt editing in the documented order.
contract: handle_plan_feedback_key SHALL treat bare Tab as Prompt/Commenting to Preview or Preview to Prompt and discard an in-progress comment when leaving it. Esc SHALL clear file search first, restore a stashed comment prompt or clear text while returning from Commenting to Preview, and otherwise focus Preview. Bare a SHALL approve only when not commenting, prompt text is blank, file search is hidden and no comments exist. route_enter SHALL handle newline, comment save, empty-revision toast, revision submission and non-prompt no-op; remaining keys route through prompt.handle_key and open pending viewer requests.
scenarios: Tab navigation
Tab is pressed in prompt/commenting or preview focus
focus moves between prompt and preview, with comment draft discarded when leaving commenting.
Esc priority
file search is visible, commenting is active, or another plan focus is active
file search clears first; otherwise comment prompt restores/clears and focus returns to preview.
Direct approve
bare a is pressed with empty prompt, hidden file search and no comments
approve_plan is invoked.
Enter revision
Enter is submitted from prompt with text or pending comments
send_plan_feedback is invoked; empty text with no comments produces the revision-notes toast.
Prompt routing
a non-submit key edits the prompt or opens a pending viewer request
InputOutcome::Changed is returned and the requested line viewer opens.

requirement: Plan approval commenting SHALL capture selected source ranges, edit or append PlanComment records, rebuild the preview, and restore the prior feedback prompt on save or cancel.
contract: enter_plan_commenting SHALL edit the comment under the selected physical line when one exists, otherwise capture selected_line_range; visual multi-selection exits while retaining its start identity. It stashes the prompt, records commenting_range/editing_comment_id, focuses Commenting and clears prompt. save_plan_comment SHALL ignore blank text or missing approval/range, update an existing comment or allocate the next id, focus Preview, rebuild comments, and restore stashed feedback or clear prompt. delete_plan_comment_at_cursor SHALL remove only the comment represented by the selected physical line and rebuild; missing viewer/selection/comment is a no-op.
scenarios: Edit existing
cursor is on an approval comment line
the comment text/range is loaded into the prompt and editing mode is entered.
Create comment
cursor has a selected source range without a comment
the range is captured and a new commenting prompt is opened.
Save
a nonblank comment is submitted
the record is created or updated, preview is rebuilt, and the stashed prompt returns.
Blank save
comment text is blank
no comment mutation occurs and the handler reports Changed.
Delete
cursor is on a comment line
that comment is removed and the viewer is rebuilt; unrelated comments remain.

requirement: Casual plan preview commenting SHALL support new/edit comment drafts, prompt restoration, visual selection normalization, cancellation, deletion, and prompt key routing outside the approval modal.
contract: enter_casual_plan_commenting SHALL edit a selected existing plan_comments record or capture a selected source range, exit visual mode while preserving the range start, stash the prompt once, set casual_commenting_range/editing_comment_id and clear prompt. save_casual_plan_comment SHALL treat blank text as cancel, create/update the comment, restore the stashed prompt, rebuild the viewer and return Changed. cancel_casual_plan_commenting SHALL clear casual state and restore/clear prompt. handle_casual_plan_feedback_key SHALL prioritize file-search Esc, then cancel Esc/Tab, Enter save, and other keys through prompt.handle_key. delete_casual_plan_comment_at_cursor SHALL return Unchanged for missing targets and otherwise remove the selected comment and rebuild.
scenarios: New casual comment
a source line/range is selected in a PlanPreview
a stashed prompt and new comment range are created with an empty editor.
Edit casual comment
cursor is on an existing casual comment
its text/range is loaded and edit mode is entered.
Save/cancel
nonblank text is submitted or Esc/Tab is pressed
save creates/updates and restores the prompt; cancel drops draft state without saving.
Delete
cursor is on a casual comment row
the selected comment is removed and viewer annotations rebuild; missing target returns Unchanged.
Input precedence
file search, Enter, Tab, Esc or ordinary prompt editing is active
file search clears first, then save/cancel actions run, otherwise prompt editing handles the key.

requirement: Sending casual plan comments SHALL format comments with available inline or artifact plan content, clear local comment state and viewer, and submit one prompt action.
contract: send_casual_plan_comments SHALL show No comments to send. and return Changed when empty. For nonempty comments it SHALL prefer inline approval content, otherwise read plan.md best effort, format comments with optional plan content, clear comments and reset ids, cancel the line viewer, show Plan feedback sent., and return Action::SendPrompt containing Plan feedback text.
scenarios: Empty send
no casual comments exist
no prompt action is emitted and the no-comments toast is shown.
Inline context
approval view has nonblank plan content
that content is passed to format_plan_comments.
Artifact context
inline content is absent but plan.md is readable
artifact text is used as the formatting context.
Send cleanup
comments are nonempty and send is requested
comments/id/viewer state clears, success toast appears and one SendPrompt action is returned.

requirement: Diagnostic fix identity, registry, and availability projection
contract: Fix identifiers SHALL resolve from canonical `terminal.<name>` and short handles, human_fix_command SHALL emit the canonical doctor command and reject unknown IDs, and applicable automatic fixes SHALL be filtered by finding remediation and planner availability. A local planner failure SHALL classify a fix as unavailable, while a remote SSH session SHALL classify tmux fixes as runnable here and SSH wrapping as runnable locally.
scenarios: Canonical identity
a known canonical ID, short handle, or generated doctor command is supplied
all known forms resolve to the same DiagnosticId and the generated command is `grow doctor fix <handle>`.
Unknown identity
an unknown diagnostic ID is supplied
human_fix_command returns None and resolve_fix_id returns UnknownId.
Finding metadata
a report has or lacks automatic_remediation
only findings with automatic remediation appear in the applicable list.
Planner availability
planning succeeds locally, fails locally, or the terminal is SSH remote
availability is Here, omitted, or RunLocally according to the planner result and fix locality policy.

requirement: Tmux plan paths, managed blocks, safety validation, and preview rendering
contract: Tmux planning SHALL emit one exact independent managed block for each supported option, target the physical `.tmux.conf` under a validated absolute HOME or Byobu directory, and reject unsafe relative, traversal, root, tilde, or newline-containing directories. Preview and reload guidance SHALL shell-quote paths, escape Markdown backticks, expose requested/actual/backup paths for symlinks, and explain that tmux changes require reload or re-running doctor; unavailable Byobu configuration SHALL return ByobuConfigUnavailable.
scenarios: Independent option plan
a supported tmux clipboard, passthrough, or extended-keys fix is requested
the plan contains the exact option line and its own managed markers without an SSH-wrap block.
Unsafe directory
HOME or Byobu directory is relative, traversal-based, root, tilde-based, or contains a newline
planning returns UnsafeDirectory before producing a change.
Safe reload text
a config path contains spaces, quotes, backticks, or newlines
reload text uses safe shell quoting and Markdown code delimiters, or falls back to detach/reattach for unsafe newline paths.
Symlink preview
the requested tmux config is a symlink with backticks in requested, target, or backup paths
the preview renders all paths safely and distinguishes requested from actual file.
Byobu path
Byobu supplies a custom config directory or no config is available
the physical custom path is used, or planning returns ByobuConfigUnavailable.

requirement: Tmux scanner, managed configuration transaction, and idempotence contract
contract: Tmux scanning SHALL recognize healthy or conflicting direct top-level assignments across supported server/window scopes, command separators, environment prefixes, and native command spellings; it SHALL ignore comments, user options, option-name variants, conditionals, and non-global target assignments. Ambiguous or conflicting forms SHALL fail closed as ExistingCustomization. Managed writes SHALL coexist in one Grow block with one item block per option, repair noncanonical managed content even when a healthy direct line exists, reject stale plans, and return AlreadyConfigured without a backup when the exact setting is already present.
scenarios: Scanner healthy forms
a supported option is assigned using accepted scopes, prefixes, separators, or native passthrough spellings
scan_direct_tmux_option returns Healthy.
Scanner ignored forms
the text is a comment, user option, near-name option, conditional, or local target assignment
the scanner returns Absent.
Scanner conflict and ambiguity
a direct option has a bad value, malformed continuation, extra token, missing value, or target ambiguity
the scanner returns ExistingCustomization.
Managed coexistence
each of the three tmux fixes is applied sequentially
all option blocks remain exactly once inside one Grow managed block and each outcome requires reload.
Persistent conflict
an unmanaged direct conflict occurs after a managed block
persistent verification reports the option as not configured.
Repair precedence
a noncanonical managed block conflicts with a healthy direct assignment
planning and apply repair the managed item to the canonical healthy line.
Stale and idempotent apply
the file changes after planning, or already contains the exact setting
apply returns StalePlan for the changed file; an exact setting returns AlreadyConfigured without backup and verifies persistent state.

requirement: SSH shell planning, platform gates, and exact customization conflict detection
contract: SSH-wrap planning SHALL select Bash, zsh, or fish config paths and emit the exact shell-specific managed alias plus operational caveats; it SHALL refuse remote sessions, official VS Code remote sessions, unsupported shells, and (on Windows) automatic shell selection. Conflict detection SHALL preserve existing exact ssh aliases/functions, accept shell whitespace variants, and match only the exact `ssh` name while ignoring `ssh_wrap`, `sshuttle`, and other near-name declarations.
scenarios: Supported shell plan
Bash, zsh, or fish is requested
the plan targets `.bashrc`, `.zshrc`, or `.config/fish/config.fish`, emits the matching alias block, and includes command bypass, ssh forwarding, ControlPersist, and suspend caveats.
Environment gate
the terminal is SSH remote, official VS Code remote, unsupported shell, or Windows
planning returns the corresponding refusal instead of creating a plan.
Existing customization
an exact alias or function already defines ssh
planning returns ExistingCustomization and leaves the original file unchanged.
Whitespace and boundary
supported declarations use varied whitespace or near-name tokens
exact ssh aliases/functions are detected while near-name declarations are ignored.

requirement: Validated shell discovery, source snapshot integrity, and fail-closed decoding
contract: Validator discovery SHALL use an executable explicit shell path as-is, resolve basename-only shell names through PATH to the first executable candidate, and return no validator for a non-executable explicit path rather than substituting a same-basename PATH binary. SSH configuration conflict scanning SHALL use the exact validated source snapshot, reject stale plans before mutation, and fail closed on non-UTF-8 source bytes.
scenarios: Explicit executable
SHELL is an executable custom path
resolve_validator_program returns that exact path.
Basename lookup
SHELL is a basename and PATH contains non-executable then executable candidates
the first executable candidate is returned.
Invalid explicit path
SHELL names a non-executable path
resolution returns None and does not substitute PATH.
Snapshot replacement
the source changes after plan creation
apply returns Managed StalePlan and preserves the replacement content.
Invalid encoding
the existing source contains non-UTF-8 bytes
planning returns Managed UnsafePath before conflict handling.

requirement: SSH managed outcomes, planned-shell verification, and diagnostic report filtering
contract: SSH managed alias detection SHALL ignore comments and the exact Grow-managed alias as configured, but a later unmanaged exact ssh customization SHALL make the file unconfigured. Applying a valid plan SHALL report Applied with the requested ID, changed path, planned shell, and verified managed state; stale plans SHALL preserve user content. configured_report SHALL remove only the SSH-wrap finding when the exact planned alias is verified, while an unconfigured report retains it and a healthy report can still produce an idempotent plan.
scenarios: Managed-only source
the source contains comments and the exact Grow-managed alias
apply returns AlreadyConfigured without a backup.
Later conflict
an unmanaged exact ssh alias/function follows a managed block
managed_alias_configured returns false.
Apply outcome
a Bash plan is applied to an unchanged source
the outcome is Applied, retains SSH_WRAP_ID and Bash, points to the changed path, and verifies the alias.
Stale outcome
the source changes after planning
apply returns StalePlan and leaves the changed source intact.
Planned shell
the process SHELL is absent or belongs to another family after a Bash plan
outcome verification continues to use Bash and configured_report removes SSH-wrap only for that verified outcome.
Report filtering
configured is false or true
the SSH-wrap finding remains or is removed respectively; healthy reports still allow idempotent planning.

requirement: Shell alias runtime expansion and explicit bypass
contract: The generated POSIX and fish SSH aliases SHALL expand `ssh -p 2222 host` into the exact argv sequence `wrap`, `ssh`, `-p`, `2222`, `host`; `command ssh host` SHALL bypass the alias and invoke the underlying executable. The fish alias SHALL not export an `ssh` environment variable, and runtime cases SHALL be skipped only when the shell is unavailable.
scenarios: Bash expansion
bash is available and the generated alias is sourced
grow receives wrap/ssh/options/host as separate arguments in order.
Zsh expansion
zsh is available and the generated alias is sourced
zsh produces the same exact argv.
Explicit bypass
bash defines the alias but invokes command ssh
the fake underlying ssh executable runs and records bypass.
Fish expansion
fish is available and the fish alias is sourced
fish produces the same exact argv and no ssh environment variable is present.

requirement: peek_live_tail_desired_content SHALL budget a no-question live-tail peek from status, optional pinned user, measured body and reply rows while keeping content within max_content and capping body height.
contract: reply_rows SHALL be floored to one. Fixed content is one status row plus reply_rows plus one optional pin row. If max_content is below fixed, live_tail=0 and content_rows=max_content. Otherwise body is measured content or one empty/hint row, capped by MAX_LIVE_TAIL_ROWS and remaining capacity; a blank row is preferred when body and capacity permit, but omitted when no body room remains. content_rows never exceeds max_content.
scenarios: Empty body
body_measured is zero and enough room remains
one live-tail body row plus a breathing blank is budgeted.
Pinned prompt
pin_user is true
one additional pin row is reserved and measured body remains representable.
Tight content
max_content leaves only fixed rows plus body
blank_row is false and body still fits.
Long body
body_measured exceeds available space or MAX_LIVE_TAIL_ROWS
live_tail is capped and content_rows stays within max_content.
Very small box
max_content is below status/reply/pin fixed rows
no body/blank is reserved and content_rows equals max_content.
Fits without marker
the flattened body length is at most the row budget
pure_tail_with_ellipsis returns no ellipsis and preserves every line.
Truncated body
the flattened body exceeds a budget greater than one
one marker is reported and the returned body contains only the newest budget-minus-one lines.
One-row budget
the body exceeds a budget of one
the newest line is retained and no marker is emitted because there is no room for both.
Current-turn measurement
scrollback contains a previous turn and a latest user prompt
densified_body_line_count excludes all entries before the latest user and returns zero for a user-only turn.

requirement: allocate_peek SHALL reserve chrome and a list floor before allocating a peek box, enforce minimum and fractional maximum heights, and return inner content capacity for the chosen whole-box height.
contract: peek_max_box_rows SHALL calculate floor(H * 3/8). allocate_peek SHALL subtract fixed_overhead, reserve min(12, after) list rows, cap remainder by peek_max_box_rows, derive max_content_rows by subtracting two border rows, hide the peek when max_peek is below peek_min_box, and otherwise choose min(max(desired_content_rows+2, peek_min_box), max_peek). chrome_overhead SHALL expose dashboard fixed overhead. max_peek_content_rows SHALL return zero at heights <=8 and otherwise probe the full candidate with the live-tail minimum.
scenarios: No remaining area
area height is fully consumed by fixed overhead
allocate_peek returns show_peek=false and zero box/content heights.
Below minimum
remainder after list floor is below peek_min_box
the peek is hidden while max_content_rows reports the bounded candidate.
Desired content
desired_content_rows grows within the candidate
peek_box_h grows from content plus borders and list shrinks.
Fraction cap
desired content is large
peek_box_h never exceeds floor(height*3/8) and list retains LIST_FLOOR_ROWS when possible.
Short terminal probe
height is 8 or less
max_peek_content_rows returns zero.

requirement: compute_layout SHALL tile the dashboard content area into top margin, header, header gap, list, dispatch, footer and bottom margin rectangles with responsive chrome thresholds and aligned horizontal insets.
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: Top margin exists when height>6, header when height>4, header/list gap when height>10, footer when height>=2, dispatch/footer gaps when height>10, and bottom margin when height>16; a short_terminal flag is height<=8. Header and dispatch use two-column outer padding, list uses LIST_OUTER_HPAD, footer/gaps/margins span the full area. Header and list share x/width, dispatch aligns to those columns, gaps are represented in y spacing, and the rectangles tile the area after intentional gap rows.
scenarios: Tall terminal
the area is 80x30 or otherwise above thresholds
top/bottom margins and header/list/dispatch breathing gaps are reserved.
Short terminal
height reaches a chrome threshold such as 6, 10 or 16
the corresponding margin/gap collapses so list space is preserved.
Column alignment
header, list and dispatch are laid out
header and list align, and dispatch uses the same inset columns.
Outer padding
area is wide enough for insets
dispatch/header/list widths lose their configured padding on both sides while footer remains full width.
Tiling
all layout sections are measured
section heights plus intentional gap rows account for the full area without overlap.

requirement: compute_layout_with_dispatch SHALL grow the dispatch box for multiline input while preserving list/footer spacing, and all layout paths SHALL return valid zero or narrow rectangles without arithmetic panics.
contract: compute_layout SHALL request one dispatch text row. compute_layout_with_dispatch SHALL use max(dispatch_text_rows,1) and add two border rows when no peek is forced; with short_terminal it uses one row. A zero-height area returns all zero-height subrects at the original x/width; zero-width and below-minimum-width areas remain valid with saturated inset widths and leave narrow-mode truncation to the renderer.
scenarios: Multiline input
dispatch_text_rows grows from one to three
dispatch height grows by two rows and list height shrinks by the same amount while footer gap remains.
Zero text rows
dispatch_text_rows is zero
the dispatch still has the single-line three-row chrome.
Zero height
area.height is zero
all subrects have zero height and no underflow/panic occurs.
Zero width
area.width is zero
list and dispatch widths are zero and the layout remains valid.
Narrow area
width is below MIN_DASHBOARD_WIDTH
valid inset subrects are returned for renderer narrow-mode truncation.

requirement: Dashboard peek visibility SHALL grow the dispatch rectangle using list-first allocation while retaining a zero standalone peek rectangle, and callers with a chosen box height SHALL be bounded by the same list floor and fractional cap.
contract: compute_layout_with_peek_box SHALL route a forced height through compute_layout_with_dispatch_inner with at least three rows. When peek_visible without a forced height, short terminals use one dispatch row; otherwise allocate_peek chooses a live-tail box or the fallback three-row dispatch. forced_peek_box_h SHALL be clamped to available remainder, max peek fraction and at least three. The returned peek field remains Rect::default because peek content is rendered inside dispatch; list height stays at least LIST_FLOOR_ROWS whenever allocation permits.
scenarios: Visible live tail
peek_visible is true on a tall area
dispatch grows to the allocated peek box and list remains at least the floor.
Too short
peek_visible is true on a short area
standalone peek is zero and dispatch uses the short one-row path.
Forced height
caller supplies a selected peek_box_h
dispatch uses the bounded forced height and standalone peek stays zero.
Content growth
desired dispatch text rows increase while peek is visible
dispatch grows until max fraction and list gives up only available rows down to floor.

requirement: DashboardLayout SHALL expose named rectangles and allocation DTOs as the geometry contract for renderers, including a retained zero-height peek field and explicit short-terminal/width boundaries.
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: DashboardLayout exposes top_margin, header, header_gap, list, peek, dispatch, footer and bottom_margin. PeekAllocation exposes show_peek, whole-box peek_box_h and max_content_rows. MIN_DASHBOARD_WIDTH documents the meaningful-row threshold while compute_layout still returns valid geometry below it. PEEK_MIN_BOX_QUESTION is available as the question-peek minimum constant even though this module's default allocation path uses the live-tail minimum. The standalone peek rect is intentionally retained at zero for existing destructuring callers while peek rendering occurs in dispatch.
scenarios: Layout consumers
a renderer consumes DashboardLayout
all named sections are available with zero/default rectangles for absent areas.
Compatibility peek
a caller still reads layout.peek
it receives a zero-height rect while dispatch carries the peek allocation.
Question minimum
a question/permission caller selects a different minimum
the public question minimum constant is available for the caller's allocation policy.
Boundary values
height/width is zero, short, narrow or exactly a threshold
layout and allocation return bounded DTOs without overflow.

requirement: Cancellation, rewind resubmission, and orphan prompt response isolation
contract: Cancellation SHALL preserve a prompt block that has already been committed to native scrollback: it SHALL emit the ordinary CancelTurn effect, leave the committed block in scrollback, avoid restoring its text into the composer, and enter cancelling state. After a rewind, the session SHALL become idle with no current prompt id so a new prompt can send immediately; each new turn SHALL receive a distinct prompt id, and late cancelled PromptResponse messages whose promptId does not match the current turn SHALL be discarded without changing the active turn or adding banners.
scenarios: Committed in-flight prompt
a queued prompt has been committed to scrollback before CancelTurn
the prompt remains exactly once in scrollback, the composer stays empty, CancelTurn is emitted, and session state is cancelling.
Immediate post-rewind send
a first turn is cancelled and a second prompt is submitted before the cancelled response arrives
the second prompt sends immediately with a new prompt id and remains turn-running when the orphan first response arrives.
Stacked cancelled responses
two cancelled turns produce two distinct prompt ids and both late responses arrive while no turn is current
both responses are silently ignored, scrollback remains empty, and the session ends idle.

requirement: Inline edit entry, rewind mode selection, and cancellation overlays
contract: Submitting a changed inline edit SHALL enter the same rewind flow as `/rewind`, preselecting the edited prompt and fetching rewind points while keeping the editor open; unchanged or empty text SHALL close the editor without effects. Loaded points SHALL open ModeSelect over the editor, hide the FilesOnly option for inline edit, preserve that hidden state when returning from preview, and retain the FilesOnly option for classic rewind. A busy inline submit SHALL open a targeted CancelOffer; confirming SHALL emit CancelTurn plus FetchRewindPoints and retain the target, while dismissing any mode or cancel overlay SHALL restore the editor text and clear transient rewind state without stashing a resubmit.
scenarios: Changed inline submit
the editor text differs from the original and the session is idle
FetchRewindPoints is emitted, phase is Loading, selected target is the edited prompt, and the editor remains open with no pending resubmit.
No-op inline submit
the editor text is unchanged or empty
no effect is emitted, the editor closes, no rewind state is entered, and inline edit layout is cleared.
Inline points loaded
rewind points arrive for a preselected inline target
phase is ModeSelect with the target and file-change flag, offer_files_only is false, and the editor remains open.
Classic points loaded
classic `/rewind` has no inline editor
ModeSelect keeps offer_files_only true.
Back navigation
an inline All-mode preview has opened and RewindBackToModeSelect is dispatched
ModeSelect is restored with offer_files_only false and the editor still open.
Dismissal
ModeSelect or CancelOffer is dismissed
rewind state and pending inline resubmit are cleared, and the original edited text stays in the editor.
Busy confirmation
a changed inline edit is submitted during a running turn and the cancel offer is confirmed
CancelTurn and FetchRewindPoints are emitted, phase becomes Loading, selected target remains the edited prompt, and the editor stays open.

requirement: Inline edit rewind execution, mode-specific resubmission, and draft reconciliation
contract: A successful inline conversation rewind SHALL arm the edited text only when execution begins, truncate the transcript at the target, close the editor, preserve the composer draft, and resubmit the edited text from the rewound point. All-mode SHALL require preview and confirmation when file changes exist before the same resubmit. FilesOnly SHALL execute without preview when appropriate, leave conversation entries intact, close the editor, and place the edited text in the composer without sending. Resubmission SHALL treat slash-prefixed text literally, and if the active view changed it SHALL append the text to the target agent composer without sending; existing image draft elements and image registrations SHALL survive that append.
scenarios: Conversation-only success
inline edit targets the newest prompt and rewind succeeds in conversation_only mode

RewindExecute is emitted after confirmation, pending text is armed at execute time, transcript is truncated, edited text is sent, editor closes, composer draft survives, and no reverted-conversation notice is added.
All-mode preview
file changes exist and All is selected
RewindPreview is emitted first, then Confirm, then RewindExecute; after success the edited text is resubmitted and editor closes.
Files-only success
FilesOnly is selected for an inline edit with no conversation rewind
RewindExecute is emitted directly, no SendPrompt occurs, editor closes, edited text fills composer, and original prompt/reply remain.
Slash-looking edit
edited text begins with `/`
SendPrompt receives the exact text literally instead of routing it as a slash command.
View switch
the active view changes before successful conversation rewind completes
no SendPrompt is emitted and the text is appended on a new line to the target composer.
Image draft
the target composer contains an image chip before the view switch append
the text is appended while one image chip remains and its drained image retains the re-registered element id.

requirement: Inline rewind failure recovery and editor preservation
contract: A failed rewind execution or an unsuccessful rewind response SHALL emit no further effect, drop pending inline resubmit text, transition to the Error phase, preserve the inline editor and its edited text, and leave the transcript untouched so dismissing the error can return to editing.
scenarios: Execution failure
RewindExecuteFailed carries an error after an inline resubmit was armed
pending_inline_resubmit is cleared, Error phase is shown, no effects are emitted, editor text remains, and transcript length is unchanged.
Unsuccessful response
RewindExecuteComplete contains success=false and an error
the same Error state and editor preservation occur without truncating the transcript.

requirement: Successful rewind memory release and screen-mode confirmation surface
contract: Successful conversation rewinds SHALL remove the transcript tail from the resolved prompt anchor, explicitly drop removed entries before invoking the retained-memory release hook exactly once; FilesOnly SHALL not truncate or purge. Full TUI mode SHALL show the mode-specific success message as a toast without adding a confirmation block to scrollback, while Minimal mode SHALL avoid toasts and append the success notice as a system block.
scenarios: Files-only memory
a successful files_only response does not remove conversation entries
the retained-memory hook count does not increase.
Conversation memory
a successful all response removes the tail from the prompt anchor
scrollback shrinks and retained-memory release is called exactly once after removal.
Full TUI
all or files_only succeeds in non-Minimal screen mode
the correct Reverted conversation/file changes message appears as a toast and no confirmation scrollback block is appended.
Minimal TUI
files_only succeeds in Minimal mode
no toast exists and the exact Reverted file changes system block is committed to scrollback.

requirement: Shell prompt index and scrollback entry lookup with interjection-aware fallback
contract: Prompt lookup SHALL prefer explicit prompt_index metadata and return the corresponding user prompt entry, while the positional fallback SHALL count only indexed non-interjection user prompts. shell_prompt_index_at SHALL resolve an interjection or later block in the same turn to the enclosing prompt and skip interjections for legacy metadata-less scrollbacks; lookup SHALL return None when no matching prompt exists.
scenarios: Explicit index path
user prompt blocks carry prompt_index 0, 1, and 2
find_user_prompt_entry_for_shell_index returns the exact entry index for each shell prompt.
Metadata-less fallback
prompt blocks have no prompt_index and ordinary agent messages separate them
positional lookup returns the first, second, and third real prompt entries.
Interjection fallback
an interjection appears between two real prompts
the next shell index maps to the next real prompt and never to the interjection.
Enclosing turn
the selected entry is an interjection or a block after it before the next prompt
shell_prompt_index_at returns the preceding turn index.
Legacy interjection count
metadata-less shell_prompt_index_at resolves a prompt after an interjection
the interjection is excluded from the count and the prompt receives the correct index.

requirement: Terminal Mermaid dispatch
contract: The pager Mermaid detection layer SHALL inspect the MarkdownRenderView code-block spans, accept a fence when its first whitespace-delimited info token equals `mermaid` case-insensitively, and preserve closed spans in document order. mermaid_blocks SHALL return each clean span body plus its pre-wrap output-line range; mermaid_block_ranges SHALL return only those ranges without cloning sources. MermaidContent SHALL be a source-only detection skeleton with from_view, is_empty, len, and bounds-checked source access; it SHALL not render diagrams or store per-diagram render state.
scenarios: Fence recognition
a code-block info string is mermaid, Mermaid, MERMAID, or mermaid followed by options
the span is included.
Other fence
the first info token is another language or a mermaidx prefix
the span is excluded.
Container cleanup
a Mermaid fence is nested in a blockquote or list
the returned body is de-prefixed clean source.
Document order
multiple closed Mermaid spans occur in one view
blocks and ranges retain source document order.
Streaming fence
a Mermaid fence is not closed yet
no block is reported until the closing fence is present.
Content skeleton
a view contains one detected diagram
MermaidContent exposes its count and source, returns None out of bounds, and has no render state.

requirement: Mermaid affordance routing and dropdown geometry contract
contract: mermaid_display SHALL map RenderMermaid::Off to SourceOnly and Auto/On to Affordances. mermaid_display_static SHALL force SourceOnly for static_commit and otherwise delegate to mermaid_display. affordance_buttons SHALL lay out Open Image, Copy Image Path, and Copy Source left-to-right with a three-column gap from the supplied start column. affordance_row SHALL anchor the label at column 0, keep all three buttons clickable, and add the rendering diagram hint only when rendering is true after the final button plus the same gap.
scenarios: Setting display
render_mermaid is Off, Auto, or On
the inline-art-only or affordance-row display is selected accordingly.
Static commit
static_commit is true for any setting
SourceOnly is returned so a noninteractive reserved row is not committed.
Interactive display
static_commit is false
the normal per-setting display is preserved.
Button order
an affordance row is laid out
the three fixed labels and action kinds occur in Open, CopyPath, CopySource order with three-column gaps.
Render status
rendering is false or true
idle rows have no status; busy rows place `rendering…` after the final button without changing label/button columns.

requirement: The slash suggestion dropdown SHALL count each suggestion as one flat row when its description is empty or cannot receive the minimum description width, otherwise count its Unicode-aware wrapped description lines, and SHALL cap the returned visible row count at MAX_DROPDOWN_ROWS while returning zero for an empty list.
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: desired_item_rows delegates to flat_line_count. flat_line_count computes the shared label column, reserves PREFIX_W plus LABEL_DESC_GAP, treats desc_space below 14 as a single row, wraps descriptions with simple_word_wrap otherwise, and stops counting once the cap is reached. The count therefore describes rendered physical lines rather than suggestion count.
scenarios: Empty suggestions
the item list is empty
desired_item_rows returns 0.
Short-item cap
many short suggestions would exceed MAX_DROPDOWN_ROWS
the returned row count is exactly MAX_DROPDOWN_ROWS.
Wrapped descriptions
a description has enough horizontal space to wrap
the row count is greater than the item count when wrapping adds continuation lines and remains bounded by the cap.
Insufficient description space
the available description width is below 14 columns or the description is empty
the suggestion contributes one physical row.

requirement: The slash dropdown SHALL derive a shared label column from the available content width so command labels, optional kind prefixes, and optional bracketed source tags remain aligned and bounded without overflowing the row.
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: compute_label_column_w uses the full row width below 52 columns and three-fifths of wider content, then caps the result at LABEL_CAP and at the widest row label. kind_prefix appears only when content_w is at least 18; tag_suffix appears only when content_w is at least 52 and contributes bracket plus spacing width; row_label_width includes both metadata pieces. LABEL_DESC_GAP separates the label column from the description, and PREFIX_W reserves the selection gutter.
scenarios: Wide metadata
content width is at least 52 columns
kind and a bracketed tag may be rendered and the tag is included in the shared label width.
Medium command rows
content width is at least 18 but below the tag threshold
the kind prefix and command label remain visible while source metadata is omitted.
Narrow command rows
content width is below 18
the kind prefix is hidden so the command label remains available.
Long dynamic labels
a command or tag exceeds the label budget
the visible label/tag text is truncated to the computed budget and does not write past the row width.

requirement: When the slash snapshot is open and the terminal rectangle has usable geometry, the dropdown SHALL render its visible physical lines with selected and hovered row styles, clamp an out-of-range selected index, and return the source suggestion index associated with each rendered line.
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: render_dropdown returns a default RenderedDropdown for a closed snapshot, zero-height area, or width below 4. For usable geometry it clamps selection to the last item, builds flat lines and item starts, paints only the portion intersecting the buffer (safe under resize races), and computes row_items by partitioning line starts so continuation lines map to their owning suggestion. Selected rows take precedence over hover styling.
scenarios: Closed dropdown
snap.open is false
no dropdown lines are painted and the returned result is empty with no scrollbar.
Tiny or empty geometry
the area height is zero or width is below 4
render_dropdown returns without panicking or hanging.
Selection clamp
the snapshot selected index is greater than the available item count
the last suggestion is treated as selected without indexing outside the item list.
Line-to-item mapping
a suggestion description wraps into continuation lines
row_items contains the owning suggestion index for every visible physical line.
Resize race
a computed paint coordinate falls outside the supplied buffer
the line is skipped or clipped safely rather than writing out of bounds.

requirement: The dropdown SHALL reserve a scrollbar column when the flattened physical-line count exceeds the visible height, choose a scroll offset that keeps the selected line visible with centered bias, and render a styled track/thumb without changing suggestion ownership mapping.
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: render_dropdown detects overflow by counting against visible_rows+1, subtracts two columns from row width when needed, and renders the scrollbar in the rightmost usable columns with total physical lines, visible height, and current scroll offset. The offset is zero when all lines fit, advances to keep the selected start near the middle, and bottoms out when the selected region reaches the end. Returned row_items still maps each line to its source item.
scenarios: No overflow
all flattened lines fit in the visible rows
has_scrollbar is false and no scrollbar column is reserved.
Physical-line overflow
wrapped or numerous suggestions exceed the visible rows
has_scrollbar is true, row width loses the scrollbar gutter, and the visible mapping has one entry per painted row.
Selection near top
the selected line is already within the initial centered viewport
scroll offset remains zero.
Selection near bottom
the selected line plus the centering bias reaches the end
the offset is clamped so the final physical line remains visible.

requirement: Each suggestion SHALL be rendered with a selection gutter, optional kind and tag metadata, highlighted fuzzy-match character spans, and a description aligned after the shared label column; wrapped continuation lines SHALL retain the description indentation and visual row background.
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: build_item_lines emits prompt_arrow for the selected item, applies selected/hover row background through build_flat_lines, truncates the display label to the label budget, emits kind and tag in the configured accent style, and uses build_highlighted_spans to style matched character indices. Descriptions start at PREFIX_W plus label_col_w plus LABEL_DESC_GAP; continuation lines are padded to that same start. Selected styling takes precedence and tag metadata is right-aligned within the label area.
scenarios: Selected suggestion
an item index equals the selected index
the row shows the selection arrow and selected visual style.
Hovered suggestion
an unselected item is hovered
the row uses hover styling without replacing selected styling on another row.
Fuzzy match
match indices identify characters in the display text
matching character spans use the theme accent while the remaining spans use normal text styling.
Wrapped description
description text requires multiple lines
the first line follows the label and continuation lines begin at the shared description indent.
Tagged command
a row has a source tag and sufficient width
the tag is rendered in brackets with accent styling and does not collide with the description.

requirement: The dropdown SHALL wrap description and label text using Unicode display width, normalize embedded newlines, prefer the last fitting word boundary, and fall back to a valid character boundary when a token is wider than the available width.
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: simple_word_wrap returns the original text as one element for width zero, replaces newline characters with spaces, checks UnicodeWidthStr for complete fits, chooses a fitting space using UnicodeWidthChar widths, otherwise scans char_indices until the display width limit and splits on a valid UTF-8 boundary, trimming leading/trailing whitespace before continuing. Wide CJK and long unbroken tokens therefore cannot cause a panic or infinite loop.
scenarios: Zero width
the requested width is zero
the function returns the full text as one line without looping.
Newline normalization
the text contains line breaks
line breaks are treated as spaces during wrapping.
Word boundary
a line contains spaces and a word fits before the limit
the last fitting space is chosen and surrounding whitespace is trimmed.
Long unbroken token
no space fits before the limit
the text is split at a valid UTF-8 character boundary using display width.
Wide Unicode
the text contains CJK or other wide characters
the computed break respects display columns and rendered buffer writes remain bounded.

requirement: Btw overlay state, markdown content, and bounded scrolling
contract: BtwOverlayState SHALL represent Loading, Done, and Error phases while preserving the question; Done SHALL store rendered MarkdownContent with an initial zero offset. `done` SHALL use the shared markdown renderer, scroll_up SHALL saturate at zero, scroll_down SHALL clamp to a supplied maximum, scroll_offset SHALL return zero for non-Done states, and max_scroll_offset SHALL derive wrapped line count at a nonzero width minus the visible body limit. The full selection model SHALL expose every wrapped Done line regardless of the current viewport offset.
scenarios: Done construction
a response is received
the state contains the original question, rendered Markdown content, and scroll offset zero.
Scroll bounds
the caller scrolls a Done response up or down
the offset never underflows and never exceeds the supplied or computed maximum; non-Done states remain offset zero.
Width boundary
content width is zero or the response fits in the body
maximum scroll offset is zero and full selection remains empty only for non-Done/zero-width state.
Full selection
a long Done response is scrolled to a nonzero viewport offset
full_selection_model still includes all response lines with source joiners and stable block indexes.
Markdown source
Done content includes formatting syntax
rendered content is represented by MarkdownContent rather than raw source text.

requirement: Btw panel geometry, status rendering, title truncation, and close affordance
contract: btw_panel_height SHALL return 0 for no state, 3 rows for Loading/Error, and two borders plus one through DONE_MAX_BODY_LINES wrapped body rows for Done. render_btw_panel SHALL no-op for areas below 12 columns or 3 rows, clear and draw a rounded themed border, render a spinner and Answering… for Loading, a width-truncated themed error for Error, and reserve a right-aligned [Esc] close hint before truncating the `/btw <question>` title. Long titles SHALL use an ellipsis; narrow Done panels SHALL fall back to bare [Esc]; the close hit area SHALL remain positive, inside the panel, and on the top border.
scenarios: Panel height
state is None, Loading, Error, or Done with wrapped content
height follows the state-specific border/body rules and caps Done body at DONE_MAX_BODY_LINES.
Loading/error body
the panel is rendered in Loading or Error state
the body shows spinner/status or a width-safe error line, with no Done selection content.
Long title
the question is wider than the title space
the title is truncated with an ellipsis while [Esc] remains visible.
Short title
the question fits
the full `/btw hi` title and [Esc] hint are visible without an ellipsis.
Narrow Done panel
the full position/scroll hint cannot fit
the position indicator is dropped and bare [Esc] remains visible.
Mouse close
a hit area is supplied even with a long question
the hit area is on the top border, has positive width, and stays within the panel rectangle.

requirement: Overlay text selection geometry and complete copy reconstruction
contract: A Done panel SHALL populate a ResolvedSelectionModel using the synthetic BTW_OVERLAY_ENTRY_IDX and range id zero, with one selectable line per rendered body line, source joiners, screen coordinates offset below the top border, and visible block geometry marked drag_startable. Loading and Error states SHALL contribute no ranges or visible blocks. The full model SHALL cover scrolled-out lines so text selection and reconstruction can copy the complete selected span with newline/soft-wrap semantics.
scenarios: Done selection
a Done response is rendered
selection ranges use the synthetic overlay entry/range, line indexes are stable, screen rows begin at body row one, and visible geometry is present.
Non-Done selection
state is Loading or Error
ranges and visible_blocks remain empty.
Viewport scroll
Done content has a nonzero scroll offset
visible line block indexes begin at the offset while the full selection model still starts at zero.
Scrolled-out copy
a drag spans lines outside the current viewport
reconstruct_selection_text returns every selected source line in order, including the correct joiner/newline handling.

requirement: Source-aware Markdown hyperlink, URL, file path, and viewport link overlays
contract: Done rendering SHALL feed the same source-aware collect_content_links pipeline used by scrollback, preserving Markdown hyperlinks and plain URL autolinks as OSC-8 overlay destinations, mapping absolute file paths to file:// targets, and resolving relative project/media links through cwd and media_paths. Overlay links SHALL occupy positive body columns, never the title border, map only visible rows after clamped scrolling, and preserve an outer URL when a URL contains a nested URL query.
scenarios: Markdown hyperlink
Done content contains `[docs](https://example.com/btw-link)`
a body link overlay resolves to the exact HTTPS destination with a positive column span.
Plain URL
Done content contains a bare HTTPS URL
the URL is auto-linked to the same OSC-8 destination.
File path
Done content contains an absolute project file path
the shared collector creates a file:// overlay containing the file name.
Scrolled row
a link is on the last visible line of a long response
its screen row is the visible body row after the scroll offset, rather than its absolute source line.
Nested URL
a URL query contains another HTTPS URL and the content is wrapped/scrolled
the LinkTarget remains the complete outer URL and stays inside the panel rows.

requirement: The workflow overlay SHALL construct pause, resume, and stop slash commands only when the selected run capability permits the operation, with the budget_limited management-available resume exception preserved; unsupported or terminally non-resumable operations SHALL be consumed without dispatch.
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: management_command maps pause/resume/stop to WorkflowRunSnapshot::can_pause/can_resume/can_stop and returns `/workflow-run {op} {name}` only when the gate passes. resolve_management_command first uses that gate, then allows resume for a budget_limited run only when management_available is true. handle_workflows_overlay_input hides the overlay and returns SendSlashCommandPreservingDraft for a resolved command, otherwise returns Changed and keeps the overlay open.
scenarios: Allowed pause/resume/stop
the selected detail or list run reports the corresponding can_* capability
the overlay dispatches the normalized workflow-run command and closes.
Budget-limited resume
the run status is budget_limited and management_available is true
resume dispatches even when the ordinary can_resume gate does not allow it.
Failed-run resume
the run is failed and its resume capability is available
r dispatches `/workflow-run resume <name>` and closes the overlay.
Unsupported resume
a completed, unsupported, or management-unavailable run is selected
no command is dispatched and the overlay remains visible.

requirement: The workflow overlay SHALL translate definition focus, edit, validate, run, publish, and discard actions into `/workflow` prompts, with publish and discard available only for session-scoped definitions; action dispatch SHALL preserve the current draft and close the overlay.
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: definition_command returns None for a missing definition, unknown operation, or publish/discard on a non-session definition. focus, edit, validate, and run include the definition_id and operation-specific instruction; edit explicitly derives a saved definition session draft and limits changes to the next Run. When a definition shortcut or list Enter selects edit, handle_workflows_overlay_input returns Action::SendSlashCommandPreservingDraft, sets show_workflows false, and does not execute the workflow itself.
scenarios: Focus definition
a definition is selected and f or the focus shortcut is pressed
the overlay sends a `/workflow` focus instruction containing the definition id.
Edit definition
a definition is selected and Enter/e or the edit shortcut is pressed
the overlay sends the draft-preserving edit instruction and closes.
Validate or run
a definition is selected and v/r or its shortcut is pressed
the overlay sends the corresponding validation or run instruction with the definition id.
Session publish/discard
a session-scoped definition is selected
p publishes or d discards through the workflow command route.
Non-session publish/discard
a project/user definition is selected
the operation is rejected locally and the overlay remains open.

requirement: Opening workflow details SHALL validate the run identity, reset the workflow view, set both selected and detail run ids, show the overlay, and hide goal detail; list navigation SHALL preserve the selected run identity when newer runs are inserted.
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: open_workflow_detail resolves a name to a run id and delegates to open_workflow_detail_by_run_id. The id variant returns without mutation when the id is absent; otherwise it resets workflows_view, stores selected_run_id/detail_run_id, enables show_workflows, and calls set_goal_detail_visible(false). Key and mouse list activation use the normalized newest-first run snapshot and existing run identity to open details, rather than relying on a stale numeric row index.
scenarios: Valid run open
a name or run id exists in session.workflow_runs
the view is reset, detail and selection point at that run, the overlay is visible, and goal detail is hidden.
Missing run
the requested name or id is absent
the open helper returns without changing the workflow overlay state.
Keyboard list open
the list has a selected run and Enter or Right is pressed
that run becomes detail_run_id and the overlay remains open.
Newest-first insertion
a selected older run remains in the session while a newer run is appended
normalization resolves the selected run by selected_run_id and Enter opens the original run.
Mouse run activation
a left click hits a known run rectangle
the hit run is selected by id, detail is opened, and phase pinning is cleared.

requirement: While the workflow overlay is active, keyboard input SHALL provide modal-local close and navigation: Ctrl-Q bubbles as Unchanged, Esc/q closes or backs from detail, g closes the overlay, Tab/Left backs from detail, arrows select runs or phases, and Enter in detail opens the selected phase transcript when a target exists.
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: handle_workflows_overlay_input ignores key-release events, returns Unchanged for Ctrl-Q, returns Changed for modified local keys without dispatch, and normalizes a cloned WorkflowsView before routing. In detail, Esc/q/Tab/Left clear detail_run_id and phase_pinned when the run list has multiple items (Left always backs even for one run); on the list Left is consumed as a no-op. Up/k and Down/j select phases in detail or list items otherwise. Enter in detail uses transcript_target and open_subagent_fullscreen; Enter/Right on the list opens a definition edit command or the selected run.
scenarios: Ctrl-Q bubble
Ctrl-Q arrives while the overlay is shown
the result is Unchanged and the overlay remains visible for the outer cancel owner.
Close from list
Esc, q, or g arrives while the overlay is on the list
Esc/q close the overlay and g closes it directly.
Back from detail
Esc/q, Tab, or Left arrives in detail
detail and phase pin are cleared while the overlay remains available according to the run-count close rule; Left also works with one run.
List Left no-op
Left arrives while already on the runs list
the event is consumed as Changed without changing selection or closing the overlay.
Run and phase navigation
up/down or j/k arrives in list or detail
the selected run or phase advances within the normalized view.
Detail transcript
Enter arrives in detail and a transcript target exists
the selected child transcript opens fullscreen and the overlay remains underneath.
Modified local key
a local control character carries modifiers
no workflow command is dispatched and the overlay remains shown.

requirement: Entering a workflow detail transcript SHALL target agents in the selected phase, or all agents for a run with no phase data, preferring the newest running agent and falling back to the last available agent; with no agents it SHALL do nothing safely.
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: transcript_target treats an empty phases list plus no current_phase as an all-agent view and otherwise calls agents_in_phase with the selected phase. It searches the returned list in reverse for state == running, then falls back to agents.last(), and clones the agent_id. handle_workflows_overlay_input opens the child fullscreen only when this returns Some.
scenarios: Running phase agent
the selected phase contains both done and running agents
the newest running agent id is selected.
No running agent
the selected phase contains agents but none is running
the last phase agent is selected as fallback.
All-agent run
the run has no phases and no current phase
the target is chosen from the full agent list.
Empty roster
the selected scope has no agents
Enter is consumed as Changed without opening a child view.

requirement: Mouse input owned by the workflow overlay SHALL first honor modal window outcomes and shortcut ids, then activate agent, phase, definition, or run hit rectangles with coordinate containment; unhandled clicks SHALL still return Changed and keep the overlay state stable.
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: handle_workflows_overlay_input delegates mouse events to handle_modal_mouse. CloseRequested applies the same detail-back versus overlay-close policy; OPEN/RUNS mutate run detail and phase pin; definition shortcut ids dispatch definition_command; management shortcut ids dispatch resolve_management_command. For left-down unhandled clicks, detail agent hits open a local child fullscreen, phase hits select and pin a phase, list definition hits select a definition, run hits select/open a run, and empty body clicks are consumed without closing.
scenarios: Agent roster click
a left click is inside an agent hit rectangle and a local subagent view exists
the child transcript opens fullscreen while the workflow overlay stays underneath.
Missing local view
an agent hit has no matching subagent view
the click is consumed and no active subagent is opened.
Phase click
a left click hits a phase row in detail
the phase is selected and phase_pinned becomes true.
Definition click
a left click hits a definition rectangle on the list
the matching definition is selected without executing it.
Run click
a left click hits a run rectangle
the run is selected, detail opens, and phase pinning is cleared.
Empty modal body
a left click misses all registered hit rectangles
the result is Changed and the overlay remains open.
Modal shortcut
the modal helper reports a recognized shortcut
the corresponding open/runs/definition/management behavior is applied before raw hit testing.

requirement: Scrollback entry identity, initialization, timestamps, and lifecycle metadata
contract: EntryId SHALL be a stable, copyable, hashable wrapper around a u64 with explicit construction and value access. ScrollbackEntry::new/with_id SHALL initialize a non-running entry with the block default display mode, pending-input false, raw false, unpinned display mode, empty caches, and a local creation timestamp; running/running_with_id SHALL preserve those defaults while setting is_running. with_display_mode SHALL change only the selected display mode and retain metadata such as created_at. Entry fields SHALL retain block content, hook data, completion timestamp, and pending-user-input state for renderer coordination.
scenarios: Normal entry
a block is wrapped with new or with_id
the entry is not running, has the block default display mode, is not pinned, and receives created_at.
Running entry
a block is wrapped with running or running_with_id
is_running is true, display mode is the block default, and created_at is present.
Explicit identity
an EntryId is constructed or read
new preserves the supplied u64 and value returns it for external handles.
Display builder
with_display_mode is applied to a new entry
the requested mode is stored without clearing the creation timestamp.
Completion metadata
mark_completed is called
running and pending user input are cleared and caches are invalidated.

requirement: Display mode, raw mode, foldability, and thinking visibility controls
contract: ScrollbackEntry SHALL expose display_mode and set_display_mode, invalidate width-dependent render caches when the mode changes, toggle raw rendering only for blocks supporting raw mode, and toggle fold state only when the block or hook data is foldable. Block-owned foldable modes SHALL use next_fold_mode with running state; hook-only foldability SHALL switch Collapsed/Expanded. is_hidden_thinking SHALL report true only for a thinking block when show_thinking is false.
scenarios: Foldable block
toggle_fold is called on an expanded stub/block that supports folding
display mode changes to Collapsed and a second toggle returns to Expanded.
Non-foldable block
toggle_fold is called without block or hook foldability
display mode is unchanged and no invalidation is needed.
Raw-capable block
toggle_raw is called
raw flag and block raw mode toggle together and all content/width caches are invalidated.
Mode assignment
set_display_mode receives a different mode
the mode changes and caches are invalidated; assigning the same mode is a no-op.
Thinking visibility
a thinking block is rendered with show_thinking false or true
is_hidden_thinking is true only in the hidden case.
Running fold cycle
a running thinking block is folded from Collapsed, Truncated, or Expanded
next_fold_mode returns Expanded, Expanded, or Truncated respectively.
Finished fold cycle
a finished thinking block is folded from Collapsed, Truncated, or Expanded
next_fold_mode returns Expanded from Collapsed and Collapsed from the other two modes.
Completion collapse
the caller asks for collapse_mode or finished_display_mode after completion
the resting mode is Collapsed and the optional finished mode is Some(Collapsed).
Raw projection
set_raw_mode is called
MarkdownContent receives the raw-mode setting and its cached source/render projection owns the resulting behavior.
Neutral block geometry
the common renderer queries background, accent_background, padding, or grouping
the block reports None/false/false/false/true for those respective block-level policies.

requirement: Width-aware source line estimation and cheap estimate cache
contract: estimate_source_lines SHALL derive a cheap wrapped-line estimate from searchable source text by stripping one trailing newline, measuring each source line in Unicode display width, summing per-line ceiling divisions at content_width (with minimum width one), and saturating at u16::MAX; no searchable text SHALL estimate as one line. The width-independent line-width profile SHALL survive invalidate_width_caches but be cleared by invalidate_cache. Explicit cheap estimates SHALL be keyed by content width and cleared by invalidate_cache.
scenarios: Per-line ceiling
a multi-line prompt is estimated at widths 10, 5, and 100
each source line is independently ceiling-wrapped and the sums are 5, 8, and 3.
No searchable source
the block has no searchable text
estimate_source_lines returns one line.
Resize invalidation
invalidate_width_caches is called after estimating
the cached width profile remains available.
Content invalidation
invalidate_cache is called after estimating
the width profile and keyed estimate cache are removed.
Explicit estimate key
a stored estimate is queried at its original and another width
the original width hits and another width misses.

requirement: Render output cache keys, selection branches, and edit boundary sidecars
contract: ensure_cached SHALL lazily render and memoize RenderedBlockOutput under width, raw flag, current theme, effective selection, and cwd keys. Selection SHALL affect the cache key only for UserPrompt, ToolCall, Thinking, BgTask, and Subagent blocks; other block selection changes SHALL normalize to false. cached_output_ref SHALL borrow the validated render output, output SHALL reuse it for ordinary rendering, and effective_output SHALL return Cached or Selected kind with a context reflecting selection and vertical padding. Edit blocks SHALL retain boundary sidecar metadata in modes where boundaries are rendered and clear it in collapsed mode.
scenarios: Cache hit/miss
the same block is output at the same and a different width
the same-width call reuses valid output and width change regenerates output without changing logical line count.
Edit boundaries
an edit block is cached expanded, selected, then collapsed
boundary sidecar remains available for expanded output and is empty for collapsed output.
Unselected effective output
effective_output is requested with is_selected false
kind is Cached and output is available through the borrowed cache.
Selected effective output
effective_output is requested with is_selected true
kind is Selected, ctx.is_selected is true, and output is available.
Cache key context
theme, cwd, raw, width, or an output-varying selection changes
the cached rendering is regenerated; irrelevant selection changes do not thrash non-varying blocks.

requirement: Truncated height caching, width invalidation, eviction, and render contexts
contract: ensure_truncated_height_cached SHALL compute the Truncated block output height plus vertical padding and cache it by content width, raw flag, current theme, and cwd, excluding selection because line count is selection-independent. Repeated calls with an unchanged key SHALL return the cached height; width/raw/theme/cwd changes SHALL replace it. invalidate_width_caches SHALL clear render, truncated-height, and estimate caches while retaining the width-independent profile; invalidate_cache SHALL clear all caches, and evict_render_cache SHALL drop heavyweight render caches while preserving cheap layout estimates. Context builders SHALL preserve entry state while applying optional mode, row budget, selection, appearance, and cwd overrides without mutating display_mode.
scenarios: First height call
truncated height is requested for an uncached entry
a positive height is returned and the cache is populated.
Height cache hit
the same width/raw/theme/cwd is requested twice
the height and cached tuple remain unchanged.
Height width miss
the width changes from 80 to 40
a new tuple is stored with width 40.
Full invalidation
invalidate_cache follows a populated height/output cache
both truncated height and cached output are cleared.
Resize invalidation
invalidate_width_caches is used for terminal resize
width-keyed caches clear while source width profile survives.
Context override
a caller requests budget, mode, mode+budget, or selection context
the returned BlockContext carries the override and cwd/appearance without mutating the entry.

requirement: Tool hook rendering and output composition
contract: When hook_data is attached, output_with_hooks SHALL render the base tool block followed by lifecycle/pre/post hook content according to the requested display mode. Collapsed output SHALL append an inline [hooks: N/M] suffix to the first header line when hook content exists; expanded output SHALL insert a hook separator for non-lifecycle blocks, append pre/post sections and lifecycle details, and omit the redundant separator/section header for lifecycle blocks whose event name is already the block header. The injected output SHALL retain the base RenderedBlockOutput sidecar boundaries.
scenarios: Collapsed hooks
a hook-bearing tool entry is rendered in Collapsed mode
the first line receives the inline hook summary when available.
Expanded tool hooks
a non-lifecycle ToolCall has pre/post/lifecycle hook runs
a separator and mode-specific hook sections follow the tool output.
Lifecycle block
the block itself is a lifecycle tool event
the separator and redundant section header are skipped while hook details are appended.
No hooks
hook_data is absent or empty
base block output is returned unchanged.

requirement: The agent catalog modal SHALL expose a single Agents surface while retaining typed tab identity, initialize its window/list/search/selection state from the cwd and toggle map, and report close, change, no-op, view, and editor-refresh outcomes without mixing surface semantics.
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: AgentsTab::ALL contains only Agents and label returns Agents. AgentsModalState::new creates a one-tab ModalWindowState, builds the agent list, starts selection/scroll/search empty, stores cwd/default_agent/active_agent, and clears hit mappings/message. AgentsModalMessage distinguishes Error and Info; AgentsModalOutcome carries Close, Changed, Unchanged, ViewAgent metadata/content, or EditInEditor path/tab. refresh_after_editor rebuilds entries from current toggle configuration and clamps selection.
scenarios: Single surface
the modal asks for its available tabs
ALL contains only Agents and the label is Agents.
Fresh state
AgentsModalState::new receives cwd, toggles, bundle and optional active agent
the modal starts on Agents with built entries, zero selection/scroll, inactive search, and resolved default agent.
Editor refresh
an editor action returns to the modal
the agent catalog is rebuilt from the cwd and persisted toggles, with selection clamped.
Message kind
an operation reports an error or informational status
the message preserves its typed kind and text.

requirement: The agent catalog SHALL include the user-visible built-ins, discover project/user/bundled definitions from the cwd, resolve name collisions by scope priority, suppress non-project built-in subagent duplicates, and preserve enabled/source/scope/definition metadata for each entry.
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: build_agent_list seeds Grow, GeneralPurpose, Explore, and BrowserUse as enabled built-ins by default, then consumes agent::discovery::discover(cwd). Built-in discoveries are skipped; subagent variant names are suppressed outside Project scope; collisions replace only when Project > User > Bundled > BuiltIn. Each AgentListEntry records name, description, scope, optional source path, builtin flag, enabled toggle, expansion state, and full AgentDefinition. build_switch_agent_catalog filters primary-agent-eligible definitions, deduplicates names, projects AgentArg name/description/scope, and appends qualified trusted-plugin or frontmatter-only untrusted-plugin agents.
scenarios: Built-in baseline
the cwd has no custom definitions
the four user-visible built-ins are present and enabled unless explicitly toggled.
Scope override
the same name is discovered at multiple scopes
the highest priority project/user/bundled definition replaces the lower-priority entry.
Subagent collision
a built-in subagent name is discovered outside Project scope
the duplicate is omitted; a project-scoped definition may replace it.
Switch catalog eligibility
a definition is not primary-agent eligible or its name was already seen
it is omitted from the switch catalog.
Plugin discovery
an enabled plugin exposes agent markdown files
trusted plugins parse full definitions while untrusted plugins use frontmatter-only parsing, names are qualified as plugin:name, and duplicate qualified names are skipped.

requirement: Agent selection and spawn toggles SHALL read effective configuration, resolve a non-empty configured default before the MVP resolver fallback, and persist default-agent and subagent-toggle changes through the editable config document while returning explicit errors for unreadable or malformed configuration.
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: load_agent_toggle reads subagents.toggle boolean entries and otherwise returns an empty map. resolve_default_agent_name uses a non-empty AgentSelectionConfig.name first, otherwise MvpAgent::resolve_agent_definition(...).selector_identity(). set_default_agent creates the config parent, reads an editable TOML document, creates [agent] when needed, writes or removes agent.name, and writes the document back. toggle_agent similarly creates [subagents].toggle and writes the requested boolean. Both operations surface read/parse/table/write failures as String errors; handle_agents_key refreshes default or list state only after success.
scenarios: Configured default
effective config contains a non-empty agent.name
resolve_default_agent_name returns that exact name.
Resolver fallback
agent.name is absent or empty
the MVP agent resolver supplies selector_identity as the default.
Set default
s is pressed for a selected agent that is not the current configured name
agent.name is persisted and the state message reports the new session default.
Clear default
s is pressed for the currently configured default
agent.name is removed and the resolved fallback is reported.
Toggle spawn
t is pressed for a selected entry
the corresponding subagents.toggle boolean is persisted and the list is rebuilt.
Config failure
the config cannot be read, parsed, or has a wrong table shape
the operation returns an error message and does not claim success.

requirement: The agent modal SHALL filter case-insensitively over agent name and description, keep selection within the filtered entries, saturate navigation at both edges, and expand or collapse only the selected entry without panicking on an empty result.
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: filtered_indices returns all indices for an empty query, otherwise lowercases query/name/description and returns matching source indices. select_next/select_prev no-op when no matches, choose the first/last match when current selection is outside the filtered set, and saturate at the corresponding edge. reset_selection_after_search_change selects the first current match. expand/collapse mutate only the selected AgentListEntry when it exists.
scenarios: Empty query
the search query is empty
all agent indices are returned in catalog order.
Name or description match
the lowercased query occurs in either field
the matching source indices are returned and non-matches are excluded.
Search selection reset
editing the query changes the filtered set
selection moves to the first matching entry when one exists.
Navigation edges
j/k or arrows reach the first/last filtered entry
further movement remains at that edge.
No matches
the filtered set is empty
navigation returns without changing selection.
Expand/collapse
e/Right or E/Left targets a selected entry
only that entry's expanded flag changes.
