requirement: The agent modal SHALL render centered modal chrome with search/message state, visible/default/spawn markers, descriptions and optional expanded details, selected-row highlighting, bounded scrolling, truncated text, and row_map entries that map agent and description rows back to their source index.
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: format_agent_detail emits role composition, tool count/list with name_override or id suffix, skills, source path, and scope. synthesize_agent_markdown uses the definition prompt body or a base-system-prompt fallback; render_prompt_body resolves tool template variables through TemplateRenderer and falls back to the original body on render error. render_agents_modal uses modal_sizing/shortcuts, records content_rect, paints message and search/cursor, builds Agent/Description/Detail RenderRows with active/default/spawn-off suffixes, keeps selected rows highlighted, adjusts scroll to selected row and content height, truncates by content width, and records row_map for owned rows.
scenarios: Agent row markers
an entry is active, default, disabled, or expanded
the row includes the corresponding active/default/spawn-off marker and detail rows when expanded.
Detail metadata
an expanded definition has tools, skills, source, or scope
the detail view shows role composition, tool names, skills, source, and scope lines.
Built-in view
Enter/o selects an entry without a source_path
ViewAgent includes synthesized markdown using the prompt body or base-system fallback.
File-backed view
Enter/o selects an entry with a source_path
ViewAgent carries the source path and no synthesized content.
Viewport scroll
the selected row lies above/below available content
scroll is adjusted and clamped so the selected row is visible.
Narrow content
row text exceeds content width
truncate_str clips display text to the content width without overpainting; row_map still identifies owned rows.

requirement: Agent modal input SHALL give active search first ownership, delegate modal chrome before local controls, map navigation/fold/page/view/search/default/toggle keys to typed outcomes and persistence, accept paste only into active search, and route mouse close, scroll, selection, and expansion through content hit rows.
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: handle_agents_key clears transient messages, handles search Esc reset and Enter commit, maps remaining keys through LineEditor and line_edit_outcome, otherwise lets modal_window handle close before local j/k, e/E, page and Ctrl-d/u, Enter/o, /i, q, s and t branches. View uses source path or synthesized content; s toggles/clears default and refreshes on success; t toggles enabled and rebuilds on success. handle_agents_paste returns Unchanged when search is inactive, otherwise inserts text and resets selection after changes. handle_agents_mouse lets modal chrome close/handle first, ignores outside-content events, scrolls selection, and on a left row click toggles expansion for the selected row or selects another agent.
scenarios: Search editing
search is active and Esc/Enter/text/paste arrives
Esc resets and exits search, Enter commits and exits, text changes update selection, and handled editor events return Changed.
Modal close
modal chrome reports CloseRequested or q is pressed
the outcome is Close.
Navigation and fold
j/k, arrows, page keys, e/E or Right/Left arrive outside search
selection or expansion changes and the outcome is Changed.
View action
Enter/o targets an existing agent
ViewAgent carries its title, source path, and optional built-in content.
Default/toggle action
s or t targets a selected agent
configuration is persisted, state is refreshed on success, and failures become typed messages while the event remains Changed.
Paste outside search
paste arrives while search is inactive
the outcome is Unchanged and state is not edited.
Mouse content routing
scroll or left click occurs inside content_rect
selection moves or the mapped row selects/expands; outside content returns Unchanged.

requirement: Prompt-to-entry mapping with explicit metadata and interjection-aware fallback
contract: The dispatcher SHALL map shell prompt indexes to scrollback user-prompt entries by preferring explicit prompt_index metadata from the newest matching entry, then falling back to positional counting of non-interjection UserPrompt blocks. shell_prompt_index_at SHALL walk backward from an entry, skip mid-turn interjections to the enclosing prompt, return explicit metadata when present, and count only indexed user prompts for legacy metadata-less scrollbacks. Missing anchors SHALL return None.
scenarios: Explicit lookup
scrollback contains prompt_index 0, 1, and 2
find_user_prompt_entry_for_shell_index returns each matching entry index.
Positional lookup
prompt metadata is absent
the fallback returns the first, second, and third real user prompt while ignoring interjections.
Interjection anchor
the selected entry is an interjection or a block after it before the next prompt
shell_prompt_index_at resolves to the preceding enclosing turn.
Legacy interjection count
a metadata-less prompt follows an interjection
the interjection is excluded from the shell index count.
No match
no user prompt can anchor the target
the helper returns None rather than inventing an entry.

requirement: Rewind entry dispatch, busy cancellation, draft stashing, and session effects
contract: dispatch_rewind and dispatch_rewind_show_picker SHALL operate only on the active Agent view and an agent with a session id; otherwise they SHALL return no effects and report No active session when applicable. They SHALL dismiss a stale jump picker, derive the selected shell prompt anchor, stash a nonempty composer draft, and enter Loading with FetchRewindPoints when idle. When the session is busy they SHALL enter a targeted CancelOffer instead. dispatch_rewind_cancel_offer SHALL preserve anchor/target/draft, enter Loading, emit CancelTurn with cancel_subagents=true and rewind_if_pristine=false, then fetch points; it SHALL avoid removing the in-flight prompt itself.
scenarios: Idle rewind
the active agent has a session and is idle
jump picker is dismissed, draft is stashed, Loading state is created, and FetchRewindPoints is emitted.
Busy rewind
the active agent is busy
no fetch is emitted immediately; CancelOffer stores the anchor, selected shell index, and draft.
Busy confirmation
the cancel offer is confirmed
CancelTurn precedes FetchRewindPoints, target survives, and the rewind flow owns history cleanup.
Committed prompt
the in-flight user block was already committed
rewind dispatch does not restore/remove the committed block; ordinary cancellation leaves it printed.
Late cancellation response
a cancelled PromptResponse belongs to an old prompt id
the cross-dispatch task-result path discards it while the new turn remains active.

requirement: Rewind points resolution, picker/mode state machine, and inline edit entry
contract: handle_rewind_points_loaded SHALL retain returned points, restore a stashed draft on an empty response and toast No rewind points available, resolve a desired inline target or sort ordinary points descending into Picker, select and center the matching scrollback anchor, and create ModeSelect with file-change metadata. Inline edit SHALL hide FilesOnly because conversation rewind is implicit; classic rewind SHALL offer it. Mode selection SHALL require a conversation-only confirmation for target zero, execute conversation-only directly for other targets, execute All/FilesOnly directly when no file changes exist, and emit RewindPreview before confirmation when file changes exist. Dismiss/back actions SHALL preserve draft and inline editor while rebuilding the appropriate state.
scenarios: Inline submit
inline edit text differs from the original and the session is idle
Loading is entered with selected target and FetchRewindPoints is emitted while editor stays open.
No-op submit
inline text is empty or unchanged
editor exits with no rewind state or effects.
Targeted points
points load for a selected inline prompt
ModeSelect targets the point, carries has_file_changes, and hides FilesOnly.
Classic points
ordinary `/rewind` points load without inline editor
ModeSelect offers FilesOnly.
All mode
file changes exist
RewindPreview is emitted and successful preview transitions to Confirm.
Direct mode
conversation-only or files-only has no file changes
RewindExecute is emitted and inline text is armed only at execution.
Busy inline submit
inline edit is submitted during a running turn
CancelOffer is targeted at the edited prompt; confirm cancels and fetches points, dismiss returns to editing.
Back/dismiss
the user dismisses or backs out of an overlay
rewind state is cleared or rebuilt, pending resubmit is absent, and editor text/draft remains.

requirement: Successful rewind application, inline resubmission, and composer/image preservation
contract: dispatch_rewind_success SHALL consume pending inline resubmit text, transition unsuccessful responses to Error, and on success close the inline editor before mutating its transcript anchor. Non-files-only modes SHALL remove the target tail, drop removed entries before releasing retained memory, clear rewind points, move to the prompt pane/bottom, and show a mode-specific confirmation as toast or minimal scrollback notice. FilesOnly SHALL preserve conversation, place inline text in the composer, and avoid SendPrompt. Non-files-only inline resubmission SHALL restore the full draft and send the edited text literally with consume_input=false when the agent view is active; if the view changed, it SHALL append text to that agent composer without clobbering existing text or image chips.
scenarios: Conversation-only inline success
execution succeeds for the newest prompt
transcript truncates, inline editor closes, pending text is sent, composer draft survives, and no redundant revert notice is added.
All-mode success
preview/confirm completes successfully
the same inline text is resubmitted after RewindExecute.
Files-only success
files-only execution succeeds
no prompt is sent, editor closes, text fills composer, and original transcript remains.
Literal slash text
edited text starts with `/`
dispatch_send_prompt_inner receives it with literal=true as a prompt.
View switch
active view changes before completion
the edited text is appended to the target composer and no SendPrompt is emitted.
Image draft
target composer already contains an image
append preserves one image chip and its element id/image registration.

requirement: Rewind preview and execute failure recovery
contract: Preview completion SHALL convert clean files and conflicts into Confirm state with ConflictDisplay projections, but an error with no clean files or conflicts SHALL enter Error without effects. Preview failure SHALL preserve anchor/draft in Error. Execute failure or a success=false response SHALL clear pending inline resubmit text, preserve the inline editor and transcript, retain the draft for dismissal, and expose the error message until the user dismisses it.
scenarios: Preview success
preview returns clean files or conflicts
Confirm state carries target, mode, files, conflict displays, prompt preview, and active selection index zero.
Preview error
preview returns an error with no file details
Error state is entered and no effect is emitted.
Execute failure
TaskResult reports RewindExecuteFailed
pending resubmit is dropped, editor remains open, transcript is untouched, and Error state is visible.
Unsuccessful execute
RewindExecuteComplete has success=false
the same error recovery occurs using response.error or unknown error.

requirement: Rewind success memory release and presentation by screen mode
contract: Successful conversation rewind SHALL remove scrollback from the resolved prompt anchor and call release_retained_memory_with exactly once after dropping removed entries; files-only SHALL not truncate or purge. Full TUI SHALL present the exact mode-specific success as a toast and avoid appending a system block, while Minimal SHALL avoid toast and append the corresponding notice block because committed lines cannot be erased.
scenarios: Files-only side effect
files_only succeeds
scrollback is unchanged and retained-memory release is not called.
Conversation side effect
all/conversation_only succeeds with a matching anchor
scrollback tail is removed and retained-memory release runs once after drop.
Full screen
screen mode is non-Minimal
toast says Reverted conversation, Reverted file changes, or Reverted conversation and file changes and scrollback has no confirmation block.
Minimal screen
screen mode is Minimal
no toast exists and a Reverted system notice is committed to scrollback.

requirement: Input flight recorder dump dispatch
contract: dispatch_dump_input_log SHALL operate only for an active Agent with a nonempty input recorder. It SHALL snapshot recorder entries and timing, terminal diagnostics, session id, pager version, active pane, prompt cursor/text length/selection state, and write a pretty JSON InputDump under grow_home()/logs with a UTC timestamped input-debug filename, creating the logs directory best-effort. Empty logs show a toast; serialization and file-write failures show a toast and return no effects; successful writes show an event-count/path toast and emit a unified diagnostic message keyed by session id. The dump includes recorder entries from a snapshot and does not clear the recorder.
scenarios: No active agent
the active view is Welcome/Dashboard or its agent id is missing
the operation returns no effects without creating a dump.
Empty recorder
an active agent has zero recorded events
a no-events toast is shown and no file is written.
Successful dump
an active agent has recorded events and serialization/file I/O succeed
a timestamped JSON file is written under grow_home/logs, a path/count toast is shown, and unified diagnostics logs the count/span.
Serialization failure
InputDump cannot serialize
a failure toast is shown and no file-write path is attempted.
Write failure
log-directory or dump-file writing fails
a failure toast is shown; the dispatcher returns an empty effect list without panic.

requirement: The tool block module SHALL expose a typed ToolCallBlock sum over all supported tool and lifecycle variants, re-export each concrete block and its public helper types, and provide stable shared primitives for header selection ranges and one-based line ranges.
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: ToolCallBlock covers Execute, Read, Edit, ListDir, Search, WebFetch, IntegrationSearch, UseTool, MemorySearch, Skill, Other, and Lifecycle. The module re-exports concrete block types/helpers from submodules and defines TOOL_HEADER_RANGE as zero for a single logical path/query/url/command selection target. LineRange stores 1-based inclusive start/end values, formats `start:end` for display and `start-end` through Display.
scenarios: Variant coverage
a new tool kind is represented in scrollback
it must be added to the explicit ToolCallBlock enum and module exports before delegation/classification can compile.
Header selection
a tool header is rendered as one logical copy target
all tool kinds can share TOOL_HEADER_RANGE zero for the header range.
Line range display
a one-based range is created
display returns colon-separated bounds while Display returns hyphen-separated bounds.

requirement: ToolCallBlock SHALL dispatch common BlockContent output, styling, folding, selection, media, and preamble behavior to the matching inner block; it SHALL obtain the tool bullet from appearance, and SHALL keep coordination-bearing Other tools out of dense grouping.
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: The delegate_tool macro exhaustively dispatches output, accent, bullet, accent_background, background, vpad, raw/fold modes, selectability, image/media/open-button, and preamble to every concrete variant including Lifecycle. has_bullet reads the configured scrollback tool bullet rather than the inner variant. is_groupable returns false only for Other with coordination metadata; all other variants are groupable. The module itself does not prepend the bullet, leaving that to RenderBlock output composition.
scenarios: Inner projection
a caller asks a ToolCallBlock for BlockContent behavior
the same method is invoked on its concrete inner variant.
Configured bullet
tool bullet appearance has a character
has_bullet reports true regardless of the specific tool variant.
Coordination tool
an Other block carries coordination data
is_groupable is false so it does not merge into a dense run.
Ordinary tool
an ordinary tool, lifecycle, or Other without coordination is considered
is_groupable is true and its inner behavior remains available.
Collapsed header
a memory search block is rendered in Collapsed mode
the query is the selectable header target, the label/suffix are excluded from selection, and a result count is shown only when results are present.
Expanded result list
a block is rendered in Truncated or Expanded mode with results
the output contains wrapped header metadata, one numbered path/range/score/source row per result, and at most three non-empty snippet lines per result.
No results
results and error are both absent in a non-collapsed mode
a separator and muted `(no results)` line are appended.
Error presentation
error is present
a colored error line is appended, foldability is disabled, and the error accent/bullet is reported even when collapsed.
Fold and protocol policy
the common renderer queries the block protocol
default mode is Collapsed, collapse_mode returns Collapsed, next_fold_mode toggles only Collapsed and Expanded, and raw/background/padding capabilities remain disabled as implemented.

requirement: ToolCallBlock SHALL preserve timing when a running block is replaced by the same variant, allow cross-variant started_at assignment, start timing only once for runnable variants, leave lifecycle events untimed, and report success from the inner block or true for lifecycle events.
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: transfer_timing_from copies started_at only for matching timing-bearing variants and skips mismatches. set_started_at sets Some(instant) for Execute/Read/Edit/Search/ListDir/WebFetch/IntegrationSearch/UseTool/MemorySearch/Skill/Other but is a no-op for Lifecycle. start_timing fills None with Instant::now and never overwrites an existing timestamp; Lifecycle is always a no-op. is_success delegates to all timing-bearing variants including MemorySearch and returns true for Lifecycle.
scenarios: Completion replacement
a completed block replaces a running block of the same variant
started_at is transferred so elapsed time can include the original run.
Variant transition
a new block is assigned a captured instant from a different variant
set_started_at stores it on the new timing-bearing variant.
First start
a runnable block has no started_at
start_timing records the current instant.
Repeated start
a runnable block already has started_at
start_timing preserves the original instant.
Lifecycle event
the block is Lifecycle
timing mutators do nothing and is_success is true.
Tool failure/success
an inner block exposes its success state
is_success returns that inner result.
Construction
a memory search block is created from a query
query is retained and results, error, started_at, and elapsed_ms start empty.
Error completion
set_error receives an error while started_at exists and elapsed_ms is empty
elapsed_ms is captured once before the error is stored.
Finish idempotence
finish is called after timing was stored or more than once
stored elapsed_ms is preserved and no new duration replaces it.
Live timing
elapsed_ms is requested before completion while started_at exists
the current elapsed milliseconds are returned without mutating the stored field.

requirement: ToolCallBlock::from_name SHALL case-normalize known ACP/tool names into their concrete block variant, preserve the supplied summary, use the Creating prefix for write, and represent unknown names as Other while preserving the original name.
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: from_name lowercases the input and recognizes terminal aliases run_terminal_command/run_terminal_cmd/bash/shell/execute; read_file/read; search_replace/edit/apply_patch/strreplace; write; list_dir/ls; grep/search/glob; web_fetch/fetch; search_tool; use_tool; and skill. Known names construct the corresponding inner block, write applies with_prefix("Creating "), skill uses OtherToolCallBlock name Skill, and all unmatched names construct OtherToolCallBlock with the original name and summary.
scenarios: Shell alias
the source name is any recognized shell alias
an Execute block is created with the supplied summary.
Edit/write alias
the source name is an edit alias or write
an Edit block is created; write carries the Creating prefix.
Search/fetch/integration alias
the source name matches the corresponding alias set
Search, WebFetch, IntegrationSearch, or UseTool is constructed.
Skill
the source name is skill
a Skill variant using the Skill label is constructed.
Unknown tool
the source name is not recognized
Other preserves that name and the supplied summary.

requirement: ToolCallBlock::searchable_text SHALL build cheap full-text search input from stored source fields and copy accessors without layout or syntax highlighting, joining non-empty values and returning no fabricated text for empty sources.
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: Execute contributes command, description, output, error; Read path/content/error; Edit copy_text/error; ListDir path/output/error; Search pattern, path/glob/file type, file paths, every file match path and matched content, error; WebFetch URL/output/error; IntegrationSearch copy_text/content/error; UseTool copy_text/error; MemorySearch query, every result source/path/snippet, error; Skill/Other name/summary/output/error; Lifecycle name. join_searchable combines the optional fields and the method does not call output or wrap/highlight content.
scenarios: Command indexing
an Execute block has command, description, output, or error
search text contains those stored fields in joined form.
Structured search indexing
a Search or MemorySearch block has metadata/results
patterns, file metadata/matches, or result source/path/snippet fields are flattened into the index.
Copy accessor indexing
an Edit, IntegrationSearch, or UseTool block has source data
the block-specific copy_text representation is included without rendering the block.
Lifecycle indexing
a lifecycle event exists
its name is searchable.
No layout side effects
search indexing is requested
the method reads stored fields only and does not perform display wrapping or syntax highlighting.

requirement: VerbGroupKind SHALL provide tense-aware verbs and singular/plural nouns for every semantic group, while ToolCallBlock::verb_group_kind SHALL return only eagerly foldable non-destructive kinds and label_kind SHALL additionally bucket action tools for aggregate hidden-row labels; lifecycle chrome and coordinated Other tools remain unlabelled where specified.
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: VerbGroupKind maps File/Skill to Read/Reading and file/skill nouns; Search/MemorySearch/IntegrationSearch to Searched/Searching; Dir to Listed/Listing; WebFetch to Fetched/Fetching; Subagent/Command/OtherTool to Ran/Running; EditFile to Edited/Editing; McpCall to Called/Calling. noun uses singular only for count==1 and explicit irregular memories/MCP forms. verb_group_kind maps Read (Skill path detection), ListDir, Search, WebFetch, IntegrationSearch, MemorySearch, Skill; excludes Execute/Edit/UseTool/Other/Lifecycle. label_kind extends the map with Command/EditFile/McpCall and non-coordinated OtherTool, while Lifecycle is None.
scenarios: Running group
a foldable run is still running
verb returns its present-tense form such as Reading or Searching.
Finished group
a foldable run is not running
verb returns the past form such as Read or Searched.
Plural count
an aggregate label count is one or greater than one
noun uses the singular for one and the explicit plural for larger counts.
Skill read
a Read block path identifies a skills entry
verb_group_kind and label_kind classify it as Skill rather than File.
Action label
a hidden-row header describes Execute/Edit/UseTool/ordinary Other
label_kind supplies Command/EditFile/McpCall/OtherTool even though verb_group_kind is None.
Lifecycle/coordination
the block is Lifecycle or Other with coordination metadata
the corresponding group decision is None or non-groupable, so no misleading aggregate label is emitted.

requirement: Turn cancellation preference resolution, cancel panel choices, and wire intent
contract: Cancel dispatch SHALL resolve the per-agent cancel_subagents_preference before the global UI preference, interpret canonical always_stop/always_continue values, and default to stopping subagents when no choice exists. A running turn without running subagents SHALL emit CancelTurn immediately; running subagents SHALL open a focused choice panel unless a remembered preference applies. One-shot StopRunning/ContinueToRun choices SHALL only affect the current cancel; AlwaysStop/AlwaysContinue SHALL apply to every agent in memory, update current UI state, and emit PersistSetting only when the canonical value changes. Trigger hints SHALL be forwarded and consumed, the shared queue SHALL remain server-authoritative, idle cancellation SHALL no-op, and a second cancel while the panel is open SHALL fall through to a real cancel.
scenarios: Immediate cancel
a running turn has no running subagents
CancelTurn is emitted with cancel_subagents=true and session enters cancelling.
Trigger propagation
a cancel trigger hint is present or absent
the effect carries that one-shot hint or None and the hint is consumed.
Subagent panel
running subagents exist and no remembered preference applies
no effect is emitted, panel running_count is set, and turn remains running.
One-shot choice
StopRunning or ContinueToRun is selected
CancelTurn carries true or false without changing global preference.
Persistent choice
AlwaysStop or AlwaysContinue is selected
all agents and current UI receive canonical preference and PersistSetting records the change.
Queue authority
shared queue contains prompts
cancel does not mutate queue or emit QueueRemove; agent/server drains the front next.
Retry/edge
turn is idle, finished, already cancelling, or panel already open
idle/finished no-op, cancelling resends idempotent CancelTurn, and second panel dispatch cancels.

requirement: Goal interrupt panel and pause/cancel/stop-subagent axis mapping
contract: When a Goal is Active, dispatch_cancel_turn SHALL always open a GoalInterruptViewState and ignore the non-Goal cancel preference. With a running turn it SHALL offer PauseGoal and StopTurnOnly, plus StopTurnAndSubagents when non-workflow subagents are running; with no turn it SHALL offer PauseGoal only. Goal choices SHALL record last_interrupt and map PauseGoal with a turn to CancelTurn{pause_goal:true,cancel_subagents:false}, StopTurnOnly to false/false, and StopTurnAndSubagents to false/true. PauseGoal without a turn SHALL execute `/goal pause` while keeping the session idle and subagents alive. A retry while cancelling SHALL replay the saved pause/subagent intent.
scenarios: Goal active
Goal is active and a turn is running
the Goal panel opens regardless of preference and the turn remains untouched.
Choice count
running non-workflow subagents are absent or present
panel offers two or three choices respectively; no-turn panel offers one.
Pause with turn
PauseGoal is selected during a turn
CancelTurn carries pause_goal true and cancel_subagents false.
Stop choices
StopTurnOnly or StopTurnAndSubagents is selected
CancelTurn carries the corresponding subagent flag with pause false.
Pause without turn
Goal is active but session has no running/compact turn
ExecuteSlashCommand `/goal pause` is emitted, not fake cancel.
Retry
a prior Goal choice left session cancelling
new CancelTurn reuses last_interrupt axes without reopening panel.

requirement: Pristine cancel rewind, committed/drafted prompt safety, and task-result panel cleanup
contract: do_cancel_turn_with_pause SHALL locally rewind only an eligible pristine in-flight prompt: no shared-queue entries, cancel rewind enabled, in-flight prompt present, no pending prompts, no committed scrollback block, and no newer text or image draft. Eligible rewind SHALL restore text/images/chips, remove every combined and primary scrollback entry, finish the turn immediately, clear timing/current prompt state, and send CancelTurn with rewind_if_pristine=true. Any activity, committed block, queued prompt, or newer draft SHALL use standard cancel, preserve the sent block/draft, and set cancelling. Standard cancel SHALL drain root permissions, cancel stale plan approval, and preserve server queue authority. Cross-dispatch prompt responses SHALL reject queued/non-current RPC errors and clear the cancel panel only for the matching turn finalization.
scenarios: Committed prompt
the in-flight scrollback entry is already committed
standard cancel keeps the block and composer empty, avoiding duplicate native output.
First activity
activity cleared the in-flight stash
standard cancel does not restore the prompt and later cancellation response adds its banner.
Combined prompt
in-flight prompt has primary and combined segment entry ids
eligible rewind removes all segment entries and restores joined text.
Newer draft
composer contains newer text or images
pristine rewind is skipped and the draft survives while CancelTurn is sent.
Queued prompt
shared queue or pending prompts are nonempty
queue remains unchanged and no local queued prompt restoration occurs.
RPC routing
queued prompt error or matching response arrives
non-running error is discarded; matching final response clears panel/finalizes through task-result path.

requirement: Prompt lifecycle watchdog and authoritative status reconciliation
contract: The watchdog SHALL query authoritative prompt status rather than fabricate terminal state. TurnSubmitting prompts SHALL be queried after PROMPT_STATUS_WATCHDOG_DELAY (2s) using exact current prompt id; TurnRunning prompts SHALL be queried after PROMPT_STATUS_RUNNING_WATCHDOG_DELAY (30s) only when turn start and reducer-owned liveness anchors are stale. Recent prompt/status activity, below-threshold turns, or an in-flight query SHALL suppress duplicate queries. Each query SHALL mark one in-flight guard; status responses SHALL clear it and rearm from observation time. Unknown/error/nonterminal responses SHALL preserve running state and prompt identity while rearming; Queued responses SHALL observe without changing a running turn, but SHALL resolve a local TurnSubmitting state to Idle and clear its prompt/in-flight/timing state. Terminal responses SHALL finalize through the same first-wins finalizer exactly once. next_prompt_watchdog_deadline SHALL return the earliest eligible deadline across agents.
scenarios: Submitting stall
TurnSubmitting exceeds 2s with no query in flight
one QueryPromptStatus for the exact prompt id is emitted and marked in flight.
Running stall
TurnRunning exceeds 30s with no new reducer activity
one status query is emitted without clearing state or prompt id.
Recent activity
last prompt/status activity is recent
no query is emitted even when turn start is old.
Duplicate guard
a query is already in flight
the next watchdog tick emits no duplicate.
Running answer
status reports Running
the in-flight marker clears, display anchor stays stable, last_status_observed_at re-arms the window, and no immediate re-query occurs.
Nonterminal answer
status is Unknown or Err
turn remains running, prompt remains current, and deadline moves forward.
Queued answer
status is Queued
idle queued observation does not claim a turn; a locally submitting prompt resolves Idle and clears current/in-flight/timing state.
Terminal answer
status is Terminal
turn finalizes once, clears current prompt, and emits one TurnCompleted marker.

requirement: Demote running execute tools and reconcile background-task kill outcomes
contract: dispatch_demote_to_background SHALL act only on the active agent with a running turn and a tracked running execute tool call, then emit DemoteToBackground with the session id and tool call id. Scheduled-task cancellation SHALL optimistically remove the local row and emit DeleteScheduledTask. Background-task and subagent kill dispatch SHALL mark matching local state pending_kill with a timestamp before emitting the corresponding kill effect. handle_bg_task_killed SHALL locate agents by session id: Killed keeps pending state for the later completion notification; AlreadyExited or missing/error outcome clears pending state and timestamp while retaining the row; NotFound removes the stale row and finishes its linked running scrollback entry; inactive agents are handled equally and the handler emits no extra effects.
scenarios: Demote guard
active agent has no running turn or no execute tool
dispatch returns no effect.
Demote valid
running execute tool exists
DemoteToBackground carries current session and tool call id.
Scheduled task
task cancellation is requested
local scheduled row is removed before DeleteScheduledTask.
Kill pending
bg task or subagent exists
pending_kill and kill_requested_at are set before KillBgTask/KillSubagent.
Kill outcome
background task result is Killed, AlreadyExited, NotFound, None, or an error
pending state is retained, cleared, row removed/scrollback finished, or cleared for retry according to outcome.
Inactive session
result addresses a non-active agent by session id
the matching agent state is reconciled without relying on active view.

requirement: The scrollback verb-group scanner SHALL classify collapsed chromeless tool and subagent members, finished collapsed thinking members, transparent opened/streaming/hidden entries, and breaking entries through one shared RunStep policy; forward scans SHALL report the same claimed end and member count used by layout and range queries, and in-place tool-kind changes SHALL be detectable.
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: run_step excludes pending-user-input and hook-annotated chrome from claims. Collapsed tool calls with a VerbGroupKind become Member; manually opened groupable tools are Transparent. Collapsed subagent rows become Member, chrome-bearing subagents Break. Finished collapsed thinking is ThoughtMember only when show_thinking is true; hidden, running, expanded, or otherwise open thinking is Transparent. Other blocks Break. scan_run_forward accepts only Member/ThoughtMember anchors, advances end over claimed members/thoughts, skips transparent entries, stops at Break or missing entry, and returns None for non-anchors. RunScan::folds is true for at least one counted member, so pure-thought runs do not fold. verb_group_kind_changed compares tool group kinds and detects membership transitions while treating non-tool kinds as None.
scenarios: Collapsed tool run
a chromeless collapsed tool has a verb group kind
run_step returns Member(kind) and scan_run_forward counts it.
Opened or chrome tool
a member is expanded, pending input, or hook annotated
the entry is Transparent or Break so its own rows/chrome remain visible.
Thinking in a run
show_thinking is enabled and a finished collapsed thought lies between members
the thought claims the run end without increasing members or the label bucket.
Streaming/visible thought
thinking is running, expanded, hidden, or show_thinking is disabled
the thought is Transparent and does not break an existing run.
Pure thoughts
a scan starts on only ThoughtMember entries
folds returns false because members is zero.
Membership refinement
a tool block changes from one verb kind to another
verb_group_kind_changed returns true so layout can mark structural dirtiness.

requirement: Folded verb-run labels SHALL rebuild from the bounded run span using the shared grouping vocabulary, including eligible hidden thinking and subagent members without labeling thoughts; the resulting VerbGroupHeaderLabel SHALL expose styled and plain text plus running/failed state for the synthetic header projection.
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: verb_group_header_label clamps end to entries.len(), walks the requested header span with the same run_step rules, skips ThoughtMember/Transparent entries, stops at Break, and accumulates Member kinds in first-appearance bucket order. GroupHeaderLabel provides a shared label payload for verb and truncation folds. BucketAccumulator renders tense-aware segments, pluralized counts, a failed suffix, bold gray-bright text spans and error styling while reporting running and failed flags. The downstream renderer owns synthetic selection geometry; this source only supplies the label payload.
scenarios: Mixed tool run
a bounded run contains reads, searches, and directory listings
the label preserves first appearance order with per-kind counts and correct past tense.
Running run
any claimed member is_running
all bucket verbs use present tense and running is true.
Hidden thinking
finished collapsed or hidden thinking occurs inside the run
the label remains tools-only while the claimed run extent stays correct.
Separator
a non-groupable entry appears inside the requested span
label accumulation stops at that entry and excludes following rows.
Failed member
a grouped tool or failed subagent is unsuccessful
the plain label receives ` · N failed`, failed is true, and only failed states use error styling.

requirement: Truncation header labeling SHALL walk the hidden participant prefix, count thoughts as participants only when they are visible to the fold policy, bucket tools and subagents through the shared label vocabulary, and return None whenever the prefix is pure thought or contains an unnameable non-thought row so the caller can retain an honest numeric count.
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: truncation_header_label clamps the range, stops after limit participants, skips hidden thinking without consuming that limit, counts visible thinking as a participant but never buckets it, and maps ToolCallBlock::label_kind or Subagent to buckets. Any other participant returns None; an empty accumulator also returns None. A limit therefore describes the hidden prefix rather than bucket count, and an unbucketable row after the limit is not inspected.
scenarios: Command prefix
a hidden prefix contains commands and thoughts
the label reports only commands while visible thoughts consume participant slots.
Limit boundary
limit stops within the range
only participants before the limit contribute; a thought can consume a slot without appearing in the text.
Hidden thinking
show_thinking is false and a thought is hidden
the thought is skipped without consuming the participant limit, allowing tools after it to be labeled.
Pure thought prefix
the prefix contains only thoughts
the function returns None and the caller keeps plain `N more`.
Unbucketable row
a visible system/session row is in the walked prefix
the function returns None to avoid under-describing hidden content; if the row lies past the limit it is not considered.
Action labels
the prefix contains Execute/Edit/UseTool/ordinary Other tools
label_kind supplies Ran commands, Edited files, Called MCP tools, or Ran tools buckets.

requirement: Verb-group buckets SHALL count ordinary tool calls, count subagent rows by distinct child session id, track any running member, and mark failure only for unsuccessful tools or Failed subagents; cancelled subagents SHALL not be treated as failures.
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: BucketAccumulator::push creates buckets in first appearance order, increments calls, inserts SubagentBlock child_session_id into a per-bucket source set, checks block_failed for every ToolCallBlock variant, increments failed_count for SubagentBlockKind::Failed only, and sets running when entry.is_running. into_label uses source-set size instead of calls when present, so started plus terminal rows of one child count once; it appends the failure suffix and exposes running/failed flags. block_failed exhaustively delegates is_success for all concrete tool variants and treats Lifecycle as non-failing.
scenarios: Subagent lifecycle pair
started and completed rows share one child session id
the bucket displays one subagent.
Completion burst
terminal rows have different child session ids
each distinct subagent contributes to the count.
Failed subagent
a subagent has Failed kind
failed count and suffix increase.
Cancelled subagent
a subagent has Cancelled kind
it contributes to count but not failed count.
Tool failure
a concrete tool reports is_success false
failed count increases and the label is marked failed.
Running member
a tool or subagent entry is running
the label uses present tense and running is true.

requirement: Group headers SHALL carry exactly one shared VerbGroupHeaderLabel payload regardless of whether they originate from a verb run or a truncation fold, preserving the styled Line and its plain text for selection/copy while keeping header-family chrome decisions outside this state module.
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: GroupHeaderLabel has VerbRun and Truncation variants and label() returns the inner VerbGroupHeaderLabel by reference. VerbGroupHeaderLabel stores Line<'static> spans, plain text, running state and failed state. into_label creates one styled span per bucket and a separate error-colored failure suffix, so renderers can choose family-specific chrome without reconstructing label content or losing copy text.
scenarios: Verb run payload
a folded ordinary run requests a label
the payload is available through GroupHeaderLabel::VerbRun and label().
Truncation payload
a truncation prefix is bucketable
the payload is available through GroupHeaderLabel::Truncation with the same text and state fields.
Selection/copy text
a consumer needs the header label as plain text
VerbGroupHeaderLabel.text exactly concatenates the visible bucket segments and optional failure suffix.
Styled render
a consumer paints the header
line contains bold gray-bright bucket spans and an accent-error failed suffix.

requirement: The inline grouping contract SHALL be represented by exhaustive tests for first-appearance ordering, skill/file separation, tense and failure changes, separator and thinking transparency, truncation participant limits, action-tool buckets, and distinct subagent identities.
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: The 17 inline tests exercise both verb_group_header_label and truncation_header_label using synthetic ScrollbackEntry/RenderBlock fixtures. They assert exact plain labels, running/failed flags, None fallbacks and count behavior, including hidden versus shown thinking and subagent started/terminal rows. This static requirement records the test evidence; it does not claim the tests were executed in this audit.
scenarios: Ordering and plurality
mixed kinds appear in a run
the exact label preserves first appearance and singular/plural nouns.
Skill distinction
a skill path is read alongside ordinary files
skill and file buckets remain separate.
Run transparency
thoughts, separators, and opened members are interleaved
only eligible tools/subagents are labeled and the run stops at separators.
Truncation honesty
thought-only or unbucketable prefixes are supplied
None is returned; bounded prefixes use participant semantics.
Subagent identity
started/completed/failed/cancelled rows are supplied
distinct child ids and failure semantics match the label contract.

requirement: Project picker recents, guarded selection, and deferred session creation
contract: The project picker SHALL open only for an eligible Agent view, refuse conflicting active session/MCP/project-create state, preserve the pending prompt and return/attachment context, refresh recents only while the picker is untouched, and on selection commit the chosen or fallback directory, persist the dont-ask choice when requested, initialize session cwd/MCP state, and create or restore the deferred session prompt without losing images or chips.
scenarios: Picker guard
the active view is not an eligible unbound Agent or MCP/project creation is already active
the picker is refused with no conflicting session effect.
Initial picker
an eligible Agent invokes project selection
a current-directory choice is shown, pending project metadata is stashed, prompt input is cleared, and recents fetch is emitted.
Recents refresh
recents return while the same picker remains untouched at its initial cursor/tab state
the picker choices and resolved paths are replaced; otherwise the response is ignored.
Directory selection
a picker choice is submitted
the selected or application cwd is committed, working directory/MCP/session state is updated, and the deferred prompt plus attachments are submitted or restored.

requirement: Startup fork deferral and parent context propagation
contract: A startup fork SHALL defer its parent session id, parent cwd, and new session id until startup permits session creation; once permitted, it SHALL reuse the newly created agent, remove the placeholder CreateSession effect, resolve cwd with an application fallback, compute parent worktree state, and emit exactly one ForkSession effect carrying the parent context.
scenarios: Startup blocked
session startup is not yet allowed
the fork request is stored as deferred startup state and no fork effect is emitted.
Startup ready
session startup is allowed and a newest agent exists
the create-session placeholder is removed and ForkSession carries parent id/cwd/worktree and the child id.
Missing agent
startup completes without a matching agent
the handler emits no child session effect and leaves the state available for caller handling.

requirement: MarkdownContent SHALL wrap a StreamingMarkdownRenderer with configurable table width, pretty/source-faithful soft-break policy, tab expansion, syntax-style finalization, and distinct complete versus streaming initialization semantics.
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: new and new_with_table_width render a complete document immediately with collapse_soft_breaks enabled; new_source_faithful disables soft-break collapse so source lines map one-to-one for line-oriented previews. All constructors expand tabs using the global tab width, set max table width, push the source, and call renderer.finish(Some(get_syntect())). streaming starts an empty renderer with generation zero and defers rendering until chunks arrive. expand_tabs returns borrowed input when no replacement is needed and replaces tabs with configured spaces otherwise.
scenarios: Complete markdown
MarkdownContent::new receives source text
the renderer is finished immediately and pretty CommonMark output is available.
Source-faithful preview
new_source_faithful receives line-oriented source
soft breaks remain line boundaries and source line mapping is preserved.
Table constraint
a max_table_width is supplied
the renderer receives the width constraint before rendering.
Streaming initialization
MarkdownContent::streaming is created
source/output starts empty, generation is zero, and later chunks can render incrementally.
Tabs
source text contains tab characters
tabs expand to configured spaces while tab-free input uses the borrowed fast path.

requirement: MarkdownContent SHALL expose source text, emptiness, style-stripped rendered text, source line mapping, pre-wrap styled lines, hyperlink targets, Mermaid ranges/content, and a monotonic generation that advances on content/raw mutations while read-only projections avoid unnecessary copies where specified.
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: push_chunk expands and renders a chunk immediately, push_chunk_deferred appends without rendering for replay batching, and finish fully renders then resets frozen tracking; each mutation increments generation. text/is_empty read renderer source; rendered_plain_text concatenates spans without styles; line_source_map and pre_wrap_lines clone renderer projections; with_hyperlinks and with_link_content borrow through closures; mermaid_block_ranges scans current view and mermaid_content builds the detection skeleton. generation reports the current mutation counter and is_raw reports current pretty/raw state.
scenarios: Immediate streaming chunk
push_chunk receives new markdown
renderer output updates and generation increments.
Deferred replay chunk
push_chunk_deferred receives historical content
source/generation update without immediate render, allowing later finish/render batching.
Finish
finish is called after streaming
held renderer state flushes, frozen tracking resets, and generation increments.
Plain rendered copy
styled markdown output is requested
rendered_plain_text returns span text joined by newlines without ratatui styles.
Link and Mermaid projection
a caller requests links or diagram metadata
the closure or helper sees current pre-wrap hyperlinks/ranges/detection content without rebuilding source text.
Empty source
source has no content
is_empty returns true while output can still supply a placeholder line.
Complete message
AgentMessageBlock::new receives complete Markdown text
the MarkdownContent is immediately constructed, image references are extracted, and Mermaid metadata is detected from the complete view.
Streaming message
AgentMessageBlock::streaming receives chunks through push_chunk or push_chunk_deferred
the source and delegated renderer state update while cached Mermaid/image metadata stays empty until finish.
Finish refresh
finish is called on a streaming block
the renderer is finalized and image references plus Mermaid detection are rebuilt from the final source.
Raw or rendered copy
copy_text is requested with raw true or false
raw source is returned for true and rendered plain text without styles is returned for false.

requirement: Word wrapping SHALL be cached by content width, generation, and theme; unchanged requests SHALL reuse the cache, width/theme/content changes SHALL invalidate the necessary portion, and streaming shall wrap newly frozen prefixes once while rewrapping only the mutable tail.
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: ensure_wrapped checks cache_width/cache_generation/cache_theme. Theme changes update renderer style, force a miss, and reset frozen counters; width changes reset frozen counters. It sets renderer table width, renders, reads frozen_lines_count, wraps newly frozen pre-wrap lines and the unfrozen tail with word_wrap_lines_with_joiners, truncates stale tail while retaining cached frozen output, appends new frozen/tail lines and updates cache/frozen metadata. with_wrapped_lines ensures this state then lends cache slices through WrappedLines; repeated same-width/same-generation calls return without rebuilding.
scenarios: Cache hit
the same width, generation, and theme are requested twice
the second access reuses cache_lines/cache_joiners and preserves cache metadata.
Width change
output is requested at a different width
the frozen cache is reset and all current renderer lines are wrapped for the new width.
Content change
a chunk changes generation
stale mutable tail is dropped while stable frozen prefix output is retained and new content is appended.
Theme change
theme_cache::current_kind differs from cache_theme
renderer style and cache are invalidated even if width/content are unchanged.
Borrowed post-processing
a caller needs wrapped lines without cloning
with_wrapped_lines exposes cached lines and joiners for the closure lifetime.
Frozen streaming prefix
previously stable lines become frozen after another chunk
frozen_wrapped_count grows monotonically and the prefix is not rewrapped.

requirement: Raw mode SHALL toggle the renderer between pretty and raw output only when the requested state changes, invalidate wrap/frozen caches and advance generation on an actual toggle, and provide explicit off-screen cache eviction that preserves source/generation while forcing a later rebuild.
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: set_raw_mode is idempotent for the current state; on change it updates current_raw, calls renderer.set_pretty(!raw) and render, resets frozen counters, and increments generation. evict_wrap_cache clears cache_lines/cache_joiners and frozen counts, sets cache_generation to u64::MAX to force a rebuild, and returns immediately when caches are already empty. is_raw reflects current_raw; QuoteBarStrip in output_tail uses the opposite of raw to strip pretty quote bars.
scenarios: Enter raw mode
set_raw_mode(true) is called while pretty output is active
renderer raw mode is rendered, generation increments, and cached wrapping is invalidated.
Repeated raw request
set_raw_mode(true) is called again
generation and renderer state remain unchanged.
Return pretty
set_raw_mode(false) is called from raw mode
pretty rendering resumes and caches are invalidated for the new generation.
Evict off-screen cache
wrap caches contain lines/joiners
the cache storage is dropped without changing source text, and the next output rebuilds it.
Evict empty cache
no wrap cache is present
eviction is a no-op without unnecessary state mutation.

requirement: Markdown output SHALL convert cached wrapped lines into BlockLine values with joiners, one shared markdown body selection range, quote-bar-aware selectability, source line/column link provenance, and per-line background styles; output_tail SHALL support bounded tail cloning and return a placeholder for empty content.
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: output delegates to output_tail with an unlimited count. output_tail ensures wrapping, returns one empty Line placeholder when no wrapped lines exist, tracks source line_index and display columns across joiners, strips non-selectable quote-bar prefixes in pretty mode, clones only the retained tail, sets MARKDOWN_BODY_RANGE on every BlockLine, preserves joiner, selectable and background, and attaches LinkSource with columns/display_start. A joiner of None advances the source line; wrapped continuation joiners preserve soft-wrap source coordinates.
scenarios: Empty content
the wrapped renderer has no lines
output returns one placeholder BlockLine.
Wrapped body
a paragraph exceeds the width
multiple lines share MARKDOWN_BODY_RANGE and continuation lines retain non-None joiners.
Selectable markdown
a normal markdown body line is emitted
the line remains Selectable::All after quote-bar processing.
Source coordinates
wrapped lines are traversed
line_index and display columns advance through joiners and line widths, with display_start recording stripped quote chrome.
Tail projection
output_tail requests a finite count
only the final count wrapped lines are cloned while source/link coordinates remain based on the complete wrapped document.
Styled table widths
markdown tables contain emoji or wide glyphs
rendered line content fills the requested display width without ghost cells.
Collapsed header
the block is rendered in Collapsed mode
one non-selectable header line is returned without a markdown body selection range.
Configured body header
the thinking header setting is enabled in Expanded mode
the header and blank separator are inserted as non-selectable rows before body lines, while body lines retain selection range zero.
Wrapped body
expanded content wraps at the supplied width
body output contains multiple lines whose selection metadata remains the shared MarkdownContent range.
Quote selection
the body begins with a markdown quote
the rendered bar prefix remains visible but derive_selection_text excludes it and returns the quote text.
Empty body
expanded or truncated rendering finds no wrapped content
render_empty_placeholder reuses the collapsed renderer and does not advertise an expand hint for the empty body.

requirement: MarkdownContent SHALL maintain equivalent visible wrapped text between incremental streaming and one-shot construction for the same source, while retaining explicit source-faithful mode for line-numbered consumers and complete joiner metadata for selection reconstruction.
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: Streaming chunks may be wrapped between pushes and later appended after additional chunks; ensure_wrapped preserves frozen prefixes and rebuilds the tail so the final line text matches MarkdownContent::new(full_text) at the same width. Hard breaks retain separate logical lines while soft breaks follow the renderer collapse policy. The test suite also pins cache reuse, width invalidation, push invalidation, raw idempotence, joiners, selection range, empty placeholder and frozen-cache growth.
scenarios: Incremental equivalence
the same markdown is fed in multiple chunks with output calls between chunks
final incremental line text and count equal one-shot full construction at the same width.
Hard breaks
source uses two trailing spaces plus newline
wrapped output preserves separate logical lines and joiner entries.
Soft breaks
source contains a bare newline in pretty mode
the configured renderer policy may collapse it to a space; source-faithful mode retains the source line boundary.
Cache invalidation evidence
width, chunks, raw state and frozen prefixes change
the inline tests observe updated cache/generation behavior without losing output.

requirement: Read block construction, content state, skill identity, and timing
contract: ReadToolCallBlock::new SHALL initialize a completed-safe block with only its path set; fluent setters SHALL update the requested line range, content/total line count, or error; is_success SHALL mean error is absent and has_content SHALL require non-empty content. Skill identity SHALL be delegated to skill_name_from_path. set_error SHALL capture elapsed time once when a running block is finalized, finish SHALL be idempotent, and elapsed_ms SHALL expose the finalized value or a live duration from started_at.
scenarios: Construction
a read block is created
all optional content, range, timing, image, and media fields are None.
Content/error mutation
content, line range, or an error is supplied
the corresponding field is updated and success/content predicates reflect the new state.
Skill identity
the path is a skill SKILL.md, an ordinary file, or another markdown file
only the canonical skill path yields a skill name/is_skill_read=true.
Timing
a running block is finalized by set_error or finish
elapsed_ms is captured once; repeated finish does not replace it and a pre-completed block remains None.

requirement: Skill-aware read header identity and selection
contract: A read targeting a canonical SKILL.md path SHALL render a semantic `Skill {skill_name}` header, select only the skill name span, and omit a filesystem link target; ordinary files SHALL remain on the regular Read path.
scenarios: Skill header
the path is `/.../skills/deploy/SKILL.md`
the first line is `Skill deploy` and the selectable text is only `deploy`.
Non-skill markdown
the path is a normal file or README.md
the block is not treated as a skill read and uses the normal file header.

requirement: Read path, range, cwd, and media header formatting
contract: The header SHALL use the Read prefix for ordinary files, shorten the displayed path through the tool-path surface and cwd, show a requested range, append `of total` when the range is a strict subset of the known file, and append mutually exclusive empty/image/PDF details. Expanded headers may display a cwd-relative path while the fullscreen preamble preserves the absolute path.
scenarios: Regular file
an ordinary path is read
the collapsed header starts with `Read` and includes the basename/path.
Range and shortening
a range and cwd are available
collapsed output shows the shortened path and range; expanded output shows the cwd-relative path while the preamble uses the fullscreen path.
Total/media details
the block has total lines, empty content, image media, or PDF pages
the corresponding `(start-end of total)`, `(empty)`, `(image)`, or `(N pages)` suffix is shown.

requirement: Read header selection and semantic file links
contract: The ordinary read header SHALL expose only the painted path span as selectable, use TOOL_HEADER_RANGE for header selection, derive copied text from the displayed path, and attach an absolute OSC8 file target that remains stable across collapsed and expanded path presentation. Skill headers SHALL select the skill name without a file target.
scenarios: Collapsed selection
a long absolute ordinary path is collapsed
only span 1..2 is selectable and copied text is the basename.
Expanded selection
the ordinary path lies under cwd
copied text is the cwd-relative path.
File link
an ordinary absolute path is rendered in collapsed or expanded mode
the link target resolves to the absolute file URL and the target is reused across modes.

requirement: Read content syntax highlighting, absolute gutters, wrapping, and truncation
contract: Expanded content SHALL be line-numbered from the requested one-based start (or 1), syntax-highlighted according to the read path, wrapped to the available width with joiners, and marked with panel backgrounds. Truncated mode SHALL retain the first five and last three wrapped lines with a single ellipsis only when content exceeds that threshold; shorter content SHALL remain complete.
scenarios: Preview styling
non-empty content is shown in expanded mode
content lines carry panel background metadata and syntax-highlighted spans.
Absolute line numbers
a line range starts at 50
the gutter begins at 50 and increments for each raw line.
Truncation
more than FIRST_LINES + LAST_LINES wrapped lines exist
the first five and final three wrapped lines are retained with an ellipsis; the first and last source lines remain visible.
Width/wrapping
content exceeds the available width
wrapping is performed before truncation and joiner metadata is preserved.

requirement: Read display modes, folding, error presentation, and block protocol
contract: ReadToolCallBlock SHALL default to collapsed and finish collapsed; a content-bearing block SHALL be foldable and cycle Collapsed→Truncated→Collapsed. Expanded/truncated output SHALL include the header plus content when content exists, or styled error lines when it does not. Errors SHALL receive an error bullet accent, while read blocks have no semantic block accent, vertical padding, custom background, or raw-mode rendering.
scenarios: Foldability
content is present or absent
is_foldable returns true only for non-empty content.
Fold cycle
the current mode is collapsed, truncated, or expanded
next_fold_mode returns truncated from collapsed and collapsed from either non-collapsed mode.
Error rendering
an error exists without content in expanded/truncated mode
the header is followed by each error line using the theme error color and the bullet reports the same accent.
Protocol defaults
the block is queried for accent, background, padding, raw mode, or default/finished mode
the declared neutral/no-padding/no-raw/collapsed protocol values are returned.

requirement: Read image references and preamble projection
contract: image_references SHALL expose exactly the stored inline image reference when present and an empty slice otherwise. The preamble SHALL always project the fullscreen path/skill header with the configured detail style and cwd context, independent of the collapsed/expanded body mode.
scenarios: Image reference
image_ref is set or absent
image_references returns a one-element slice or an empty slice without allocating a new semantic reference.
Preamble
a read block is used as a fullscreen preamble
the same header formatter is used with Fullscreen path presentation and current cwd/detail configuration.

requirement: The edit highlight worker SHALL run full-file style computation off the UI thread, coalesce queued jobs by EntryId with latest-job-wins semantics, wake the async view after each result, and preserve hunk-only output whenever the job cannot produce a verified bounded FileScoped map.
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: spawn_worker creates a named edit-hl std::thread with job/result mpsc channels. The worker receives one job, drains queued jobs by EntryId through drain_coalesced, runs the latest job per key in FIFO key order, sends EditHlResult, and calls async_view::wake; a closed result receiver ends the worker. EditHlOutcome::Ready carries an Arc line-style map plus the ThemeKind used to bake it; Failed covers cap, I/O, UTF-8, mismatch and syntax absence. EditHlRuntime owns channels, pending job/entry pairs and wrapping job ids.
scenarios: Queued duplicate
multiple jobs for one entry are pending
only the latest job for that EntryId runs, while different entries retain FIFO key order.
Ready result
a bounded readable file matches hunk content and syntax is available
the worker sends Ready with line styles and the current baked theme.
Failed result
read/cap/UTF-8/syntax/mismatch validation fails
the worker sends Failed so the caller retains hunk-only rendering.
Async wake
a worker result is sent
the shared async view is signaled for completion polling.
Worker shutdown
the result receiver is dropped
the worker exits after send failure rather than looping forever.

requirement: A full-file edit highlight job SHALL read only regular UTF-8 files within EDIT_HL_MAX_BYTES and file_text_within_hl_caps, then require compute_file_scoped_styles to verify the disk hunk text and syntax before returning FileScoped styles; every rejection SHALL return Failed without unbounded work.
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: read_file_capped checks metadata success, regular-file status, metadata length, read length and UTF-8 decoding. run_job rejects any read/cap failure, then rejects files outside the logical-line cap, captures the current theme kind beside the syntect computation, and returns Ready only when compute_file_scoped_styles(path, file_text, hunks) returns Some. Missing files, oversized/non-UTF8 files, line cap overflow, disk/hunk mismatch and missing syntax remain Failed.
scenarios: Missing file
the target path does not exist
read_file_capped returns None and run_job returns Failed.
Regular bounded file
a readable UTF-8 file is within byte and line caps
run_job invokes file-scoped style computation and can return Ready.
Directory target
metadata identifies a non-file path
the job fails closed without reading it.
Oversized input
metadata or actual bytes exceed EDIT_HL_MAX_BYTES
the worker rejects the job before full-file style work.
Line cap overflow
file_text_within_hl_caps rejects the logical line count
the worker remains HunkOnly.
Hunk mismatch
new-side hunk text differs from disk
compute_file_scoped_styles returns no map and the outcome is Failed.

requirement: Edit highlight submission SHALL resolve tool paths through the shared tool-path target resolver with optional session cwd, preserve absolute and parent-sensitive path text, expand supported home-relative paths, and retain a compatibility fallback path when resolution fails.
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: resolve_edit_target_path delegates to render::tool_paths::resolve_tool_path_target. resolve_edit_abs_path returns the resolved target when available and falls back to PathBuf::from(path) when it is not. The resolver is used by submit_edit_highlight against self.session.cwd; the public helper remains callable for compatibility callers.
scenarios: Session-relative path
a relative edit path and session cwd are supplied
the target is joined under the session cwd.
Absolute path
an absolute path is supplied
the target remains absolute and is not re-rooted under cwd.
Parent-sensitive path
an absolute path contains .. components
filesystem semantics are preserved without textual normalization in this façade.
Home-relative path
a tilde path is resolved without cwd
the result becomes an absolute home-based path.
Resolution failure
shared resolution returns None
resolve_edit_abs_path returns the original path as a PathBuf, while submit_edit_highlight declines to queue a job.

requirement: AgentView SHALL submit full-file highlighting only for an existing successful Edit with non-empty hunks and a resolvable target, mark it Pending with a fresh job id, prune older pending jobs for the same entry, and revert to HunkOnly if the worker send fails.
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: submit_edit_highlight reads the live entry by EntryId and returns for missing/non-Edit/error/empty-hunk cases. It resolves against session.cwd, lazily creates EditHlRuntime, allocates a wrapping job id, removes earlier pending pairs for that EntryId, sets EditHighlightPhase::Pending before send, and sends EditHlJob containing abs_path/display path/hunks. Successful send records the pending pair; a failed send reverts the entry and abandons the runtime so all ownerless work is normalized. edit_hl_pending reports whether pending pairs remain and apply_edit_hl_completions delegates polling.
scenarios: Eligible edit
a completed Edit has no error and at least one hunk with a resolvable target
a Pending job is created and tracked.
Ineligible edit
the entry is missing, non-Edit, failed, or has no hunks
submission is a no-op and no worker job is created.
Double submit
the same entry is submitted twice
the older pending pair is pruned and only the latest job remains for that entry.
Worker send failure
the worker channel is disconnected
the entry returns to HunkOnly and the runtime is abandoned.
Pending state
at least one job/entry pair is outstanding
edit_hl_pending is true; after all results or abandonment it is false.

requirement: The completion reducer SHALL discard stale job ids, missing/replaced entries, changed display paths, and nonmatching highlight phases; Ready SHALL install FileScoped styles, invalidate the entry cache, and request redraw, while Failed SHALL revert to HunkOnly without a redraw-only mutation.
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: poll_edit_hl_results drains all currently available results, removes each job id from pending, looks up the EntryId and Edit block, checks result.path equals edit.path, and requires EditHighlightPhase::Pending with the same job id. Ready installs FileScoped {by_new_line, theme}, invalidates the entry cache and sets redraw true. Failed installs HunkOnly without cache invalidation. A disconnected result channel invokes abandon_edit_hl_worker after draining available results.
scenarios: Stale job
a result job_id differs from the block Pending job id
the result is ignored and the newer Pending marker remains.
Replaced entry
the EntryId no longer exists or no longer contains an Edit block
the result is ignored safely.
Changed path
the live Edit path differs from the result path
the result is ignored as stale.
Matching Ready
job id/path/phase match and outcome is Ready
FileScoped styles are installed, cache invalidated, and apply returns redraw true.
Matching Failed
job id/path/phase match and outcome is Failed
the block returns to HunkOnly without claiming a redraw.
Channel disconnect
the result receiver reports Disconnected
all pending jobs are reverted and runtime is dropped.

requirement: Runtime reset and worker abandonment SHALL detach the per-AgentView receiver, revert every owned Pending Edit highlight to HunkOnly, clear pending fast-tick work, and allow lazy respawn on a later eligible submission so a replayed/reloaded transcript cannot retain ownerless async state.
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: reset_edit_hl_runtime takes the runtime, iterates its pending EntryIds, and changes only matching Pending Edit blocks to HunkOnly before dropping the receiver. abandon_edit_hl_worker logs context and delegates to reset. begin_session_reload/finish_session_reload callers therefore detach the old worker and normalize restored entries; because HunkOnly paints identically to Pending, reset does not request a redraw or cache invalidation. A later submit creates a new EditHlRuntime.
scenarios: Session reload
a pending edit highlight exists when session reload starts
the old runtime is detached and the restored edit is HunkOnly rather than ownerless Pending.
Dead worker
worker channels are gone while pending entries remain
poll detects disconnect, resets all entries, clears fast-tick pending state, and drops runtime.
Partial stale state
pending list includes an entry that is missing or no longer Pending Edit
reset skips it without panic.
Lazy respawn
a later eligible edit is submitted after reset
a fresh runtime and job channel are created.

requirement: Scrollback display modes, accents, selection bounds, and render context
contract: WrapMode SHALL provide Word, Character, and Truncate with Word as its default; DisplayMode SHALL provide Collapsed, Truncated, and Expanded with Expanded as its default. AccentStyle::static_color SHALL create a non-animated style and AccentStyle::animated SHALL set the animation flag. Selectable SHALL default to All, preserve None as non-selectable, and clamp span ranges to valid ordered indices. BlockContext SHALL derive bullet indentation from the configured bullet glyph width, saturating content width after that prefix, and mute collapsed content only when enabled and either unselected or on legacy Windows consoles.
scenarios: Mode defaults
a mode is default-constructed
wrapping defaults to Word and block display defaults to Expanded.
Accent construction
a static or animated accent is requested
the color is preserved and only the animated constructor sets animated=true.
Selectable bounds
a span range exceeds the number of spans or has a start after the end
the internal range is clamped to 0..len with start <= end; All/None produce no span range.
Context width/muting
a bullet, width, selection state, and mute setting are supplied
bullet_indent uses glyph display width plus one, content_width saturates at zero, and mute_when_collapsed follows the configured legacy-console/selected predicate.

requirement: BlockLine and BlockOutput construction with selectable metadata
contract: BlockLine SHALL default to an empty Word-wrapped, fully selectable line with no backgrounds, selection metadata, joiner, link target, or link source. Its text/styled constructors SHALL remain fully selectable, separator SHALL create a non-selectable region boundary, and builder methods SHALL set background/panel distinction, partial start column, wrap mode, selection range/text, and soft-wrap joiner. BlockOutput::plain SHALL create one fully selectable line per input text line; new/push/len/is_empty/height SHALL reflect its vector contents.
scenarios: Plain output
a multiline string is passed to BlockOutput::plain
each logical line becomes a Selectable::All BlockLine and length/height match the number of lines.
Separator
a decoration line is created
the line is Selectable::None.
Literal completeness
a BlockLine is built with every field
link_source and all current metadata fields are representable without omission.

requirement: Selection text derivation and trailing whitespace normalization
contract: line_plain_text SHALL concatenate all span text in order. derive_selection_text SHALL prefer an explicit selection_text override, return empty text for None, return the concatenated selected span range for Spans with clamped bounds, and trim only trailing whitespace for Selectable::All while preserving interior alignment spaces.
scenarios: Explicit override
selection_text is Some
the override is returned even when painted content differs.
Span selection
only a contiguous span range is selectable
the selected spans are concatenated and non-selected prefix/suffix spans are omitted.
None selection
a decoration line is non-selectable
an empty selection string is returned.
All selection
painted text has render-only trailing padding or interior spaces
trailing whitespace is stripped while interior spaces remain unchanged.

requirement: Unicode display-column slicing
contract: slice_display_cols SHALL select text by terminal display columns using grapheme boundaries, return empty for an empty or non-positive range, retain zero-width combining marks attached within the selected column window, and account for wide Unicode and tab widths without splitting a grapheme.
scenarios: ASCII slice
a normal ASCII string and half-open columns are supplied
the graphemes whose display columns intersect the range are returned.
Wide grapheme
a CJK grapheme occupies two columns
the whole grapheme is returned when its two-column extent fits the range.
Combining mark
a base character and zero-width combining mark are present
the combining mark remains attached when the base column is selected.
Tab/invalid range
a tab or start >= end/empty text is supplied
tab width follows UnicodeWidthStr and invalid/empty requests return an empty string.

requirement: Selectable display columns and selection width
contract: selectable_cols_usize SHALL convert All to the full line width, None to None, and Spans to the summed display widths of the clamped span range without narrowing to u16. selectable_cols SHALL perform the same conversion but return None when either column exceeds terminal-sized u16. block_line_selectable_width SHALL measure the derived selection text, including explicit overrides, in display columns.
scenarios: Selectable columns
All, a valid span range, or None is supplied
the result is the full range, the span display range, or None respectively.
Large line
a span extends beyond u16::MAX display columns
selectable_cols_usize preserves the usize range while selectable_cols returns None.
Selection override width
selection_text overrides the painted line
block_line_selectable_width measures the override using display width.

requirement: Decorative prefixes/suffixes and shifted selection metadata
contract: BlockOutput::with_decorations SHALL prepend a display-only prefix to the first line and append a display-only suffix to the last line. Prefix insertion SHALL shift selectable span indices and link_source.display_start while preserving logical selection text/ranges; suffix insertion SHALL exclude the suffix from All selection while preserving existing Spans/None semantics. Empty outputs and absent decorations SHALL remain unchanged.
scenarios: Decorated line
a one-line selectable output receives prefix and suffix
three spans are present and only the original body span is selectable.
Metadata preservation
the body carries selection_range and selection_text before a prefix is added
those logical values survive while the span range shifts past the prefix.
Partial/none selection
a line uses Spans or None and receives decorations
the existing selected span range or non-selectable state is retained and the suffix is not selectable.

requirement: Pre-wrap source mapping and link sidecars
