When a user prompt exists, when scrollback is in a batch with a stale turn count, or when replay is still loading, it SHALL emit exactly a non-auto SendRecap effect and set replaceable `Generating session recap…` feedback without a toast.
scenarios: Empty manual session
recap is enabled, a session exists, replay is idle, and scrollback has no user prompt
SendRecap emits no effect, no loading feedback remains, the toast is `No messages yet`, and the prompt is cleared.
Message history
recap is enabled and scrollback contains a user prompt
one SendRecap effect with auto=false is emitted, live status is `Generating session recap…`, and no toast is shown.
Batched history
a user prompt is already present during begin_batch while turn_count remains zero
the entry scan recognizes history and still emits the non-auto recap request with progress feedback.
Replay in progress
replay is loading while scrollback has no prompt yet
the dispatcher does not claim the session is empty; it emits the non-auto recap request with progress feedback.

requirement: Recap transport failures clear progress and classify history-aware feedback
contract: For a non-auto RecapRequested task result carrying an error, the task-result handler SHALL clear the replaceable `recap` live feedback and call the history-aware toast contract: no user prompt yields `No messages yet`, while a session with a user prompt yields `Couldn't generate recap`.
scenarios: Failure with no turns
a non-auto recap task fails while scrollback has no user prompt
recap live feedback is cleared and the empty-state toast is `No messages yet`.
Failure with turns
a non-auto recap task fails after a user prompt is present
recap live feedback is cleared and the generic failure toast is `Couldn't generate recap`.

requirement: Minimal BTW responses are correlated per request and agent and stale results are ignored
contract: Minimal SendBtw requests SHALL carry a UUID correlation id. After Esc dismisses the active minimal overlay, a late response SHALL not recreate state. Across multiple requests and agents, an older request response SHALL not replace the newer request, each response SHALL update only its owning agent/request lifecycle, and a dismissed request SHALL leave no minimal lifecycle; reverse completion order SHALL remain isolated.
scenarios: Dismissed minimal request
a minimal BTW request is dismissed with Esc before its response arrives
the late correlated response leaves btw_state absent.
Stale same-agent response
an older request completes after a newer request is loading
the older response is ignored and the newer request remains Loading with its question.
Current same-agent response
the current request completes
only the matching request becomes Done with its own question.
Cross-agent response
background requests for two agents complete while the other agent is active
each response resolves only the owning agent, and a dismissed second-agent response leaves its state and lifecycle absent.
Reverse completion
fresh requests for two agents complete in the opposite order
both agents independently reach Done with their corresponding questions.

requirement: Minimal BTW completion dismisses into exactly one transcript block
contract: A successful correlated minimal BTW response SHALL be dismissible into exactly one RenderBlock::Btw transcript entry retaining the original question and response text.
scenarios: Successful minimal answer
a minimal request completes successfully and the Done overlay is dismissed with Esc
scrollback contains exactly one BTW block whose question and content equal the request and answer.

requirement: Fullscreen BTW late success preserves existing empty-question completion behavior
contract: A fullscreen SendBtw request SHALL use no minimal correlation id. If the fullscreen BTW state is cleared before an otherwise successful response arrives, the response SHALL still produce a Done overlay using an empty question, preserving the existing fullscreen completion behavior.
scenarios: Late fullscreen response
a fullscreen request has minimal_request_id=None and btw_state is dismissed before a successful response
btw_state becomes Done and its question is empty.

requirement: BTW missing-session feedback is mode-specific and effect-free
contract: When SendBtw is dispatched without an active session, the dispatcher SHALL emit no effect. Minimal mode SHALL append a `No active session` system notice without a toast; fullscreen mode SHALL show a `No active session` toast and leave scrollback unchanged.
scenarios: Minimal mode without session
screen mode is Minimal and session_id is None
dispatch returns no effects, no toast is set, and the system transcript contains `No active session`.
Fullscreen mode without session
screen mode is fullscreen and session_id is None
dispatch returns no effects, the toast is exactly `No active session`, and scrollback length remains zero.

requirement: Group headers consume block-viewer dispatch
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: When the selected scrollback entry is a truncated group header, dispatching OpenBlockViewer toggles the group and returns without creating a block viewer; the selection is cleared and a subsequent selection reports the expanded header as collapse. Dispatching the same action on that collapse header returns the group to the truncated expand state.
scenarios: Expand selected group header
a selected group header represents hidden tool-call entries and OpenBlockViewer is dispatched
the block viewer remains absent, selection becomes None, and the group can be selected again with fold label collapse.
Collapse selected group header
the expanded group's collapse header is selected and OpenBlockViewer is dispatched again
the block viewer remains absent and the group is truncated again with fold label expand.

requirement: Search, directory, notice, and failed-tool viewer projection
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: Selected matched Search blocks open a block viewer with ViewerKind::Grep and no effects. Selected ListDir blocks open a PlainText viewer and no effects. Command notices with details, coordination notices with details, and Other tool calls carrying an error each report normal fullscreen eligibility and open a block viewer when dispatched.
scenarios: Grep search
a matched Search block is selected and OpenBlockViewer is dispatched
effects are empty and the block viewer kind is Grep.
List directory
a ListDir block with output is selected and OpenBlockViewer is dispatched
effects are empty and the block viewer kind is PlainText.
Detailed notice or failed tool
a command/coordination notice has details or an Other tool call has an error
the block is normal-fullscreen-viewable and dispatch leaves a block viewer present.

requirement: Markdown image references use the normal block viewer
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: AgentMessage blocks containing local PNG or JPEG Markdown image references are treated as normal fullscreen-viewable blocks. With a Kitty graphics protocol guard installed, OpenBlockViewer returns no effects, sets block_viewer, and leaves image_viewer absent.
scenarios: PNG reference
an AgentMessage contains a local PNG Markdown image reference and Kitty is available
the normal block viewer opens and the image viewer remains absent.
JPEG reference
an AgentMessage contains a local JPEG Markdown image reference and Kitty is available
the normal markdown block viewer opens with no effects.

requirement: Image-only media follows native and no-graphics branches
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: An Other tool call whose output identifies a saved local image supports fullscreen but has no normal fullscreen viewer. With Kitty, OpenBlockViewer returns no effects and leaves both in-app viewers absent after native-open handling. With GraphicsProtocol::None, the same dispatch returns no effects, leaves both viewers absent, and does not open an image viewer.
scenarios: Native image open
an image-only tool block is selected while Kitty graphics are available
the block viewer and image viewer remain absent after the native-open path.
No graphics protocol
an image-only tool block is selected while GraphicsProtocol is None
the dispatch returns no effects and the image viewer is absent.

requirement: Plugin groups seed once and preserve user expansion
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: A successful PluginsListLoaded result for an open Plugins modal stores Loaded data and seeds one collapsed group per plugin origin key on first delivery. A later delivery preserves a manually removed collapsed key, including when the modal data is first reset to Loading, and both deliveries leave effects empty through the test dispatcher.
scenarios: Initial plugin load
an open Plugins modal receives two successful plugin entries from UserGrow and ConfigPath
plugins_data becomes Loaded with two entries and the collapsed keys are origin:config and origin:user.
Post-action refetch
the user removes origin:user and a second successful delivery arrives
only origin:config remains collapsed.
Reload preservation
plugins_data is set to Loading and another successful delivery arrives
origin:user stays expanded and origin:config stays collapsed.

requirement: WebFetchToolCallBlock SHALL retain URL, optional HTTP metadata, error/output, and execution timing while exposing deterministic constructors, completion/error mutation, success, elapsed-time, and copy projections.
contract: new SHALL retain the supplied URL and initialize status_code, content_type, bytes, error, output, started_at, and elapsed_ms to None. with_error and with_output SHALL replace their respective fields with Some values. is_success SHALL be true exactly when error is None; copy_text SHALL clone output or return an empty string. set_error SHALL capture start.elapsed milliseconds when elapsed_ms is unset and started_at exists, then assign the supplied Option (including clearing an error); finish SHALL return once elapsed_ms exists and otherwise capture started_at elapsed milliseconds when present. elapsed_ms SHALL return the stored value or a live started_at elapsed value when completion has not been recorded.
scenarios: Initial block
a WebFetchToolCallBlock is constructed with a URL
the URL is retained and all response, error, and timing fields are unset.
Output/error builders
with_output or with_error is applied
the corresponding optional field contains the supplied text and success follows whether error is present.
Completion timing
a block has started_at and finish is called repeatedly
the first captured elapsed duration is retained and later finish calls do not replace it.
Error timing
set_error is called before elapsed_ms is captured
elapsed time is finalized from started_at before the supplied optional error is stored.
Copy projection
output is present or absent
copy_text returns the exact output or an empty string without rendering.

requirement: WebFetchToolCallBlock SHALL render a Fetch header with width-aware URL presentation, expose only the URL as the selectable header value, and project available status/content-type/byte metadata in stable human-readable order.
contract: header_line SHALL use the literal `Fetch ` prefix, bold the prefix using primary or muted text style, and style the URL with the command color when unmuted or muted text when muted. With max_width it SHALL pass the remaining width after the prefix through truncate_str using saturating subtraction; without max_width it SHALL retain the full URL. header_block_line SHALL select the URL span (excluding the prefix), assign TOOL_HEADER_RANGE, and expose the full URL as selection_text. metadata_line SHALL omit absent fields, return None when all three are absent, and otherwise emit an indented line in status, content_type, size order with muted labels/separators and primary values; byte counts SHALL format as B below 1024, one-decimal KB below 1 MiB, and one-decimal MB at or above 1 MiB.
scenarios: Collapsed header
the block is rendered with a content width and collapsed muting policy
the header contains Fetch plus a URL truncated to the available post-prefix width and carries muted or primary styles accordingly.
Expanded header
the header is rendered without a maximum width
the full URL is retained and the URL span is the sole selectable/copyable header target.
Metadata ordering
one or more status_code, content_type, and bytes values are present
the metadata line lists present values in status, content_type, size order with comma separators.
Byte formatting
bytes is below 1024, below 1 MiB, or at least 1 MiB
the size value uses B, one-decimal KB, or one-decimal MB respectively.
No metadata
all metadata options are None
metadata_line returns no line.

requirement: WebFetchToolCallBlock SHALL render collapsed headers separately from full modes, include metadata and a bounded panel preview for successful output, and distinguish short truncated previews from larger expanded previews while preserving the full stored content for copy.
contract: output SHALL return one selectable, width-aware header line in Collapsed mode. In Truncated and Expanded modes it SHALL wrap the unmuted full header using wrap_header_flush and mark URL spans selectable, then append an optional blank separator and metadata line. When output exists it SHALL add a blank line, top panel padding, indented primary content lines, and bottom panel padding; Truncated SHALL show at most TRUNCATED_INLINE_LINES (3) content lines and Expanded at most MAX_INLINE_LINES (10). If more lines exist, it SHALL append a dim `... (N more lines, press Enter to view)` row with N equal to total_lines minus the mode cap. When output is absent and error is absent, full modes SHALL show `  (no content)`; an error with no output SHALL suppress that success placeholder. Truncated and Expanded share the same header/metadata/panel structure, differing only in inline cap.
scenarios: Collapsed output
DisplayMode::Collapsed is requested
only the width-aware Fetch header is returned, with URL selection metadata and no content preview.
Truncated preview
successful output has more than three lines and mode is Truncated
the first three lines are shown in the panel, followed by a dim nine-more-lines style notice for a twelve-line payload.
Expanded preview
successful output has more than ten lines and mode is Expanded
the first ten lines are shown, followed by a dim remaining-lines notice.
Short output
output exists within the mode cap
all available lines are shown with indentation and panel background, without an overflow notice.
No content
output is absent and the block has no error in a full mode
the renderer shows the muted no-content placeholder.
Failed empty output
output is absent and error is present
the renderer does not emit the no-content success placeholder.

requirement: WebFetchToolCallBlock SHALL expose neutral block geometry, mode-sensitive accents and bullets, success/output-gated foldability, a collapsed default, a two-state fold cycle, and an unmuted header preamble.
contract: accent SHALL be None in Collapsed mode, static error color for errors in non-collapsed modes, animated running color for successful running blocks, and static tool color otherwise. bullet SHALL always be static error color when error exists; for successful blocks it SHALL be None when collapsed and otherwise follow accent. has_vpad_for, background, and has_raw_mode SHALL always report false/None. is_foldable SHALL require both no error and Some output. default_display_mode SHALL be Collapsed. next_fold_mode SHALL map Collapsed to Expanded and every other mode to Collapsed, ignoring running state. preamble SHALL always return the full unmuted header as Text.
scenarios: Collapsed success styling
a successful block is queried in Collapsed mode
accent and bullet are absent while geometry remains neutral.
Running styling
a successful block is running in a non-collapsed mode
accent is animated with the running color and bullet follows that accent.
Error styling
error is present
accent/bullet use the static error color in applicable modes, and the block is not foldable.
Fold eligibility
output and error combinations vary
only success with output is foldable.
Fold cycle
current mode is Collapsed, Truncated, or Expanded
Collapsed advances to Expanded and any non-collapsed mode returns to Collapsed.
Preamble
a caller asks for the preamble
a Text containing the unmuted full Fetch header is returned.

requirement: The Pager WebFetch block SHALL keep transport and content acquisition outside its presentation boundary while exposing a bounded inline preview and full stored output for surrounding copy/viewer flows.
contract: The block only stores and renders data supplied by its caller: URL, response metadata, output, error, and timing. It SHALL not validate URLs, perform HTTP, apply SSRF/domain policy, cache or persist content, convert HTML/media, or manage streaming/network lifecycle. Its source comment and fold implementation treat fetch as one-shot; the display contract therefore uses the same full-mode structure for Truncated and Expanded with only a local inline-line cap. The preview cap affects rendered lines and overflow text but does not mutate output or copy_text.
scenarios: Caller-owned fetch
a caller supplies a completed or pending response snapshot
the block renders the snapshot without initiating network or persistence work.
One-shot completion
a fetch block is folded or unfolded
running state does not alter next_fold_mode and no streaming-specific renderer is invoked.
Preview versus copy
stored output exceeds the inline cap and copy_text is requested
the UI shows a bounded preview while copy_text still returns the complete stored output.
Out-of-scope policy
URL safety, HTTP failure classification, caching, or media handling is needed
those concerns remain owned by upstream web-fetch tooling rather than this block.
sources: Web fetch tool call — fetching a URL and returning markdown content
No special running-state handling: fetch completes in one shot (no streaming).

requirement: Rewind picker selection anchors and centers the corresponding scrollback prompt
contract: When rewind_state is a Picker with a valid selected point, sync_rewind_anchor_to_picker SHALL resolve that point's shell prompt index to the matching user-prompt entry, store the entry index as anchor_entry_idx, and center scrollback on it. When prompt metadata is absent, the resolver SHALL use positional user-prompt order while skipping interjections; when the picker/state/selection or target entry is unavailable, it SHALL leave scrollback unscrolled and use anchor index zero when a picker target cannot be resolved.
scenarios: Explicit prompt metadata
the selected picker row points to a prompt index and scrollback user prompts carry matching indices
anchor_entry_idx follows the selected row (charlie, bravo, alpha) and the target entry is centered.
Legacy metadata fallback
selected rows have no prompt_index metadata
positional resolution maps each row to the corresponding user prompt and still updates the anchor.
Interjection-safe fallback
scrollback contains an interjection rendered like a prompt
the shell-index lookup skips the interjection so later prompt anchors remain aligned.
Unavailable target
rewind state is absent, phase is not Picker, selection is out of range, or no matching entry exists
the method returns without scrolling; when a picker target exists but lookup fails, anchor_entry_idx falls back to zero.

requirement: Rewind dim origin is phase-aware
contract: rewind_dim_from_entry SHALL return the rewind anchor entry for Picker, ModeSelect, Previewing, Confirm, ConversationOnlyConfirm, and Executing phases so the renderer can dim content from that entry. It SHALL return None when rewind is absent or in Loading, CancelOffer, or Error phases.
scenarios: Active rewind phase
rewind_state exists in a phase with an anchored preview or execution
the stored anchor_entry_idx is returned as the dim origin.
Non-dimming phase
rewind is Loading, offering cancellation, or displaying an Error
no dim origin is returned.
No rewind
rewind_state is absent
the method returns None.

requirement: Pending permission and question marks are rebuilt from tracker ownership
contract: sync_pending_user_input_marks SHALL clear every existing scrollback pending-user-input flag on each call, then mark the entry owned by every queued permission tool call and the active question_view tool call when the session tracker resolves them. Unknown tool-call ids SHALL remain unmarked. The method SHALL be callable by full-TUI rendering and the minimal commit path so asynchronous queue changes cannot leave stale marks.
scenarios: Recompute from permissions
permission_queue contains a request whose tool-call id maps through the session tracker
stale marks are cleared and the mapped scrollback entry is marked pending.
Recompute from question
question_view exists and its tool-call id maps through the session tracker
the mapped question entry is marked pending in addition to permission entries.
Stale or unknown state
a previous mark exists but no current queue/question maps to it, or a tool-call id is unknown
the old mark is removed and no unmapped entry is marked.
Render/commit integration
a full render frame or minimal commit pass runs
the same synchronization method refreshes pending state before rendering/committing.

requirement: Rewind keyboard input moves the cursor and maps terminal actions to app actions
contract: handle_rewind_key SHALL return Unchanged when no rewind state exists. For MoveUp/MoveDown it SHALL move the phase cursor by one within the phase bounds, resync the picker anchor, and return Changed. ConfirmCursor and all non-movement RewindInput values SHALL be mapped through rewind_input_to_outcome to the corresponding Rewind action; consumed or movement sentinel inputs SHALL return Changed, while an underlying non-rewind state remains Unchanged.
scenarios: No overlay
rewind_state is absent and a key arrives
InputOutcome::Unchanged is returned.
Cursor movement
the overlay handler returns MoveUp or MoveDown
the phase cursor changes, picker anchor synchronization runs, and InputOutcome::Changed is returned.
Confirm and navigation
the overlay handler returns ConfirmCursor, Dismissed, mode selection, confirmation, back, error dismissal, conversation-only confirmation, or picker selection
the corresponding Action variant is returned in InputOutcome::Action.
Consumed input
the overlay handler returns Consumed or another sentinel that has no app action
the event is consumed as InputOutcome::Changed.

requirement: Rewind mouse hit testing updates hover and activates the clicked row
contract: handle_rewind_mouse SHALL return Unchanged without rewind state, outside the prompt area, outside a selectable row, or for non-hover/non-left-click mouse events. A valid Moved event SHALL update the phase cursor and return Changed only when the cursor changes. A valid left click SHALL set the cursor, activate the selected row with Enter-equivalent semantics, synchronize the picker anchor for Picker phases, and map the resulting RewindInput to the corresponding InputOutcome.
scenarios: No target row
rewind state is absent or rewind_row_at rejects the prompt area/coordinates
InputOutcome::Unchanged is returned and state is untouched.
Hover move
a Moved event lands on a selectable row
the row cursor is updated and Changed is returned only for an actual cursor change.
Left click
Down(Left) lands on a selectable row
the cursor is set, the row is activated, picker anchors are synchronized when applicable, and the mapped action/Changed outcome is returned.
Other mouse button/event
the event is neither Moved nor Down(Left)
InputOutcome::Unchanged is returned.

requirement: Coordination rows use composite inquiry identity
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: A coordination row is located by the pair of source_peer_id and inquiry_id. Rows with the same inquiry_id from different peers occupy separate entries, while separate inquiries from one peer update only their matching rows. Once an existing row is terminal, a later nonterminal receipt does not replace its identity or running state.
scenarios: Peer isolation
two rows share an inquiry_id but have different source_peer_id values
both rows remain in the scrollback and the second row can remain running independently.
Independent inquiries
two nonterminal rows from one peer receive a terminal update for only one inquiry
the matching row stops while the other row remains running until its own terminal update.
Terminal protection
a terminal row receives a later nonterminal tail receipt
the existing row remains terminal, keeps its EntryId, and no running entry is created.

requirement: Coordination replay and live state preserve timing
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: upsert_coordination_row starts a non-replay, nonterminal row as running, retains a live row when an older replay receipt is applied, and returns false for an unchanged replay duplicate. Terminal live updates finish the running entry; replay terminal updates call block.finish while leaving finished_at unset in the tested row and retaining elapsed timing. Foreground finish_all_running does not finish the passive coordination row.
scenarios: Live versus replay
a live coordination row receives an identical replay receipt
the operation reports no change and the row remains running.
Foreground cleanup
a running coordination row and a separate ordinary tool are present and finish_all_running is called
the ordinary tool stops while the coordination row remains running with started_at and no elapsed_ms.
Replay completion
a live row receives a terminal replay receipt
the row is no longer running, finished_at remains None, and elapsed_ms is populated without a replay flash.

requirement: Coordination rows retain passive renderer chrome
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: A nonterminal coordination row remains in DisplayMode::Collapsed with animated accent and bullet chrome. After a terminal update the same collapsed row has nonanimated accent and bullet chrome. Coordination rows are represented as Other tool blocks and use the normal tool renderer.
scenarios: Running chrome
a nonterminal coordination row is rendered in its default entry context
the mode is Collapsed and both accent and bullet are animated.
Finished chrome
the same row receives a terminal update and is rendered again
the mode remains Collapsed and both accent and bullet are nonanimated.

requirement: Reconnect tail completion preserves original row state
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: merge_coordination_rows_from_tail scans only coordination Other tool entries that already have a matching row in the original state, upserts the tail block into the original row, transfers a committed tail marker to the original EntryId, and removes the consumed tail entry. The tested merge preserves the original EntryId, manual Expanded display mode, elapsed timing, and an unrelated tail entry.
scenarios: Tail completion
a fresh continuation contains a terminal completion for an existing live coordination row and an unrelated notice
the completion replaces the original row in place, the unrelated notice remains in the tail result, and the original row is not emitted twice.
Manual fold
the original row was manually expanded with respect_manual_folds enabled before tail merge
the merged row remains Expanded and its timing remains available.

requirement: Coordination rows stay outside primary tool grouping
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: Adding a coordination row does not replace the last ordinary tool-call EntryId. In the tested state the ordinary Other tool block remains groupable, while the coordination row is not groupable, so passive inquiry rendering does not join the main tool group.
scenarios: Primary hook isolation
an ordinary Other tool call is inserted before a terminal coordination row
last_tool_call_entry_id still returns the ordinary tool EntryId.
Group isolation
the ordinary tool and coordination row are inspected for groupability
the ordinary tool is groupable and the coordination row is not.

requirement: The ListPane module SHALL expose the reusable ListPane, ListPaneState, layout, matcher, input-mode, and wrap/query types needed by callers, and SHALL provide a theme-derived ListPaneStyle for framework-owned overlays.
contract: The module SHALL keep layout, render, and state implementation modules private while re-exporting QueryKind, ListLayoutCache, WrapMode, ListPane, InputBarMode, ListMatcher, ListPaneConfig, ListPaneState, and MatchMode. ListPaneStyle SHALL carry selection_bg, visual_select_bg, input_bar_bg, input_bar_prompt_fg, input_bar_text_fg, scrollbar_bg, scrollbar_fg, indicator_fg, follow_indicator_fg, toast_fg, uniform_visual_bg, and show_corner_indicators. Default SHALL obtain theme colors from Theme::current; uniform_visual_bg SHALL default false and show_corner_indicators SHALL default true. Match highlights use inversion and therefore do not require dedicated colors.
scenarios: Public surface
a caller imports the generic pane API
the module exposes the documented state/render/layout/matcher types while keeping submodules private.
Theme defaults
a ListPaneStyle is constructed with Default
all overlay colors are sourced from the current theme and the two behavior flags default to false/true.
Uniform visual selection
uniform_visual_bg is true
cursor rows inside a visual selection may use visual_select_bg and rely on prefix_cursor to distinguish the cursor.
Corner indicator ownership
show_corner_indicators is false
the renderer can suppress its corner indicators for a pane that draws its own affordance.

requirement: ListItem SHALL support a preferred content/prefix model with framework-derived rendering and a custom rendering escape hatch for items whose layout cannot be represented as one logical line.
contract: content SHALL default to a shared empty Line, which signals that the framework should use custom render. prefix SHALL default to None and represent a fixed-width left column; prefix_in_selection and prefix_cursor SHALL default to prefix and allow range/cursor-specific visuals. background SHALL default to None and, when Some, represent a full item-area background applied before content. render SHALL default to a no-op and is called only when content is empty; custom renderers MUST override desired_height because the default sizing is content-based. These hooks borrow item data from the model rather than owning it in the view.
scenarios: Content item
content returns a nonempty logical Line
the framework can render the item, wrap or truncate it, and apply overlays without a custom painter.
Prefix column
an item supplies a prefix
the prefix occupies a fixed-width left column and wrapped continuation lines are indented by its display width.
Selection-specific prefix
an item is in visual selection or is the cursor line
prefix_in_selection or prefix_cursor is called instead of the ordinary prefix.
Custom item
content returns the default empty Line
the framework invokes render and callers provide a matching desired_height implementation.
Item background
background returns Some(color)
the framework fills the full item row area before writing prefix/content.

requirement: The default ListItem::desired_height SHALL calculate a nonzero soft-wrap height from display-cell width, prefix width, and FirstFit word wrapping while remaining safe for zero or fully consumed widths.
contract: desired_height SHALL return 1 when width is zero, content display width is zero, or the prefix consumes the width. Otherwise it SHALL subtract the prefix display width with saturation, flatten all content span strings, call textwrap with the available text width, FirstFit, and break_words=true, and return the wrap count clamped to at least 1. NoWrap callers are expected to ignore this estimate and use one row; custom renderers are expected to override it. The calculation uses display-cell width via line_display_width rather than byte or character count.
scenarios: Zero width
desired_height receives width 0
the result is 1 and no wrapping operation is needed.
Empty content
content has no display cells
the result is 1 even if a prefix exists.
Prefix consumes area
prefix display width is at least the requested width
the available text width saturates to zero and the result remains 1.
Wrapped content
nonempty content has available text width
the flattened spans are wrapped with FirstFit and break_words=true and the number of visual lines is returned.
NoWrap caller
the pane is configured not to wrap
the pane ignores this estimate and uses one row as documented by the trait.

requirement: ListItem SHALL provide stable model identity and conservative defaults for selectability, source-line navigation, ticking, searching, highlight offsets, and copy text so ListPane state can survive model mutations without owning item data.
contract: stable_id SHALL be required and unique within the list so selection survives insertion, removal, and reorder. is_selectable SHALL default true; goto_line_number SHALL default None, allowing callers to map semantic source lines instead of visual indices; needs_tick SHALL default false. search_text SHALL default to an empty string, making the item non-searchable, and the framework may call regex.is_match and find_iter on the returned bytes. search_text_col_offset SHALL default to the prefix display width as u16, aligning byte-match highlighting with rendered content; custom renderers may override it. copy_text SHALL concatenate content span strings without style metadata and may be overridden when custom render has empty content.
scenarios: Stable selection
items are reordered or inserted/removed while an item remains present
the unique stable_id, rather than an index, is the state identity.
Separator row
an item should not receive selection
the implementation can override is_selectable to false; ordinary items remain selectable by default.
Goto line
an item has a semantic source line
goto_line_number can return Some(line) so navigation need not use the visual index.
Non-searchable item
search_text is not overridden
the empty string causes filter/highlight matching to find no item text.
Prefixed search
searchable content follows a prefix
the default column offset equals the prefix display width so match highlights begin at content.
Copy content
copy is requested for a content-based item
copy_text returns concatenated plain span text without styles.

requirement: line_display_width SHALL compute the terminal display width of a ratatui Line by summing Unicode display widths for every span and ignoring style metadata.
contract: line_display_width SHALL iterate all spans, pass each span content to unicode_width::UnicodeWidthStr::width, and sum the resulting cell widths. It SHALL count the visual width of Unicode graphemes according to the dependency rather than bytes or Rust scalar count, and style changes between spans SHALL not affect the numeric width.
scenarios: Multiple spans
a Line contains several styled or unstyled spans
their individual Unicode display widths are summed in source order.
Wide Unicode
a span contains wide Unicode text
the result follows Unicode terminal-cell width rather than byte length.
Style-only difference
two lines have identical span text with different styles
both return the same display width.
Empty line
the line has no spans or only zero-width text
the result is zero.

requirement: The list_pane module SHALL remain a reusable view contract: item models own data, ListPaneState owns scroll/selection/layout state in the sibling state module, and rendering/input behavior remains delegated to sibling modules.
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: The module documentation defines ListPaneState plus ListPane as a generic scrollable, selectable list whose state is non-generic and owns only scroll/selection/layout data while item data remains external and borrowed. This file declares the trait/style and width primitive but does not perform scrolling, filtering mutation, input editing, scrollbar rendering, buffer painting, or model persistence; those behaviors belong to the private layout/render/state modules and their callers. No inline tests exist in this 314-line source, so only the documented contract and signatures are proven here.
scenarios: Borrowed model
a pane is created over an external item slice
the view borrows items and does not duplicate model ownership.
State ownership
scroll, selection, or layout changes are needed
callers use ListPaneState from the sibling state module rather than fields in ListItem.
Rendering ownership
items use content-based or custom rendering
the sibling renderer consumes these trait hooks and applies overlays after item rendering.
Audit boundary
this source is inspected without inline tests
test_count is zero and sibling-module behavior is not claimed from this file.

requirement: Search-tool discovery identity, constructors, and completion timing
contract: DiscoveredTool SHALL preserve name, server, description, and score. discovered_tool_action SHALL strip a trusted `{server}__` prefix from a tool name while preserving flat names and names whose prefix does not match the server. SearchToolCallBlock::new SHALL initialize a query with no limit, zero result count, empty results/content/error, and no timing. with_error SHALL set an error; is_success SHALL be true exactly when error is absent. set_error and finish SHALL capture elapsed milliseconds once a started_at exists, and elapsed_ms SHALL return stored elapsed time or the current duration while running.
scenarios: Local MCP name
tool.name starts with tool.server followed by `__`
discovered_tool_action returns only the action suffix.
Gateway/flat name
the name does not have the exact server-prefixed form
discovered_tool_action returns the original full name.
Fresh block
SearchToolCallBlock::new(query) is constructed
query is retained and optional/result/error/content/timing fields use their documented empty defaults.
Error state
with_error or set_error receives an error
error is present and is_success returns false; set_error records elapsed time when a started block had not been completed.
Completion timing
finish or elapsed_ms is called after started_at
elapsed_ms is captured once, finish does not overwrite an existing value, and an unfinished block reports the current elapsed duration.

requirement: Search-tool copy text exposes query, limit, result count, and titled tool details
contract: copy_text SHALL emit a stable text representation with `query:`, an optional `limit:` line, singular `1 result` or plural `{N} results`, then numbered discovered tools. Each tool line SHALL titleize the action and server independently, and SHALL include a description line only when the description is non-empty.
scenarios: Query and limit
a block has a query and optional limit
copy text starts with query and includes the limit line only when present.
Result count grammar
result_count is one or any other value
the count is rendered with `result` for one and `results` otherwise.
Tool details
results contain action/server names and descriptions
each result is numbered, action/server labels are MCP-titleized, and non-empty descriptions follow on an indented line.
Empty description
a discovered tool has an empty description
no blank description line is added for that tool.

requirement: Search-tool headers truncate queries and expose only the query for selection
contract: header_line SHALL render a bold `Search Tools ` label, a command-colored query, and an optional dim result suffix when a bounded width can fit it. For a bounded width it SHALL omit the suffix when the label plus suffix does not fit, allocate the remaining query budget with saturating subtraction, and truncate the query to that budget. header_block_line and expanded wrapped header lines SHALL make only the query span selectable, attach TOOL_HEADER_RANGE and the query selection text on the first line, and omit selection text from continuation lines.
scenarios: Unbounded header
header_line is rendered without max_width
the label and full query are rendered without a result suffix.
Bounded fitting header
max_width is large enough for label, query budget, and suffix
the query is truncated to the available budget and the dim `(N result[s])` suffix is included.
Bounded narrow header
the label plus suffix cannot fit
the suffix is omitted and the query uses the remaining width budget.
Collapsed selection
the collapsed header is converted by header_block_line
the label/suffix are excluded and only the query span carries selection range/text.
Wrapped expanded header
the header wraps across lines
each line remains selectable after the label span, while only the first line exposes the query selection text and later lines use a joiner.

requirement: Search-tool block output renders collapsed, expanded, empty, and error states
contract: BlockContent::output SHALL render a collapsed selectable header using configured collapsed muting and bounded width. Truncated and Expanded modes SHALL render a wrapped header; when results exist they SHALL render numbered action/server rows with titleized action and dim server, when results are empty and no error they SHALL render `(no results found)`, and when error is present they SHALL append the error in the error accent. Expanded output SHALL keep result descriptions out of the compact result rows while copy_text remains the detailed representation.
scenarios: Collapsed display
ctx.mode is Collapsed
only the bounded header line is returned, with muted styling according to collapse configuration and query-only selection.
Results display
ctx.mode is Truncated or Expanded and results are non-empty
wrapped header, separator, and one numbered row per result are emitted; rows show action and optional server labels.
No results
expanded/truncated output has no results and no error
a separator and muted `(no results found)` line are emitted.
Error display
the block has an error
an error line is appended in the theme error color, including when the block has no results.
Mode consistency
ctx.mode is Truncated or Expanded
both modes use the same expanded result/error structure rather than a collapsed-only header.

requirement: Search-tool visual status, folding, padding, and viewer metadata
contract: SearchToolCallBlock SHALL have no vertical padding, no raw mode, and no background. Its collapsed display has no accent/bullet except an error bullet; running expanded blocks use animated running accent, completed successful expanded blocks use static tool accent, and errors use static error accent. It SHALL be foldable only when successful with at least one result, default to Collapsed, toggle Collapsed to Expanded and every other mode back to Collapsed, and expose the header as its preamble.
scenarios: Successful running block
error is absent, ctx is expanded, and the entry is running
accent and bullet use the animated running color.
Successful completed block
error is absent and the entry is not running in an expanded mode
accent and bullet use the static tool color.
Error block
error is present in any mode
accent and bullet use static error color; foldability is false.
Collapsed success
ctx.mode is Collapsed and no error exists
accent and bullet are absent and foldability depends on results.
Fold/display metadata
the block is queried for fold mode, default mode, preamble, padding, background, or raw mode
default mode is Collapsed, only Collapsed toggles to Expanded, preamble is the header, padding/background/raw mode remain disabled, and successful non-empty blocks are foldable.
Integration classification
the block is wrapped as ToolCallBlock::IntegrationSearch
tool grouping labels it as Searching and MCP tool/MCP tools according to count.

requirement: Hook run data and content predicates
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: HookRunStatus represents Success with elapsed time, Skipped, Blocked with detail and elapsed time, and Failed with error and elapsed time. HookRunEntry carries a name, status, and optional output. ToolCallHookData stores pre_hooks, post_hooks, and named lifecycle groups; is_empty is true only when all three collections are empty, while has_content is true when any run in any collection is not Skipped.
scenarios: Empty hook data
pre_hooks, post_hooks, and lifecycle are all empty
is_empty returns true and has_content returns false.
Skipped-only data
collections contain only HookRunStatus::Skipped entries
is_empty is false when entries exist but has_content remains false.
Content-bearing data
any pre, post, or lifecycle run has Success, Blocked, or Failed status
has_content returns true.

requirement: Hook count summaries classify outcomes and omit skipped runs
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: The inline hook summary aggregates pre, post, and lifecycle runs. Success and Blocked count as successes, Failed counts as failures, and Skipped contributes to neither. No runs produce None; otherwise the summary starts with two spaces and `[hooks: `, colors success and failure numbers using the current theme, inserts `/` only when both counts are present, and closes with `]`. Stop-hook summaries apply the same counts per named event, skip groups with no non-skipped runs, and join remaining event groups with two muted spaces.
scenarios: Success-only summary
one or more Success or Blocked runs exist and no Failed runs exist
the summary contains only the success count without a slash or failure count.
Failure summary
Failed runs exist and no Success or Blocked runs exist
the summary contains only the failure count.
Mixed stop groups
named stop groups contain a mixture of active and skipped runs
skipped-only groups are omitted and remaining event summaries are separated by two spaces.

requirement: Expanded hook details render status, timing, errors, output, and truncation
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: Expanded hook rendering suppresses a section when every run is Skipped; otherwise it emits an indented bold muted event header followed by one detail line per run. Success uses a check mark and elapsed milliseconds, Skipped uses `- name skipped`, Blocked uses a running arrow and up to three detail lines, and Failed uses a ballot-X, strips a leading `hook 'name' ` prefix from the error, and emits up to three error lines. Optional output is appended for every run as up to three lines after truncation to 120 characters, with muted styling.
scenarios: All skipped section
render_hooks_expanded receives a run list where every status is Skipped
it returns no lines.
Blocked detail
a run has Blocked status with detail and elapsed time
the output contains a running marker, the hook name and duration, followed by at most three truncated detail lines.
Failed error cleanup
a run has Failed status and its error begins with the hook name prefix
the prefix is removed before at most three truncated error lines are rendered.
Captured output
a run has optional stdout/stderr output
up to three truncated output lines are appended after the status-specific lines.

requirement: Display modes gate hook sections and separators
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: render_hooks_for_mode and render_hooks_detail return no lines for empty runs or Collapsed mode. Expanded and Truncated modes render hook content; the former includes the event section header while the detail helper emits only per-run lines. render_hook_separator returns one muted separator line containing four spaces followed by three horizontal box-drawing characters. The detail helper is intended for lifecycle blocks whose event name is already the block header.
scenarios: Collapsed mode
hook runs are supplied with DisplayMode::Collapsed
both section and detail render helpers return an empty vector.
Expanded or truncated mode
nonempty hook runs are supplied with DisplayMode::Expanded or DisplayMode::Truncated
render_hooks_for_mode emits the event header and details, while render_hooks_detail emits details without the header.
Separator
a caller requests the shared hook separator
one muted separator BlockLine is returned.

requirement: Hook phases and lifecycle grouping retain source ownership
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: HookPhase distinguishes Pre and Post phases. ToolCallHookData keeps pre_tool_use and post_tool_use runs in separate vectors and keeps lifecycle runs as event-name/vector pairs, allowing the rendering helpers to aggregate all runs for inline summaries while preserving phase and event grouping for expanded output.
scenarios: Pre/post ownership
a caller supplies runs from the two tool execution phases
the data model retains them in separate pre_hooks and post_hooks collections.
Lifecycle ownership
a lifecycle event supplies one or more hook runs
the event name and its run vector remain paired in lifecycle data and are available to summary/detail renderers.

requirement: AtContext SHALL represent the complete @-token byte range, cursor byte position, and query text while exposing mode predicates and a path-only replacement range that preserves the @ and hidden marker.
contract: AtContext::range SHALL include the leading @ and extend through the detected token terminator, cursor SHALL be the supplied byte position, and query SHALL be the text after @ through cursor (including a leading ! when present). is_dir_mode SHALL test query.ends_with("/"); is_hidden_mode SHALL test query.starts_with("!"); matcher_query SHALL strip exactly one leading ! for fuzzy matching. path_range SHALL start after @ plus one extra byte in hidden mode and end at range.end, so callers replace only path bytes while retaining @/!.
scenarios: Plain context
the cursor is inside @foo
range covers the token, query is foo, and directory/hidden modes are false.
Directory mode
query ends with /
is_dir_mode is true and matcher_query retains the slash.
Hidden mode
query starts with !
is_hidden_mode is true and matcher_query removes only the leading !.
Hidden directory
query starts with ! and ends with /
both mode predicates are true and the fuzzy query excludes only !.
Path replacement
a plain or hidden context is accepted
path_range excludes @ and, when present, !, while ending at the whole token end.

requirement: detect SHALL identify the rightmost valid @-token at or before the cursor, reject invalid cursor positions and email-like anchors, stop at whitespace/comma/semicolon, and return no context when the cursor lies after the token.
contract: detect SHALL delegate to detect_with_drill with no drill prefix. detect_with_drill SHALL return None when cursor exceeds text length or is not a char boundary, find the rightmost @ in text[..cursor], reject @ when immediately preceded by an alphanumeric character or underscore, and locate token_end at the first whitespace, comma, or semicolon after @ (or text.len()). The cursor SHALL be accepted at or before token_end and rejected only when cursor > token_end. A successful result SHALL use byte-safe slicing to return AtContext with range at_idx..token_end and query text[at_idx+1..cursor].
scenarios: Cursor validity
cursor is outside text or splits a UTF-8 code point
detection returns None without constructing an invalid slice.
Anchor validation
@ is preceded by an alphanumeric or underscore
detection returns None, preventing email/user_identifier activation.
Special-character anchor
@ follows whitespace, punctuation, or an opening delimiter
the token is accepted.
Delimiter
a whitespace, comma, or semicolon follows the token
range ends immediately before that delimiter.
Cursor after token
cursor is after the delimiter
detection returns None.
Rightmost anchor
multiple @ characters precede the cursor
the rightmost @ is used as the active token.
Empty token
text is exactly @ and cursor is after it
a context with an empty query is returned.

requirement: detect_with_drill SHALL optionally treat whitespace inside the currently drilled directory prefix as token content while reverting to ordinary delimiters when the text no longer starts with that exact prefix.
contract: When drill_prefix is Some(prefix) and the text after @ (and optional !) starts with prefix, detection SHALL establish an internal_until byte boundary after that prefix. Whitespace, comma, or semicolon before that boundary SHALL not terminate the token; delimiters at or after it SHALL terminate normally. A prefix mismatch, an empty prefix, or text edited so it no longer starts with the prefix SHALL leave whitespace as a terminator. The rule SHALL work for hidden mode, tabs, multi-byte prefix names, second-level path segments, cursor-in-token queries, and a trailing slash directory mode.
scenarios: Space in drilled name
drill_prefix exactly matches a path containing a space
the entire drilled name remains one token and its query includes the space.
Tab in drilled name
drill_prefix exactly matches a path containing a tab
the tab is retained as token content.
Hidden drilled name
the token begins @! and the prefix matches after !
hidden mode remains active and matcher_query removes !.
Second-level space
the prefix contains multiple path segments with spaces
all matching internal spaces remain within one token.
Drilled directory
the matching prefix is followed by /
is_dir_mode is true.
Mismatch
the text after @ does not start with drill_prefix
ordinary whitespace termination applies and a cursor after that space yields None.
Post-prefix whitespace
whitespace occurs after the matched prefix
the whitespace terminates the token.
Backspace invalidation
editing removes part of the drill prefix
the drill rule becomes inert and the normal delimiter rejects the context.
Mid-token cursor
cursor is inside a matching drilled token
range still covers the full token while query ends at the cursor.
Unicode prefix
drill_prefix contains multi-byte characters
byte offsets remain valid and the full prefix is retained.

requirement: normalize_display_path SHALL remove one leading `./` from a display path while preserving other path text and returning a borrowed slice.
contract: normalize_display_path SHALL return path.strip_prefix("./").unwrap_or(path): `./foo/bar` becomes `foo/bar`, `./` becomes the empty string, and paths without that exact leading segment remain unchanged. It SHALL not canonicalize, resolve, trim, collapse repeated prefixes, or touch filesystem state.
scenarios: Relative prefix
path starts with ./ followed by content
the returned display path omits exactly that prefix.
Bare prefix
path is ./
the returned display path is empty.
Other path
path does not start with ./
the original path is returned unchanged.

requirement: The file-search context module SHALL parse prompt bytes and expose completion modes/ranges without performing filesystem search, fuzzy ranking, path validation, insertion, or viewer side effects.
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: This module owns lexical @-token detection, hidden/dir mode interpretation, matcher-query extraction, replacement boundaries, and display-prefix normalization. It consumes only prompt text, cursor bytes, and an optional already-selected drill prefix. It does not inspect the filesystem, apply ignore rules, perform fuzzy matching, mutate prompt text, open viewers, or close undo groups; those responsibilities remain in FileSearchState, prompt integration, and search/viewer callers. The 31 inline tests cover lexical and range behavior only.
scenarios: Lexical-only input
prompt text, cursor, and optional drill prefix are supplied
the result is a pure AtContext or None with no external I/O.
Matcher handoff
a caller needs fuzzy input
matcher_query supplies the lexical query after removing only the hidden marker.
Insertion handoff
a caller accepts a file result
path_range supplies the path replacement span while preserving @/! markers.
No filesystem claim
a path token is detected
this module does not assert that a matching file exists or is allowed.
Test boundary
the source is audited statically
31 inline tests establish lexical cases; integration with FileSearchState and filesystem results remains unproven here.

requirement: Session entry title precedence, cleaning, truncation, and fallbacks
contract: entry_title SHALL choose the first non-empty source in this order: display_name, generated_session_title, first UserPrompt text, then a short session id or `loading...` when no session id exists. Every selected human/model/prompt title SHALL be trimmed, skill command XML SHALL be converted to its display text when applicable, terminal control characters SHALL be sanitized, and the final title SHALL pass through the shared character-based truncation. A session id fallback SHALL use its first eight Unicode characters prefixed by `session `.
scenarios: Manual title precedence
display_name is non-empty
it wins over generated title and prompt content and is returned after trim/sanitize/truncate.
Generated title precedence
display_name is absent/blank and generated_session_title is non-empty
the generated title is cleaned for skill command markup and used before scrollback.
Prompt fallback
no usable name exists and a UserPrompt block is present
the first prompt text is trimmed, skill markup is projected to display text, sanitized, and used as the title.
Session id fallback
no usable title or prompt exists and session_id is present
the first eight session-id characters are returned as `session <short-id>`.
Loading fallback
no usable title/prompt exists and session_id is absent
the exact title is `loading...`.
Blank values
display/generated/prompt text is empty after trim
that source is skipped and precedence continues to the next fallback.

requirement: Latest prompt and agent reply summaries obey turn pairing and safe first-line projection
contract: last_user_prompt_line SHALL scan newest-first for the latest non-empty UserPrompt first line, strip ANSI escapes, sanitize ASCII controls, and trim the result. last_agent_message_line SHALL scan newest-first for the newest AgentMessage, return its first non-empty rendered line after the same cleaning, return None when that message has no renderable line, and return None immediately when a newer UserPrompt marks an unanswered turn so an older reply is not paired with it. first_user_prompt_text SHALL scan oldest-first and return the first UserPrompt full text, skipping non-prompt entries and defensive missing entries.
scenarios: Latest user prompt
scrollback contains one or more UserPrompt blocks
the newest prompt with a non-empty first line is projected as a sanitized single-line string.
Unanswered turn
a UserPrompt is newer than every AgentMessage
last_agent_message_line returns None rather than pairing the prompt with an older reply.
Latest agent reply
the newest relevant block is an AgentMessage with a non-empty rendered line and no newer UserPrompt
only its first non-empty line is returned after ANSI/control sanitization.
Empty reply
the newest AgentMessage has no non-empty renderable line
last_agent_message_line returns None and does not fall back to an older message.
First prompt fallback
first_user_prompt_text scans a scrollback containing structural blocks and prompts
the oldest UserPrompt text is returned; a missing indexed entry is skipped defensively.

requirement: Display text sanitization removes terminal control injection without needless allocation
contract: sanitize_display_text SHALL replace every ASCII control character, including ESC, BEL, DEL, tab, newline, and carriage return, with U+FFFD while preserving all other Unicode/codepoint content. For already-clean input, including clean Unicode and empty strings, it SHALL return Cow::Borrowed; for input containing controls it SHALL return Cow::Owned with no remaining ASCII controls.
scenarios: Clean ASCII
input contains no ASCII controls
the text is unchanged and returned as Cow::Borrowed.
Clean Unicode
input contains wide or accented Unicode codepoints without controls
the text and codepoints are unchanged and returned borrowed.
Terminal escape payload
input contains OSC/CSI escape bytes or BEL
all control bytes become U+FFFD and no ASCII control remains.
DEL and line controls
input contains DEL, tab, newline, or carriage return
each control is replaced with U+FFFD while surrounding characters remain in order.
Empty text
input is empty
an empty borrowed Cow is returned.

requirement: Derived titles truncate by Unicode codepoint without splitting UTF-8
contract: truncate_title SHALL return short text unchanged. When text exceeds MAX_TITLE_CHARS (60 Unicode codepoints), it SHALL keep the first 60 codepoints and append exactly `...`, producing 63 codepoints total. The truncation SHALL be codepoint-based so multibyte UTF-8 characters are not split; grapheme-cluster boundaries are outside this contract.
scenarios: Short title
text length is at most 60 codepoints
the exact original string is returned without an ellipsis.
Long ASCII title
text exceeds 60 codepoints
the first 60 codepoints plus `...` are returned and total length is 63 codepoints.
Long multibyte title
text exceeds 60 codepoints using multibyte characters
truncation succeeds without invalid UTF-8 or partial codepoint bytes.

requirement: Relative time formatting uses compact floor-second buckets
contract: format_relative_time SHALL format elapsed durations using floor seconds: less than 1 second as `now`, 1–59 seconds as `{n}s ago`, 1–59 minutes as `{n}m ago`, 1–23 hours as `{n}h ago`, and 1 or more days as `{n}d ago`.
scenarios: Sub-second age
elapsed duration is below one second
the exact label is `now`.
Seconds bucket
elapsed duration is 1 through 59 seconds
the integer seconds and `s ago` suffix are returned.
Minutes bucket
elapsed duration is 60 seconds through 59 minutes
whole minutes and `m ago` are returned.
Hours bucket
elapsed duration is 60 minutes through 23 hours
whole hours and `h ago` are returned.
Days bucket
elapsed duration is at least 24 hours
whole days and `d ago` are returned.

requirement: Permission responses surface disconnected requesters
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: respond_permission sends the selected ACP response through the request's oneshot response_tx. When the receiver is closed, it leaves the response unsent and calls AgentView::show_toast with the exact requester-disconnected message `This permission request is no longer valid (the requester disconnected)`.
scenarios: Live requester
the permission response receiver accepts the response
the ACP response is sent and no disconnected-requester toast is added by this helper.
Disconnected requester
the receiver is closed before respond_permission sends
the send error is converted into the standardized AgentView toast.

requirement: Permission selection builds scoped metadata and session approval transitions
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: dispatch_permission_select requires an active Agent view and a front permission request. It removes the front request, records only allow-flavored per-request option kinds in the sticky permission cursor, and sends Selected with optional metadata. MCP `allow-always-mcp` metadata selects the configured tool or server (falling back to tool when server prefix is absent); otherwise a positive bash selection count serializes the first highlighted words as command_parts. Selecting the global enable-always option first answers the current request, then for a root session that is not already AlwaysApprove calls set_permission_mode(AlwaysApprove), while the default permission is not changed in this function.
scenarios: Ordinary selection
the active root or selected permission owner has a front request and a normal AllowOnce, AllowAlways, or reject option
the request is popped, a Selected response is sent with no unrelated metadata, and allow-flavored kinds alone may update the sticky cursor.
MCP scope selection
option id is allow-always-mcp and the request has MCP scope
response metadata encodes a tool selection or a server selection when a server prefix exists, with no-prefix server scope falling back to the tool selection.
Bash scope selection
the request has bash_highlights and bash_selection_count is positive while MCP scope branch does not apply
response metadata encodes the first selected highlight words as BashCommandSelectedTerms command_parts.
Enable always approve
the selected option id is ENABLE_ALWAYS_APPROVE_OPTION_ID and the active view resolves to a root session that is not already AlwaysApprove
the current request is answered Selected and set_permission_mode is called for session AlwaysApprove.

requirement: Permission follow-up and cancellation resolve the front request
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: dispatch_permission_followup and dispatch_permission_cancel operate on the active permission owner's front request and return an empty effect list. Followup searches for a RejectOnce option: when absent it sends Cancelled; when present it sends Selected for that option and attaches followup_message metadata only when the original text is not blank after trim. Cancel always sends Cancelled. Each path invokes resolve_permission_queue_transition after responding.
scenarios: Follow-up rejection
the front request exposes RejectOnce and follow-up text is nonblank
the request is answered Selected with the RejectOnce id and the original follow-up text is carried in followup_message metadata.
Missing RejectOnce
the front request has no RejectOnce option
the request is answered Cancelled and no follow-up metadata is sent.
Cancel
a front permission request exists and cancellation is dispatched
the request is answered Cancelled and queue transition handling runs.

requirement: Root permission draining preserves child-owned requests
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: drain_root_permission_queue returns without mutation when the Agent has no session_id. With a bound root session, it removes every queued permission whose request session_id equals the root session and answers each with Cancelled, while retaining requests from other session ids in their queue order. It compares the original front request identity using session_id and tool_call_id, and invokes queue transition handling only when a removed root request changed the visible front.
scenarios: Unbound root
the Agent session_id is None
the permission queue and response channels are untouched.
Root-owned drain
the queue contains one or more requests with the Agent root session_id
matching requests are removed and each receives a Cancelled response.
Child preservation
the queue also contains requests with a different session_id
child requests remain queued and are not answered by this root drain.
Front identity
root requests are removed behind a different front request
the visible front request is preserved and its transition state is not reset by the drain.

requirement: Permission queue transitions clear transient input and restore stashes
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: resolve_permission_queue_transition clears last_permission_click on every call. If the queue is empty, it calls restore_permission_stashes; otherwise it clears prompt text and sets the next front PermissionFocus to Options. restore_permission_stashes takes and restores permission_stashed_prompt and takes permission_stashed_pane to force_active_pane, leaving each stash consumed after restoration.
scenarios: Queue emptied
a permission response leaves the queue empty
the double-click tracker is cleared and any stashed prompt and pane are restored.
Next request remains
a permission response leaves another request at the front
the double-click tracker is cleared, prompt text is emptied, and the next request focus becomes Options.
Stash restoration
permission_stashed_prompt or permission_stashed_pane is present
the corresponding value is taken and applied to the composer or active pane.

requirement: PlanApprovalViewState SHALL retain the source interaction identity, plan preview, stashed prompt, one-shot response sender, focus, comment records, editing/range state, and stashed feedback prompt, with deterministic constructor defaults.
contract: PlanApprovalFocus SHALL distinguish Preview, Prompt, and Commenting. PlanComment SHALL carry an id, a 1-based half-open line_range, and comment text. PlanApprovalViewState::new SHALL clone request.session_id into source_session_id, retain tool_call_id and plan_content, store stashed_prompt, wrap response_tx in Some, set focus to Preview, initialize comments empty and next_comment_id to 0, and clear editing_comment_id, commenting_range, and stashed_feedback_prompt. State fields remain public for AgentView orchestration.
scenarios: Focus model
the approval surface changes ownership between preview, prompt, and comment editor
focus is represented by exactly one PlanApprovalFocus variant.
Constructor identity
a PlanApprovalExtRequest, stashed prompt, and response sender are supplied
session/tool/plan/prompt data are retained and the sender is available once.
Comment defaults
a new approval view is created
comments are empty, next id is zero, no comment is being edited, and no commenting range or feedback stash exists.

requirement: PlanApprovalViewState::format_feedback and format_plan_comments SHALL produce stable human-readable feedback that labels 1-based selected plan lines, quotes available source snippets, preserves comment text, and appends nonblank freeform feedback in comment-aware form.
contract: Each comment SHALL render in insertion order as `Proposed plan line N:` for a one-line range or `Proposed plan lines N-M:` where M is range.end-1, followed by inline_plan_snippets, a blank line, `Comment:`, and the exact comment text. Blocks SHALL join with two newlines. format_feedback SHALL ignore freeform text when None or trim-empty; with no comments it SHALL append the original freeform text unchanged, and with comments it SHALL prefix it with `Additional feedback:` while preserving its original non-trimmed body. format_plan_comments SHALL apply the same comment rendering to a supplied slice and optional plan content.
scenarios: Single-line comment
a comment range covers one line
feedback uses singular Proposed plan line N and quotes that line.
Multi-line comment
a comment range covers multiple lines
feedback uses inclusive display end range.end-1 and quotes each selected line.
Additional feedback
freeform text is nonblank and comments already exist
an Additional feedback section is appended after the comment blocks.
Standalone feedback
freeform text is nonblank and there are no comments
the original freeform text is appended without the Additional feedback label.
Blank feedback
freeform is None or trim-empty
no freeform section is emitted.
Stable ordering
multiple comments exist
blocks preserve comment vector order and are separated by exactly two newlines.

requirement: inline_plan_snippets SHALL convert a valid 1-based half-open line range into quoted plan lines and return explicit unavailable markers for absent content or invalid ranges.
contract: When plan_content is None, inline_plan_snippets SHALL return `> [plan content unavailable]`. With content, it SHALL use lines(), reject ranges where start==0, start>=end, or start>line_count, clamp the inclusive end to min(range.end-1,line_count), reject end<start, and otherwise prefix each selected 1-based line with `> ` and join lines with `\n`. Out-of-range ends are truncated to available content rather than causing a slice panic.
scenarios: Missing content
plan_content is None
the explicit plan content unavailable marker is returned.
Invalid range
start is zero, start is not before end, or start exceeds line count
the selected lines unavailable marker is returned.
Valid single line
range is N..N+1 for an existing line
one quoted line is returned.
Valid multi-line
range spans several existing 1-based lines
all selected lines are quoted in source order.
Clamped end
range.end extends beyond available lines
the output stops at the final available line.

requirement: Plan approval response helpers SHALL map approval actions to typed outcomes, omit trim-empty feedback, serialize an ExtResponse payload, and consume the response sender so repeated actions cannot send twice.
contract: send_plan_approval_response SHALL filter feedback to None when f.trim().is_empty(), construct PlanApprovalExtResponse with the given outcome and normalized feedback, serialize it to a raw JSON value, wrap it in acp::ExtResponse, and attempt to send Ok(response), ignoring a closed receiver. send_ext_response SHALL take the Option sender and return false without sending when it is None; otherwise it SHALL consume the sender, dispatch the response, and return true. send_approved maps to Approved, send_abandoned to Abandoned with no feedback, send_cancelled to Cancelled, and send_stale_cancel to Cancelled with no feedback.
scenarios: Approved response
send_approved is called without feedback
the receiver gets JSON outcome approved with feedback omitted.
Approved feedback
send_approved receives nonblank text
the receiver gets approved plus the exact feedback string.
Cancelled response
send_cancelled receives feedback or no feedback
the receiver gets cancelled and optional feedback.
Empty feedback
feedback contains only whitespace
feedback is omitted from JSON.
Abandon/stale cancel
send_abandoned or send_stale_cancel is called
the receiver gets abandoned or cancelled with no feedback.
Double send
an action is sent twice on one state
the first call returns true and consumes the sender; later calls return false.

requirement: The plan approval view module SHALL provide pure formatting and response-channel helpers for AgentView while leaving focus transitions, prompt editing, comment selection, viewer lifecycle, and external transport ownership to its callers.
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: This file owns PlanApprovalViewState data, comment/plan feedback text assembly, inline source quoting, and serialization of the response sent through the supplied oneshot channel. It does not handle keys, mouse selection, line-viewer opening, prompt restoration, comment editing/deletion, undo groups, or network dispatch. The sender is supplied by the caller and consumed exactly once; stashed_prompt and stashed_feedback_prompt are state carriers whose orchestration is outside this file. Ten inline tests prove constructor defaults, outcome/feedback JSON and pure formatting cases, but not the AgentView integration.
scenarios: Caller-owned interaction
focus, prompt, comment selection, or viewer state changes
AgentView owns the transition and uses these helpers for data/response projections.
Transport handoff
a response sender is supplied
the module serializes and sends through that channel but does not create or retry transport.
Pure formatting
comments and optional plan content are supplied
feedback is built without filesystem reads or viewer side effects.
Integration boundary
the source is audited with its ten inline tests
JSON and formatting behavior is proven locally while UI routing and ACP caller behavior remain outside scope.

requirement: Use-tool block identity, state, copy text, and completion timing
contract: UseToolCallBlock SHALL store a qualified tool name, ordered input key/value pairs, optional output/error, and optional timing. new SHALL initialize empty arguments/output/error/timing; with_error and set_error SHALL mark failure; is_success SHALL be true exactly when error is absent. set_error and finish SHALL capture elapsed milliseconds once started_at exists without overwriting an existing elapsed value, while elapsed_ms SHALL expose stored time or the current duration. copy_text SHALL emit the tool name, each argument, a blank separator, and output text or `(no output)` when output is absent.
scenarios: Fresh block
UseToolCallBlock::new(tool_name) is constructed
the name is retained and args/output/error/timing are empty.
Error state
with_error or set_error receives an error
error is present and is_success returns false; set_error also captures elapsed time when applicable.
Completion timing
finish or elapsed_ms is called after timing starts
elapsed milliseconds are reported once and finish does not replace a stored duration.
Copy with arguments/output
the block has input_args and output
copy text lists `tool:`, each `key: value`, a blank line, and the output verbatim.
Copy without output
output is None
copy text ends with `(no output)` regardless of whether an error exists.
ACP materialization
a completed ACP tool call carries variant UseTool with tool_name and tool_input
tracker creates a UseTool block with the qualified name; a missing raw input does not panic.

requirement: Use-tool headers split qualified names and fit the action to available width
contract: split_name SHALL split once on MCP_TOOL_NAME_DELIMITER, titleize server and action independently, and return an empty server plus titleized full tool name for unqualified names. header_line SHALL render a qualified name as bold server plus command-colored action, an unqualified name as one bold span, and use truncation only on the action portion within the remaining width budget; unbounded headers SHALL preserve the full titleized name.
scenarios: Qualified name
tool_name contains the validated MCP delimiter
server and action are titleized and rendered as separate spans with a space separator.
Unqualified name
tool_name has no delimiter
the full titleized name is rendered as one bold header span and no empty server prefix is shown.
Narrow qualified header
max_width is smaller than server plus action
the server prefix is retained and only the action is truncated using saturating remaining width.
Narrow unqualified header
max_width is bounded for an unqualified name
the full titleized name is truncated to the width.
Collapsed muting
collapsed output requests muted styling
header styles use the theme muted style while expanded/preamble output uses normal primary/command styles.

requirement: Use-tool output renders arguments and bounded inline result panels
contract: BlockContent::output SHALL render a collapsed bounded header only. Truncated and Expanded modes SHALL render the unmuted wrapped header, then optional argument rows, then an output panel when output is present. Truncated mode SHALL show at most 3 output lines and Expanded mode at most 10; when more lines exist, each mode SHALL append a dim `{remaining} more lines, press Enter to view` marker. Output lines and panel separators SHALL use the dark panel background, arguments SHALL show muted keys and primary values, and errors SHALL append in the error color.
scenarios: Collapsed mode
ctx.mode is Collapsed
only the header line is emitted with collapsed muting and width truncation.
Arguments
input_args is non-empty in Truncated or Expanded mode
a separator and one `key: value` row per argument are emitted before output.
Truncated output
output has more than 3 lines
the first 3 lines render and a `(9 more lines, press Enter to view)` style marker reports the remainder.
Expanded output
output has more than 10 lines
