contract: Status mapping SHALL be active→Running, complete→Done{elapsed}, failed/interrupted→Failed{elapsed}, cancelled→Cancelled{elapsed}, cleared→remove the run_id mapping and finish its existing running entry, and unknown values→Paused{elapsed}. Existing mappings SHALL be used only when their EntryId still resolves; stale mappings are removed and a new WorkflowBlock::started is pushed. New blocks SHALL be indexed by run_id and mark the last scrollback entry running before status reconciliation. Existing blocks SHALL update status, cloned phase title/state, current_phase, active_agents, elapsed, and invalidate cache. Running entries SHALL be set running; non-running entries SHALL be finished; terminal Done/Failed/Cancelled entries SHALL remove the workflow_blocks mapping, while Paused retains it.
scenarios: Fresh active run
no valid mapping exists and status is active
one started Workflow block is pushed, mapped by run_id, and marked running.
Progress update
a mapped block receives new phases/current phase/active count/elapsed
the same block is mutated and its render cache invalidated.
Terminal completion
status is complete, failed, interrupted, or cancelled
the status includes elapsed duration, the entry is finished, and run_id mapping is removed.
Unknown status
wire status is not recognized
the block is Paused with elapsed duration and mapping remains available.
Cleared run
status is cleared
existing mapping is removed and its running entry is finished without creating a replacement block.
Stale mapping
workflow_blocks points to a missing scrollback entry
the stale map entry is removed and a new block is created.
Active roster
agent states are supplied
active_agents passed to block is recomputed from exact `running` states.

requirement: AgentView::ingest_workflow_update SHALL apply each accepted workflow projection to session.workflow_runs and the matching scrollback block within one view-domain method so rendering does not observe a partial update.
contract: For accepted non-cleared updates, ingest SHALL build a snapshot using the exact availability of an available command named `workflow-run`, replace the existing session snapshot with matching run_id or append it, then upsert the corresponding transcript block. For cleared updates, it SHALL remove all session snapshots with that run_id, then clear/finish the block mapping. It SHALL recompute active agents from the roster and pass the same phase/current/objective/status/elapsed data to block ingestion. Foreground, wire active_agents, and current_agent_label are intentionally ignored by this method.
scenarios: New snapshot
accepted non-cleared update has no matching session run
one WorkflowRunSnapshot is appended and one transcript block is upserted.
Existing snapshot
accepted update matches run_id in workflow_runs
the existing snapshot is replaced rather than duplicated.
Management command gate
available_commands contains name exactly workflow-run
management_available is true in the snapshot.
Missing gate
command list lacks exact workflow-run
management_available is false.
Cleared snapshot
status is cleared
all session snapshots with run_id are removed before block cleanup.
Atomic view update
rendering observes after ingest returns true
session projection and transcript block have both been processed by the same method.

requirement: Workflow ingestion SHALL treat Shell workflow notifications as authoritative projection data while keeping scrollback identity/cache and revision/tombstone bookkeeping local to AgentView/session state.
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: The method does not execute workflow operations, fetch definitions, infer process liveness, validate status/phase vocabulary, or derive active agent count from the wire count; it maps strings and roster facts into the common snapshot and block. Local workflow_run_revisions and cleared_workflow_runs gate replay/stale notifications, workflow_blocks maps run_id to EntryId, and ScrollbackState owns running/cache transitions. This source has no inline tests; integration tests in other modules are outside this file and cannot be claimed as local proof.
scenarios: Authoritative wire fields
a notification supplies arbitrary status/phase/state strings
values are retained/mapped according to visible string matches without schema validation.
Local identity
a run is updated repeatedly
run_id maps to a stable EntryId when the entry still exists.
Replay guard
old or cleared notifications arrive
local revision/tombstone state rejects the applicable stale update.
No inline proof
the source is statically audited
test_count is zero; ACP routing, server delivery, persistence/reload merge, and UI rendering remain unproven here.

requirement: Jump picker key mapping and activation contract
contract: handle_jump_key SHALL consume key-release events without state changes; map j/Down to MoveDown, k/Up to MoveUp, Enter to the selected row's JumpInput::Select or Consumed when no row exists, Esc to Dismissed, and every other key to Consumed. jump_activate SHALL resolve only the current selected index and return its prompt_entry_id as a stable EntryId; an empty list or stale selected index SHALL return Consumed.
scenarios: Navigation keys
a pressed key has j/Down, k/Up, Enter, Esc, or another key code
the corresponding JumpInput variant is returned and Enter carries the selected prompt EntryId when available.
Key release
a key event has KeyEventKind::Release
JumpInput::Consumed is returned regardless of its key code.
Empty activation
Enter is handled while entries are empty or selected is outside entries
activation returns Consumed and cannot produce an invalid EntryId.
Stable activation identity
a selected TimelineEntry exists and its positional index could later shift
activation returns prompt_entry_id rather than a positional turn index.

requirement: Jump picker cursor and hit-test contract
contract: move_cursor SHALL leave an empty picker unchanged and clamp selected to the inclusive [0, entries.len-1] range for positive or negative deltas. set_jump_cursor SHALL leave an empty picker unchanged, clamp a hovered index to the last row, and return true only when selected changes. jump_row_at SHALL delegate row geometry to ListOverlay using the current length and selected cursor, while jump_overlay_height SHALL use the same list geometry and screen height.
scenarios: Cursor movement
a nonempty picker receives a positive or negative delta
selected moves by the delta and clamps at the first or last entry.
Empty cursor
a picker has no entries and move_cursor or set_jump_cursor is called
selected is unchanged and set_jump_cursor returns false.
Mouse hover
a valid or out-of-range row index is supplied
the index is clamped to the last entry and the function reports whether selection changed.
Row hit geometry
a screen coordinate is above the title, on a visible row, outside the area, or beyond the visible window
jump_row_at returns the delegated visible entry index or None; overlay height follows ListOverlay's title/row/padding and screen-fraction caps.

requirement: Jump picker row rendering contract
contract: render_jump_overlay SHALL render through ListOverlay with the title Jump to which turn?, use the current theme, number the rows oldest-first from entry.turn_idx+1 with a gutter width equal to the decimal digit count of entries.len(), show (no preview) for empty previews, and truncate nonempty previews to the available content width after the ordinal gutter. Ordinals SHALL use gray over the shared row background; previews SHALL use text_primary over that background and become bold only for the cursor row. Shared ListOverlay focus, cursor background, unfocused dimming, title, accent bar, and visible-window geometry SHALL remain authoritative.
scenarios: Normal preview
a timeline entry has a nonempty preview and the overlay is rendered
the row contains a right-aligned one-based ordinal, a truncated preview within the row content width, and the cursor row uses bold preview text.
Missing preview
a timeline entry preview is empty
the row displays the literal (no preview) placeholder.
Wide ordinal gutter
entries.len has more decimal digits or turn_idx is larger
all ordinals use the shared widest decimal width and preserve row alignment.
Unfocused overlay
focused is false
ListOverlay dims the rendered area after the row content is painted, while row content still uses its resolved row background.

requirement: Jump picker transcript preview and viewport ownership contract
contract: A JumpState SHALL retain oldest-first TimelineEntry rows, selected cursor, and a JumpRestore containing optional width-stable ScrollAnchor, prior selection, and follow_mode. AgentView keyboard/mouse/wheel movement SHALL use the pure cursor helpers and live-scroll the selected prompt to the transcript top; Enter SHALL dispatch stable prompt selection; Esc SHALL dismiss and restore the bookmark/selection/follow mode. Input-owning overlays SHALL prevent or dismiss a hidden jump picker before it can consume input, while a running turn's cancel chord SHALL dismiss the picker and continue to CancelTurn.
scenarios: Open and preview
two or more timeline turns exist and /jump opens
the active/top turn is selected, restore state is captured, and the selected prompt is previewed at the transcript top.
Cursor preview
the selected row moves by key, mouse, or wheel
the cursor is clamped and the selected prompt is live-scrolled to the same top anchor used by Enter.
Dismiss restore
Esc or JumpDismiss occurs after preview movement
jump_state is removed and the captured scroll bookmark, prior selected entry, and follow mode are restored.
Stale selection
the selected stable EntryId disappears before confirmation
selection fails safely and the captured viewport is restored.
Overlay ownership
rewind, inline edit, /btw, pending input overlays, or session reload owns the prompt slot
the picker is refused or dropped before hidden state can consume wheel/keys; Ctrl-C remains available to cancel a running turn.

requirement: Minimal reasoning stream and native-palette fixture
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: run_reasoning_turn starts a ContentController with a Responses-backed test model, scripts a reasoning summary followed by answer text, sets the expected answer, writes show_thinking_blocks=true into the sandbox .grow/config.toml, optionally writes minimal_collapse_thinking=true to the sandbox pager.toml, spawns the pager in minimal mode with NO_COLOR=1, enables query responses, waits for minimal readiness, submits PROMPT, and waits for the answer sentinel and Thought header. Turn retains the harness, content controller, and inference expectation for later assertions.
scenarios: Reasoning stream setup
a test calls run_reasoning_turn with collapse_thinking false or true
the isolated Responses fixture streams reasoning and answer content through a minimal PTY with thinking blocks enabled and optional collapse configuration.
Post-turn observation
the helper completes its readiness, prompt submission, answer wait, and Thought-header wait
the returned Turn keeps the live harness and controller-backed expectation available to the caller.

requirement: Minimal reasoning and answer visual distinction check
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: The ignored minimal_thinking_is_visually_distinct_from_output PTY test waits for the reasoning sentinel, then checks plain screen text for a U+2503 accent rail on the reasoning row and its absence on the answer row. It inspects styled screen runs and requires every reasoning run containing the sentinel to be dim and italic, while at least one answer run containing its sentinel is neither dim nor italic. It also rejects a visible panicked marker and calls quit_minimal.
scenarios: Structural distinction
a reasoning response and answer are committed in minimal mode
the reasoning row starts with the configured rail and the answer row does not.
Native-palette emphasis
the test observes styled runs while NO_COLOR=1 is active
reasoning sentinel runs are DIM and ITALIC, while at least one answer sentinel run remains upright and undimmed.
Liveness
the visual assertions complete
the captured screen does not contain `panicked` and the test requests minimal-mode cleanup.

requirement: Minimal collapsed-thinking hint and Ctrl+E reopen check
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: The ignored minimal_collapse_thinking_toggle_folds_and_ctrl_e_reopens PTY test runs the fixture with minimal_collapse_thinking=true, waits for the `ctrl+e to expand` text, and requires the reasoning sentinel to be absent from full_text while collapsed. It injects byte 0x05 (Ctrl+E), then requires the reasoning sentinel to reappear in full_text, rejects a visible panicked marker, and calls quit_minimal.
scenarios: Collapsed body
the configured minimal thinking turn settles
the collapsed header advertises `ctrl+e to expand` and full_text does not contain the reasoning body sentinel.
Ctrl+E expansion
the test injects byte 0x05 after the collapsed assertion
the reasoning sentinel is reprinted into full_text.
Liveness
the expansion assertion completes
the captured screen does not contain `panicked` and the test requests minimal-mode cleanup.

requirement: The take-deferred test fixture SHALL construct ModelState with a current grow-build model, Medium reasoning state, and either a parseable or unsupported reasoning-effort metadata shape so resolution gates are exercised against explicit catalog facts.
contract: model_with_support SHALL create a ModelId from the supplied id and ModelInfo whose meta contains reasoningEffort=medium plus deep/xhigh and high/high menu options when supports is true, or only reasoningEffort=medium when false. models_with_current SHALL insert grow-build into available, set it current, and set reasoning_effort=Medium. All outcome assertions use these fixtures to distinguish supported menu, unsupported model, and active-model absence.
scenarios: Supported fixture
supports is true
the active model exposes remapped deep→Xhigh and canonical high→High choices.
Unsupported fixture
supports is false
the active model lacks a parseable reasoning menu and gate-first resolution reports Unsupported.
No-model fixture
ModelState::default is used
there is no current model for effort-only resolution.

requirement: take_deferred_model_switch SHALL resolve an effort-only CLI token against the active model, accept canonical values and remapped menu IDs, skip equal state, and return typed errors for unsupported/unknown/no-active cases.
contract: For no stashed switch, a supported active model SHALL resolve high to ReasoningEffort::High and deep (menu id) to Xhigh. If current reasoning_effort already equals the resolved value, switch SHALL be None with no error. A model without a usable reasoning-efforts menu SHALL return switch=None and EffortTokenError::Unsupported before token classification, including unknown tokens. A supported menu with an unrecognized token, including max when not offered, SHALL return switch=None and UnknownToken{token,offered:[deep,high]}. No active model SHALL return NoActiveModel.
scenarios: Canonical token
active grow-build supports menu and token is high
outcome switch targets current model with High and no error.
Remapped menu id
token is deep
outcome switch targets current model with Xhigh and no error.
Equal effort
current effort is already High and token is high
no switch is emitted and no error is reported.
Unsupported canonical
active model lacks reasoning menu and token is high
Unsupported is reported rather than silently applying effort.
Unsupported unknown
active model lacks reasoning menu and token is bogus
Unsupported wins over unknown token classification.
Unknown supported token
supported model receives bogus or max
UnknownToken carries original token and offered deep/high IDs.
No active model
only an effort token exists with no current model
NoActiveModel is reported.

requirement: take_deferred_model_switch SHALL prefer an explicit stashed model/effort pair, re-resolve only when stashed effort is absent, and preserve a stashed model even when requested effort is unknown or unsupported.
contract: When a stashed (model,Some(effort)) exists, it SHALL be returned unchanged and ignore CLI effort. When a stashed model has None effort, CLI token resolution SHALL target that model/current catalog: deep can remap to Xhigh; an unknown token SHALL return switch=Some((model,None)) plus UnknownToken; an unsupported target model SHALL return switch=Some((model,None)) plus Unsupported. The model switch is never dropped merely because effort resolution fails.
scenarios: Explicit stash
stash is other-model/Low and CLI says high
outcome preserves other-model/Low with no error.
Missing stashed effort
stash is current/None and CLI says deep
outcome keeps model and resolves Xhigh.
Unknown stashed effort
stash is current/None and CLI says bogus
outcome keeps model with None effort and reports UnknownToken.
Unsupported stashed target
stash targets plain model with None and CLI says high
outcome keeps plain model with None effort and reports Unsupported.

requirement: apply_deferred_switch_outcome SHALL publish an effort-resolution failure as exactly one Error/Control Notice block, return no effect, and avoid also setting a toast.
contract: Given an agent and DeferredSwitchOutcome{switch=None, effort_error=Some(Unsupported)}, apply_deferred_switch_outcome SHALL return None, append exactly one scrollback entry, leave agent.toast None, and make the newest entry RenderBlock::Notice with NoticeTone::Error and NoticeCategory::Control. The test proves typed notice classification and no duplicate toast; it does not assert the complete notice text.
scenarios: Unsupported apply error
outcome contains Unsupported and no switch
one typed control error notice is appended and no effect is returned.
Toast exclusivity
the same failure is applied
agent.toast remains None, so the failure is not duplicated as a toast.
Notice classification
the newest block is inspected
it is RenderBlock::Notice with Error tone and Control category.

requirement: The take-deferred test module SHALL record resolution and notice contracts as focused lifecycle evidence while leaving stash consumption, model application, request effects, and transport behavior to the lifecycle implementation and other tests.
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: This 253-line source invokes take_deferred_model_switch and apply_deferred_switch_outcome only; it does not test apply_deferred_model_switch consumption, actual model-setting effects, ACP requests, or retry/transport. The fixture uses exact catalog IDs/menu IDs and asserts full DeferredSwitchOutcome equality, including offered IDs and preserved model. The notice test checks count, toast absence, variant, tone, and category but not message content.
scenarios: Outcome evidence
a deferred switch input is resolved
the test compares the complete typed outcome rather than only a boolean.
Notice evidence
an effort error is applied to an AgentView test app
scrollback, toast, variant, tone, and category boundaries are checked.
Unproven caller behavior
stash application or request emission is needed
this file provides no assertion about consuming stash or emitting a model/effort effect.
No runtime execution
the source is statically audited
13 inline tests are registered; Cargo/Rust execution is intentionally absent.

requirement: Scrollback horizontal column layout contract
contract: HorizontalLayout::new SHALL partition an input Rect into an accent column of width 1, a configurable left padding column, a flexible content column with Constraint::Min(1), and a configurable right padding column, preserving the input y/height. new_default SHALL use LayoutConfig::default, and chrome_width SHALL equal 1 + block_pad_left + block_pad_right. The partition is the shared column model for scrollback entry rendering and selection geometry.
scenarios: Configured layout
an area and LayoutConfig are supplied
accent width is 1, left/right widths equal the configured pads, content receives the remaining layout allocation, and all columns share the area's vertical extent.
Default layout
new_default is called
the same partition is produced using LayoutConfig::default.
Chrome width
chrome_width is requested for a config
the returned width is exactly accent plus both horizontal pads and excludes flexible content.
Narrow area
fixed pads consume most or all of the input width
the ratatui layout remains the single source for the columns and callers receive the resulting bounded Rects.

requirement: Scrollback entry area and content-width projection contract
contract: entry_content_area SHALL return one contiguous Rect beginning at accent.x/y and spanning accent, left padding, content, and right padding with the accent height. entry_area SHALL be an exact alias of entry_content_area. content_width SHALL return only the flexible content column width. These projections SHALL be used as the full EntryRenderer area versus the BlockContext/inline-edit content width so accent and padding are not double-counted.
scenarios: Full entry area
a HorizontalLayout has configured columns
entry_content_area and entry_area cover accent through right padding with the same y/height and total width.
Content width
a block or inline editor requests content width
content_width returns only the content column, excluding accent and both padding columns.
Render integration
scrollback render constructs a HorizontalLayout and passes entry_content_area to EntryRenderer
the renderer receives full entry chrome while its block context uses content width after any timestamp reservation.
Measurement integration
layout/cache or inline-edit sizing requests a simulated width
entry_area_width and entry_text_column_width round-trip through the same HorizontalLayout projections, keeping measurement and paint widths consistent.

requirement: Scrollback selection area and edge-safety contract
contract: selection_area SHALL preserve the entry row's y and height, begin one column before accent when available, and extend the entry_content_area width by two columns so selection borders occupy one outer-padding column on each side. The left x coordinate SHALL use saturating subtraction at screen edge. for_row SHALL preserve all x/width columns and replace only y/height, allowing selection and rendering to share identical horizontal geometry for each clipped or sticky row.
scenarios: Selection expansion
an entry layout is inside outer padding
selection_area starts at accent.x-1 and has entry_content_area.width+2, with the same vertical extent.
Left screen edge
accent.x is zero
selection_area.x remains zero instead of underflowing.
Row projection
a base layout is projected to a row y/height
for_row changes every column's y and height while retaining x and width, and the resulting selection area follows the row.
Sticky/selected rendering
scrollback or sticky-header code draws a SelectionBox for a row
the selection border uses the same expanded area as the content row, including one column outside each content edge.

requirement: Scrollback layout width consistency across measurement and rendering contract
contract: Every scrollback path that paints, measures, hit-tests, or edits an entry SHALL derive horizontal chrome and content widths from HorizontalLayout with the active LayoutConfig. EntryRenderer height/paint calculations, ScrollbackState simulated width helpers, selection VisibleBlockGeometry, sticky-header rendering, and inline-edit text sizing SHALL therefore agree on accent and padding widths; callers may subtract block-specific reservations such as timestamps only after obtaining content_width.
scenarios: Paint/measure agreement
a block is measured and later rendered at the same viewport width/config
both paths derive the same content column before block-specific timestamp/media adjustments.
Selection agreement
an entry is selected or hit-tested, including a sticky header
selection width is derived from the same HorizontalLayout as the painted entry and extends into outer padding consistently.
Inline edit agreement
the inline editor computes its text column from a viewport width
the textarea width uses HorizontalLayout::content_width rather than the full entry or raw viewport width.
Config change
block_pad_left/right changes in active appearance
all listed consumers observe the new pads through a fresh HorizontalLayout rather than stale hard-coded offsets.

requirement: File-search dropdown visibility and height budget
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: render_dropdown returns without writing when the item area has zero height, width below four columns, or FileSearchState::is_visible is false. FileSearchState::is_visible is true only when an @ context exists and the top-k result list is non-empty. dropdown_height returns zero when hidden and otherwise returns one separator row plus min(FileSearchState::result_count, max_rows); the caller-owned panel chrome is outside render_dropdown. MAX_DROPDOWN_ROWS is a public eight-row constant, while dropdown_height accepts its row cap as an argument.
scenarios: Hidden or undersized area
the file-search state is hidden, the area height is zero, or the area width is below four
render_dropdown exits before painting result rows.
Visible height request
the state is visible and a max_rows value is supplied
dropdown_height returns one plus the smaller of the result count and max_rows.
No results
the context is present but the top-k result list is empty
FileSearchState::is_visible is false and the renderer remains hidden.

requirement: File-search result viewport and scrollbar projection
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: render_dropdown reads the top-k results, selected index, scroll offset, hovered index, and directory mode from FileSearchState. It maps each visible row to scroll_offset + row until the top-k list ends, passes selection and hover flags to the row renderer, and reserves two columns whenever top-k length exceeds the item area height. The scrollbar occupies the rightmost one-column Rect and is rendered with total top-k length, the item area height, and the current scroll offset using the theme dark track and dim-gray thumb styles.
scenarios: Scrolled result window
a visible state has a nonzero scroll offset and enough top-k results to fill the area
rows begin at the offset index and stop at the result-list end without indexing beyond top-k.
Overflowing result list
top-k length is greater than the item-area height
two columns are reserved from row content and render_scrollbar_styled receives a right-edge one-column scrollbar area.
Short result list
top-k length is at most the item-area height
all available rows use the full area width and no scrollbar call is made.

requirement: Fuzzy path row selection and match styling
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: render_fuzzy_item returns when the content width is less than PREFIX_WIDTH plus one cell. It normalizes a leading ./ from the path, fills the row with the chosen background, and chooses embedded-row styling first, then selected background, hovered background, or the normal light background. Selected rows use the prompt arrow and bold text; non-selected rows use a two-space gutter. Characters whose zero-based path character index is the next item index receive the fuzzy accent foreground, while other characters use the primary foreground, and selected styling adds bold to both. Wide characters write continuation cells with the same style.
scenarios: Selected row
a result row is selected and has enough content width
the row background is selected or embedded-selected styling, the arrow prefix is painted, and rendered path text is bold.
Hovered row
a non-selected row is hovered
the row uses hover background while retaining the non-selected gutter and primary or fuzzy-match foregrounds.
Embedded row style
modal_window::embedded_row_style returns a style for the row
that embedded background and foreground override the normal, selected, or hover row colors according to the source precedence.
Fuzzy match indices
the result supplies character indices alongside a path
matching path characters consume indices in order and use fuzzy accent styling; unmatched characters use normal styling.

requirement: Unicode-aware path truncation and directory marker
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: render_fuzzy_item measures each path scalar with UnicodeWidthChar, writes characters from byte-aligned slices, and when the next character would exceed max_col replaces the preceding visible cell with an ellipsis when one exists. Wide characters fill their continuation cells with spaces and the same style. When directory mode is true, a slash is appended at the current column only if a cell remains inside the row width.
scenarios: Long path
a path character would exceed the available row width
the renderer stops path output and places an ellipsis in the last visible path cell when possible.
Wide path character
a path contains a character whose display width is greater than one and it fits
the leading cell receives the character and continuation cells receive styled spaces.
Directory-only query
FileSearchState::is_dir_mode is true and a column remains after the path
the renderer writes a slash with normal row styling.
No marker space
directory mode is true but the path ends at max_col
no slash is written beyond the row area.

requirement: File-search panel chrome ownership boundary
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: The dropdown renderer paints result rows only. AgentView::draw creates and clears the surrounding panel, draws the top and bottom border lines and k/n hint, computes the item area with the caller row cap, and records the item area for later interaction; render_dropdown receives that inner Rect and does not render borders, separators, or the count hint.
scenarios: Panel composition
AgentView::draw displays file search with a positive item count and sufficient panel dimensions
the caller paints panel chrome and invokes render_dropdown for the inner item area.
Panel too narrow
the computed panel width is not greater than four or the borders cannot be placed
the caller skips the panel and clears dropdown_items_area rather than invoking the row renderer.

requirement: AgentView SHALL close an open jump picker by consuming its JumpState and restoring the captured selection, width-stable scroll bookmark, and follow mode.
contract: dismiss_jump_picker SHALL take jump_state and, when present, call restore_jump_viewport. restore_jump_viewport SHALL restore prior selected EntryId, restore_scroll_bookmark when present, and re-enable follow_mode when the captured flag is true. It SHALL be safe when no picker is open; it does not synthesize a new bookmark or disable follow when the captured flag is false.
scenarios: Dismiss open picker
jump_state contains JumpRestore
state is removed and prior selection/bookmark/follow are restored.
Dismiss absent picker
jump_state is None
no scrollback mutation occurs.
Selection restoration
restore.selected is Some or None
scrollback selection is set to exactly the captured value.
Follow restoration
restore.follow_mode is true
follow mode is re-enabled after bookmark restoration.
Resize-safe bookmark
preview moved or width changed
the stored ScrollAnchor is passed to scrollback restoration rather than recomputing by index.

requirement: AgentView SHALL treat rewind, inline edit, BTW, and any pending input overlay as mutually exclusive with jump, and SHALL drop a hidden picker before it can consume input or scrolling.
contract: jump_slot_taken SHALL return true when rewind_state, inline_edit, or btw_state is present, or no_input_overlay_pending is false. dismiss_jump_picker_if_suppressed SHALL dismiss an existing picker only when that predicate is true and return true iff it dropped one; otherwise it returns false. This lets input/scroll callers spend the current Esc/key on the owning overlay rather than a shadowed picker.
scenarios: Rewind takeover
rewind_state is present while jump is open
jump_slot_taken is true and suppression clears jump.
Inline-edit takeover
inline_edit is present
jump is considered unavailable.
BTW takeover
btw_state is present
jump is considered unavailable.
Pending interaction
no_input_overlay_pending is false
jump is suppressed for permission/question/cancel/plan-style ownership.
No takeover
no other overlay owns slot
an open picker is not dismissed by suppression.
Hidden picker input
overlay appears after picker opened
caller can clear jump before wheel/key routing reaches picker cursor.

requirement: AgentView SHALL delegate jump key semantics to pure JumpState helpers, live-scroll moved selection to the transcript top, and map select/dismiss/consumed inputs to shared InputOutcome values.
contract: handle_jump_key SHALL return Unchanged when jump_state is absent. For MoveUp/MoveDown it SHALL mutate the selected cursor with move_cursor, call sync_jump_preview, and return Changed. Other JumpInput values SHALL map Select(id) to Action::JumpPickerSelect(id), Dismissed to Action::JumpDismiss, and MoveUp/MoveDown/Consumed to Changed. sync_jump_preview SHALL resolve the selected TimelineEntry prompt_entry_id by stable scrollback EntryId and call scroll_to_entry_top; missing selection or removed entry SHALL be a no-op.
scenarios: No picker
a key arrives with jump_state None
InputOutcome::Unchanged is returned.
Move preview
Up or Down is accepted by the picker
cursor moves through move_cursor, selected prompt is scrolled to top, and outcome is Changed.
Stable preview
selected prompt EntryId no longer exists
no scroll is performed rather than landing on an unrelated block.
Select
JumpInput::Select(id) is produced
Action::JumpPickerSelect(id) is returned.
Dismiss
JumpInput::Dismissed is produced
Action::JumpDismiss is returned.
Consumed navigation
helper returns Consumed
Changed is returned without dispatch action.

requirement: AgentView SHALL map mouse movement and left-button activation within the prompt pane to jump cursor updates, live preview, and stable selection/dismiss outcomes while ignoring outside or unsupported mouse events.
contract: handle_jump_mouse SHALL return Unchanged when no picker is open or jump_row_at cannot map the mouse coordinates in pane_areas.prompt. MouseEventKind::Moved SHALL call set_jump_cursor; only a changed cursor triggers sync_jump_preview and Changed, otherwise Unchanged. MouseEventKind::Down(Left) SHALL set cursor, call jump_activate, and map its JumpInput through jump_input_to_outcome. Other buttons/kinds SHALL be ignored.
scenarios: Outside picker
mouse row/column is outside prompt area
jump_row_at yields None and outcome is Unchanged.
Hover move
pointer maps to a different row
cursor changes, selected prompt previews at top, and outcome is Changed.
Same-row move
pointer maps to current row
no scroll mutation occurs and outcome is Unchanged.
Left click
left button goes down on a mapped row
cursor is set, row activation runs, and select/dismiss/consumed outcome is returned.
Other mouse event
button or kind is unsupported
outcome is Unchanged.

requirement: The jump AgentView layer SHALL keep preview and restoration consistent across key/mouse/scroll entry points without duplicating picker geometry, cursor clamping, action dispatch, or overlay admission logic.
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: sync_jump_preview uses the same selected stable prompt identity that jump_to_turn commits and scrolls it to the viewport TOP; this file delegates row geometry/cursor limits/activation to views::jump and returns Action/InputOutcome for outer dispatch. It does not open the picker, build timeline entries, handle wheel routing, execute selected turns, or decide global overlay priority beyond its jump_slot_taken predicate. The one inline test proves a selected first turn moves the transcript upward from bottom; restoration, action routing, overlay suppression, and mouse paths remain source contracts here.
scenarios: Top-anchor preview
selected first timeline entry is far above current bottom
scroll offset decreases because preview uses scroll_to_entry_top.
Shared helpers
key/mouse paths request movement or activation
both route through common JumpInput mapping instead of duplicating actions.
Outer admission
/jump needs to open or another overlay appears
root/outer handlers own picker creation and call suppression before input routing.
Audit boundary
the source is inspected with one inline test
the source-level count is one inline test; broader jump behavior is covered by other modules and not claimed here.

requirement: BlockRenderer builder and BlockContext projection contract
contract: BlockRenderer::new SHALL initialize Expanded mode, is_running=false, raw=false, no explicit background, no max_lines, and AppearanceConfig::default. The mode, running, raw, background, max_lines and appearance builder methods SHALL replace only their corresponding renderer option and return the renderer for chaining. make_context SHALL pass those options plus the requested width into BlockContext, set is_selected=false and cwd=None, and clone the stored appearance.
scenarios: Default context
a block is wrapped with BlockRenderer::new and rendered or measured
BlockContent receives Expanded, not running, non-raw context with no max_lines, default appearance, unselected state and no cwd.
Configured context
one or more builder methods are chained
the block receives the selected display mode, running/raw flags, optional max_lines, explicit appearance and requested width while unrelated defaults remain unchanged.
Background override
background(color) is chained
resolve_background returns the explicit color without consulting the block's declared background or current theme.
Block background fallback
no explicit background is set and the block reports None, Light, or Dark
the wrapper resolves None, Theme::current().bg_light, or Theme::current().bg_dark respectively.

requirement: BlockRenderer desired-height and vertical-padding contract
contract: BlockRenderer::desired_height SHALL build a BlockContext for the requested width, obtain BlockContent::output and BlockContent::has_vpad, and return output.lines.len() plus two rows when vertical padding is enabled or no extra rows otherwise. The same has_vpad decision SHALL govern render's top and bottom padding, and a one-line vpad block SHALL therefore measure and render as three rows.
scenarios: Padded block
output has N lines and has_vpad is true
desired_height returns N+2; render leaves the first row empty, paints content starting on the second row, and reserves the final row as bottom padding.
Unpadded block
output has N lines and has_vpad is false
desired_height returns N and render starts content at area.y with no synthetic top/bottom rows.
Height-limited area
the render area has fewer rows than desired_height
the wrapper paints only content lines that fit after any top pad and stops at max_row without writing below the area.
Width-sensitive output
BlockContent output or has_vpad depends on context width/appearance
desired_height and render each build the corresponding width-aware context before deciding output and padding.

requirement: BlockRenderer background and bounded line rendering contract
contract: Renderable::render SHALL return without invoking the block when area.width or area.height is zero. For a nonempty area it SHALL resolve background precedence, apply the resolved background style to every cell without changing the row layout, apply each BlockLine background from area.x + bg_start_col to the remaining row width, and render line.content with SafeBuf::set_line_safe at area.x and the current row bounded by area.width. It SHALL process output lines in order, stop at the area bottom, and leave bottom padding as already-filled background. BlockRenderer SHALL paint all line backgrounds it receives; panel-versus-semantic suppression is a higher-level EntryRenderer concern.
scenarios: Empty area
render is called with zero width or zero height
the function returns without block output, background resolution, or Buffer writes.
Resolved block background
the block declares None, Light, or Dark and no explicit override exists
the entire area receives no background, theme light, or theme dark respectively.
Explicit background
background(color) is configured
every cell in the area receives the explicit color, including top and bottom vpad rows.
Line background offset
a BlockLine has background Some(color) and bg_start_col
only the suffix beginning at area.x+bg_start_col receives that line background, while set_line_safe paints content over the bounded row.
Clipped output
output has more lines than area height
lines after the bottom boundary are not painted and no out-of-area Buffer access occurs.

requirement: Shared overlay height and row-window geometry
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: ListOverlay::height caps the data rows at MAX_ROWS (15), forms 2 + rows for title plus rows, caps that value at max(60% of screen_h using integer division, 6), and adds one padding row. ListOverlay::visible_rows subtracts three rows from the supplied area with saturating arithmetic, reserving the title and padding. ListOverlay::scroll_offset returns zero while the selected row fits in the visible window and otherwise shifts the first visible index to selected - visible_rows + 1.
scenarios: Small list
a two-row list is measured on a 40-row screen
height returns five rows for title, two data rows, and padding.
Maximum row cap
a list has thirty entries on a 40-row screen
height returns eighteen rows after the fifteen-row cap and one padding row.
Screen fraction cap
a thirty-entry list is measured on a 12-row screen
the 60% cap with its six-row minimum limits the returned height to eight.

requirement: Overlay row hit-testing excludes chrome and padding
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: ListOverlay::row_at accepts only a nonzero area at least ten columns wide, with the point inside the Rect. It treats area.y + 2 as the first selectable row, rejects the title rows and the trailing rows outside visible_rows(area), then returns scroll_offset(visible_rows) + relative row only when the resulting index is below len. Horizontal and vertical coordinates outside the Rect return None.
scenarios: Title and row mapping
a point is on the title row, first data row, later data row, or trailing padding row
the title and padding return None, while the first and third data rows map to indices zero and two.
Horizontal exclusion
the column is outside the overlay Rect
row_at returns None without producing a list index.
Last-row exclusion
the relative row is inside the geometry but the computed index is at or beyond len
row_at returns None.

requirement: Selected-row scrolling keeps the cursor visible
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: For a valid selected index at or below the current visible-row count, ListOverlay::scroll_offset shifts the row window so the selected row is the last visible row. ListOverlay::row_at and ListOverlay::render use that same offset, so logical row indices and painted rows share the window projection.
scenarios: Cursor at list end
a 20-row list has seven visible rows and selected is 19
the window starts at index 13; the first painted or hit-tested row is 13 and the last is 19.
Cursor in initial window
selected is less than visible_rows
the offset remains zero and the first row maps to index zero.

requirement: Shared overlay chrome and row-context rendering
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: ListOverlay::render returns for zero-height or sub-ten-column areas. Otherwise it fills the area with theme.bg_light, paints the theme accent bar in the first column, places a bold accent title at area.y + 1 after a three-column inset, and renders at most visible_rows rows from the shared scroll window. Each row receives RowCtx with cursor state, resolved row background, and content width; the row closure supplies Line content while the renderer paints the row background and clips the line to content width. A focused cursor row uses theme.bg_visual and every other row uses the panel background.
scenarios: Focused cursor row
render receives focused=true and the loop reaches selected
the selected row gets theme.bg_visual and RowCtx::is_cursor is true.
Non-cursor row
render paints a row that is not selected or is unfocused
the row background is theme.bg_light and RowCtx::is_cursor is false for a non-selected row.
Narrow or empty area
the area height is zero or width is below ten
render returns before changing the buffer.
Row content projection
the supplied closure returns a Line for a visible index
the closure receives the row index and RowCtx and the line is written at the content origin up to content_width.

requirement: Unfocused overlay dimming and shared picker integration
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: After painting the overlay, ListOverlay::render applies blend_area to the whole area with the panel background and a 0.66 blend when focused is false; focused overlays skip that dim pass. The /jump and /rewind views construct ListOverlay from their own length and selected state, delegate height and row hit-testing to it, and supply only picker-specific row content to render, so this module owns shared chrome and geometry while callers own entry formatting and input/state semantics.
scenarios: Unfocused overlay
focused is false after rows and chrome are painted
blend_area is applied across the full overlay with the bg_light target and 0.66 amount.
Focused overlay
focused is true
the shared unfocus blend is skipped and row content keeps its resolved styles.
Jump picker reuse
render_jump_overlay, jump_overlay_height, or jump_row_at is used
the jump view routes geometry through ListOverlay and its closure formats ordinal and preview content.
Rewind picker reuse
render_rewind_overlay, rewind_overlay_height, or rewind_row_at handles Picker phase
the rewind view routes geometry through ListOverlay and its closure formats preview and file metadata.

requirement: format_doctor SHALL render the DiagnosticReport environment section in stable order, include only available optional facts, and map terminal/host/runtime capabilities to human-readable labels without inventing unavailable evidence.
contract: The output SHALL begin with Environment and terminal, then xtversion only for RuntimeFact::Available, multiplexer, optional byobu, ssh yes/no, color only for RuntimeFact::Available, and themes as all when available count equals total or `<count>/<total>: <display names>` otherwise. keyboard SHALL render modifier_delivery.label plus OS rescue active only for HostOs::Macos and unavailable text otherwise. newline SHALL render a fixed Alt+Enter prefix with VTE version/legacy, xterm.js, or Kitty-protocol explanation. Unavailable/NoReply runtime facts SHALL not produce false rows. The formatter preserves input display labels/order and does not probe the environment.
scenarios: Healthy local
Ghostty, no tmux, truecolor, local route and no optional facts are present
Environment and Clipboard sections use the stable minimal rows and end with No issues found.
Optional runtime
xtversion is Available
an xtversion row is inserted after terminal.
Limited themes
color is available but available themes are fewer than total
theme names render as count/total with display names.
Keyboard host
keyboard fact exists for MacOS
the row includes modifier label and OS rescue active.
Newline capability
newline is Vte/XtermJs/NoKittyKeyboardProtocol
the row consistently begins Alt+Enter and explains the capability limitation.
Unavailable probes
runtime/probe results are unavailable or errors
the report omits unsupported evidence rather than creating false issues.

requirement: format_doctor SHALL project clipboard preflight, transport routes, display-server capability, and delivery confidence into a stable Clipboard section with safe human labels.
contract: Clipboard native SHALL map LocalAvailable to `local (tool)`, RemoteOnly plus container_no_display to `container (tool)`, RemoteOnly otherwise to `remote (tool)`, Unavailable to unavailable, and Disabled to off. tmux and wrap routes SHALL render on/off. osc 52 SHALL render osc52_capability.label only when osc52_route is true, otherwise off. data-control SHALL appear only for Wayland and be on only for DataControlFact::Available. delivery SHALL map Confirmed/Unverified/Failed to confirmed/unverified/unavailable. Clipboard output does not itself apply fixes or claim a successful copy beyond the supplied delivery fact.
scenarios: Local native route
native preflight is LocalAvailable
native row names local tool.
Remote SSH route
preflight is RemoteOnly
native row names remote or container based on container_no_display.
Disabled/unavailable native
preflight is Disabled or Unavailable
native row says off or unavailable.
Transport routes
tmux_route, osc52_route, wrap_sink vary
each route gets the exact on/off or capability label.
Wayland data control
display server is Wayland
data-control row appears and reflects Available vs other.
Non-Wayland data control
display server is not Wayland
data-control row is omitted.
Delivery status
delivery is Confirmed, Unverified, or Failed
status says confirmed, unverified, or unavailable.
SSH wrapping
SSH is true and wrap sink is inactive/active
unwrapped output includes terminal.ssh-wrap recommendation; wrapped output does not.

requirement: format_findings SHALL partition DiagnosticFinding values by disposition, render stable issue/recommendation sections, and choose remediation wording from automatic fix metadata and config path while preserving notes.
contract: Issues SHALL be collected in input order. When issue findings exist, output SHALL use `Issues (N)` and format each with `!`; when none exist and report.issue_count()==0 it SHALL emit `No issues found.`; when issue_count is nonzero without issue findings it SHALL emit `An issue is shown in the Clipboard status above.` Recommendations SHALL be omitted when empty and otherwise follow issues with `Recommendations` and `i` markers. format_finding SHALL print id/message, prefer human_fix_command(fix_id) over automatic.command for Automatic setup, then choose Add `<fix>` to `<config_path>` when path exists, One-off when automatic remediation exists without path, or Run otherwise, followed by Note when present.
scenarios: No findings
issues and recommendations are empty and issue_count is zero
No issues found is printed.
Legacy fact issue
issue findings are empty but report.issue_count is one
the clipboard status phrase appears and No issues found is absent.
Issue list
issue findings are present
Issues count and ! rows preserve finding order.
Recommendation list
recommendations are present
Recommendations follows issues and i rows preserve order.
Automatic config fix
automatic remediation and config_path exist
Automatic setup and Add wording are both shown.
Automatic one-off
automatic remediation exists without config path
One-off wording is shown.
Manual fix
only remediation exists
Run wording is shown.
Note
finding.note exists
Note is appended after remediation.
Ordering
runtime merge yields issues plus recommendations
one Issues section appears before Recommendations with no duplicate IDs.

requirement: The doctor formatter integration tests SHALL prove that runtime findings merge into one report, retain useful issue/recommendation content, and keep stable exact strings for terminal, clipboard, color, SSH, newline, keyboard, and WezTerm cases.
contract: The external doctor_format_tests module builds reports from probe snapshots, optionally merges collect_tui_runtime_findings, and asserts complete or substring-stable output. It SHALL demonstrate tmux issue IDs occur once after merge, startup notification/focus findings remain visible with config path, runtime issue sections precede recommendations, and exact formatted report strings remain stable for healthy local, tmux misconfiguration, limited color, SSH wrapping, WezTerm xtversion, VS Code newline, and explicit keyboard target evidence.
scenarios: Snapshot formatting matrix
the tests supply local, tmux, SSH, WezTerm, VS Code, limited-color, keyboard, and unavailable probe snapshots
format_doctor output matches the expected section/order/wording for each case.
Runtime merge
collect_tui_runtime_findings are merged into a report
existing view findings are not duplicated and issue/recommendation sections remain ordered.
Runtime startup content
notification/focus findings are generated
useful bell/config/focus guidance and exactly one ID occurrence are visible.
Host keyboard evidence
KeyboardFact uses explicit MacOS target
the formatter uses snapshot host and emits OS rescue active with modifier labels.
Regression strings
formatter output is compared with concat literals or substring assertions
small wording changes surface as test failures rather than silent schema drift.

requirement: The doctor formatter SHALL consume a completed DiagnosticReport and produce human-readable text without probing terminals, mutating diagnostics, applying fixes, writing JSON, or executing clipboard/SSH remediation.
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: format_doctor delegates fact collection and finding generation to callers and only reads report.facts, report.findings, and report.issue_count. format_findings/format_finding concatenate strings directly, preserve finding order, do not sanitize control characters or truncate messages, and use human_fix_command only for display fallback. The formatter does not alter the report or perform remediation; runtime test helpers invoke it after snapshot/view/merge setup.
scenarios: Pure input
a DiagnosticReport is supplied
the function returns a String based only on report values.
No side effects
formatting is requested for a finding with fix metadata
commands are described in text but not executed.
Long/control text
finding message/note includes arbitrary content
text is concatenated as supplied; no truncation or control-character filtering is applied.
Audit boundary
the source and external path test module are read
main formatter has no inline tests; 13 external tests provide output evidence but do not prove probes/remediation execution.

requirement: Welcome top-bar location and announcement rendering contract
contract: render_top_bar SHALL render the location_line at the first row of the supplied area after truncating it to the area's terminal width. If an announcement has a message and the area has more than one row, it SHALL render that message in text_primary on the rows below the location line using a Paragraph; absent messages or a one-row area SHALL render no announcement rows. The location row SHALL remain bounded by area.width through truncate_line and set_line.
scenarios: Location row
render_top_bar receives a nonempty area
the current location line is width-truncated and painted at area.x/area.y without exceeding area.width.
Announcement message
announcement.message is Some and area.height > 1
the message is painted with text_primary beginning at area.y+1 in the remaining area height.
No announcement
announcement is absent or its message is None
only the location row is rendered.
Single-row top bar
area.height is 0 or 1
no announcement paragraph is rendered; the location write is still bounded by the supplied width.

requirement: Git branch and worktree location-line contract
contract: location_line_at SHALL read the per-cwd lazy Git cache without spawning a blocking git operation in the render path, then compose spans in this order: optional branch span plus gray separator, optional accent_user worktree badge, and gray_dim actual cwd display. A present nonempty branch SHALL render branch_icon plus the branch; a present empty branch SHALL render branch_icon plus detached; is_worktree SHALL add exactly the worktree badge; absent Git info SHALL still render the cwd display. location_line SHALL apply the same formatting to the live process cwd, falling back to `.` when current_dir fails.
scenarios: Branched repository
cached CwdGitInfo has a nonempty branch
the line begins with the branch icon and branch in dim text_primary, followed by a gray separator and cwd.
Detached repository
cached branch is Some("")
the branch span says detached after the branch icon.
Linked worktree
cached info has is_worktree=true
a worktree badge in accent_user appears before the cwd display, while the branch span remains when present.
Cache miss or non-repository
cwd_git_info_lazy returns None
the line omits branch and badge but still shows the cwd display.
Live cwd wrapper
location_line is called
the helper reads process_cwd and delegates all composition to location_line_at.

requirement: Cwd display and worktree provenance formatting contract
contract: format_cwd_display SHALL show the actual supplied cwd, collapse a home-directory prefix to `~`, and append ` (worktree of {main_repo})` only when CwdGitInfo.main_repo is Some. It SHALL preserve subdirectories under the worktree/current cwd, show the raw cwd on cache miss, and ignore worktree_label for this display. format_cwd_parts SHALL implement the same suffix decision without global state.
scenarios: Plain repository cwd
main_repo is None and cwd is a path inside or outside home
the display is the actual cwd, with a home prefix collapsed when home_dir is available.
Worktree provenance
main_repo is Some
the actual worktree cwd is followed by the main repository suffix.
Subdirectory
cwd points below a repository or linked worktree root
the subdirectory path remains visible; formatting does not replace it with the repo root or worktree label.
Cache miss
info is None
the raw cwd is returned after home collapsing and no worktree suffix is added.
Pure formatting
format_cwd_parts receives display and optional main_repo
the exact suffix result is deterministic without reading process or Git state.

requirement: Shared location header width and staged-cwd integration contract
contract: Consumers of location_line_at SHALL supply the effective/staged cwd rather than relying on the process cwd when the application owns a different directory, then truncate the returned Line to the available label budget before painting or recording hit geometry. Dashboard header integration SHALL preserve the location label and state chips, keep the label from overlapping chips, and use the same branch/cwd/worktree span semantics as the welcome top bar. Hover decorations MAY underline visible location text while leaving whitespace and branch icon padding bare.
scenarios: Staged directory
dashboard state.cwd changes before the process cwd effect completes
the header renders the staged cwd immediately.
Wide header
the label budget is large enough
the header shows cwd location plus any Git/worktree context and preserves right-side state chips.
Narrow header
chips or CTA consume most of the row
location_line_at output is truncated against the computed budget and does not overpaint chips or buttons.
Location hover
the dashboard location hit is hovered
visible location text may be underlined while leading whitespace, separators and branch icon remain un-underlined.
Welcome caller
render_welcome builds its top_bar_inner
the top bar receives the margin-adjusted one-row area and uses the live process cwd wrapper.

requirement: Minimal transcript pager race fixture and environment setup
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: The ignored Tokio PTY test first probes `less --version` and returns with a skip message when the executable is unavailable. When available, it starts ContentController, sets the mock response to MOCK_RESPONSE_SENTINEL followed by ` transcript body.`, constructs PAGER=less and GROW_TEST_FRAME_WRITE_DELAY_MS=40 overrides, resolves the pager binary, spawns DEFAULT_ROWS by DEFAULT_COLS with MINIMAL_ARGS, enables terminal query responses, and waits for the minimal idle sentinel.
scenarios: Pager unavailable
the `less --version` command cannot be started
the test prints a skip message and returns before starting the mock server or pager.
Deterministic minimal fixture
less is available
the test runs against an isolated ContentController response with PAGER=less, a 40 ms frame-write delay, minimal/no-leader arguments, default 50x120 geometry, and query replies enabled.
Minimal readiness
the spawned pager reaches the MINIMAL_IDLE_SENTINEL
the test proceeds with the transcript round trip from an idle minimal prompt.

requirement: Committed turn and queued composer edits before pager suspend
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: After readiness, the test submits PROMPT with carriage return and waits up to 30 seconds for MOCK_RESPONSE_SENTINEL in full_text, then gives the delayed writer three seconds to settle. It injects `zetaquxdraft` through inject_keys_paced, waits 120 ms, sends Ctrl+U (byte 0x15), injects `/transcript` one byte at a time, and submits it with carriage return. This sequence creates the committed transcript content and queues draft-kill, slash-dropdown, and submit-clear frames immediately before the external pager takes the tty.
scenarios: Committed transcript
the minimal prompt is submitted and the mock sentinel appears in full_text
the test has a completed turn available before exercising the transcript pager.
Queued draft mutation
the paced draft is typed, settled briefly, and Ctrl+U is injected
the test requests deletion of the draft immediately before opening the transcript command.
Transcript launch sequence
the paced `/transcript` command is followed by carriage return
the test requests the external pager while delayed composer and viewport frames may still be queued.

requirement: External less round trip and minimal live-region restoration
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: The test waits up to 20 seconds for `grow-transcript-` on the visible screen as the less transcript-file signal, waits 300 ms, injects `q` to quit the pager, waits up to 10 seconds for MINIMAL_IDLE_SENTINEL to reappear, then allows two seconds for redraw settling and reads screen_contents. The intended round trip includes less alternate-screen use and terminal `rmcup` restoration, but this file observes those stages through the path and restored idle sentinels.
scenarios: Pager foreground
the transcript command exposes a visible `grow-transcript-` path
the test treats less as foreground and sends `q` after a 300 ms settling interval.
Live region restored
less exits and MINIMAL_IDLE_SENTINEL returns within ten seconds
the test captures the restored visible screen after an additional two-second settle period.
Restore timeout
the idle sentinel does not return before the deadline
the test fails through the harness wait diagnostic instead of evaluating stale-screen assertions.

requirement: Restored screen artifact and panic assertions
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: On the captured screen, the test requires exactly one MINIMAL_IDLE_SENTINEL and exactly one `ctrl+o transcript` info row, rejects the submitted command `❯ /transcript` and killed draft `zetaquxdraft`, rejects any visible row starting with a literal `[`, rejects the substring `panicked`, and finally calls quit_minimal. The test function is ignored, so these are executable assertions only when explicitly selected outside the default suite.
scenarios: Single idle chrome
the pager round trip completes and screen_contents is captured
the idle status and transcript info strings each occur exactly once.
No stale prompt artifacts
the restored screen is checked for the queued command and killed draft
neither stale string is present.
No torn escape row
the restored screen is split into lines
no line begins with a literal `[` fragment.
No panic and cleanup
all screen assertions pass
the screen contains no `panicked` marker and quit_minimal is invoked.

requirement: SubagentCatalogPane SHALL adapt bundled agent names into ListItem entries with a nonselectable Agents header, stable name-derived identities, styled labels, and label-based search text.
contract: CatalogEntry::content SHALL return its prebuilt styled Line; stable_id SHALL return its id; is_selectable SHALL be false for header entries and true for agents; search_text SHALL return label. sync_from_bundle SHALL clear existing entries, return empty for no cache or no agents, otherwise add an Agents header and one indented styled entry per state.agents name. Header and agent ids SHALL be computed from DefaultHasher inputs "Agents" and name respectively.
scenarios: No bundle
has_cache is false or agents is empty
entries are cleared and no header/item is retained.
Agent projection
cache exists with one or more agent names
one Agents header plus ordered agent entries are created.
Header selection
ListPane selects the header id
is_selectable is false and selected_entry returns None.
Agent selection
ListPane selects a name-derived agent id
selected_entry can return ("agent", label).
Search
ListPane filters entries
search text is the raw agent label, while styled content keeps the visual two-space indent.
Refresh
bundle contents change
sync clears and rebuilds entries, preventing stale agents.

requirement: SubagentCatalogPane::new SHALL configure a ListPaneState for a non-following, non-wrapping, searchable/filterable catalog with copy, visual select, and goto-line actions disabled.
contract: new SHALL create empty entries, ListPaneState::new_with_config(WrapMode::NoWrap,false,config), ListPaneStyle::default, and OverlayState::hidden. The config SHALL set follow_enabled=false, wrap_toggle_enabled=false, search_enabled=true, copy_enabled=false, show_selection_when_unfocused=false, visual_select_enabled=false, filter_enabled=true, and goto_line_enabled=false. Default SHALL delegate to new.
scenarios: Construction
a new pane is created
overlay is hidden, entries are empty, and list behavior matches the documented config.
Search/filter
user enters search or filter
search/filter are enabled and use ListPaneState.
Unsupported action
user requests copy, wrap toggle, follow, visual selection, or goto-line
the pane config leaves those features disabled.
Default
Default is requested
the same state as new is returned.

requirement: SubagentCatalogPane SHALL expose overlay visibility/state-change behavior, a bounded responsive desired height, selected-agent projection, and delegated key/paste/scroll/mouse handling.
contract: is_visible SHALL return overlay.visible. on_state_change SHALL close the list input bar only while the overlay is hidden. desired_height SHALL return 0 when hidden or view_height<12, return 1 for visible empty entries, and for visible entries cap height by entries.len, MAX_CATALOG_HEIGHT=8, and floor(view_height*0.15), with a minimum of 1. selected_entry SHALL resolve the selected stable id to a nonheader entry and return ("agent",label), otherwise None. handle_key SHALL reject empty entries and otherwise delegate list_state.handle_key_event; handle_paste SHALL delegate even when entries are empty; handle_scroll SHALL cap absolute lines to 1 for viewport<=5, 2 for 6..=10, and no additional cap for larger viewports before delegating; handle_mouse SHALL reject empty entries and otherwise delegate list_state.handle_mouse_event.
scenarios: Visibility
overlay.visible changes
is_visible mirrors it and hidden state closes input on_state_change.
Small viewport
pane hidden or view_height below 12
desired_height is zero.
Empty catalog
visible pane has no entries and enough height
desired_height is one.
Bounded height
visible nonempty catalog has large view
height is no more than eight rows, fifteen percent of view (floored), or entry count, with at least one row.
Selected agent
selected id resolves to nonheader entry
selected_entry returns agent plus label.
Header/stale selection
selected id is header or absent
selected_entry returns None.
Input delegation
key/paste/mouse events arrive
events route to ListPaneState with current entries and boolean consumption is returned.
Scroll cap
scroll event arrives in short viewport
requested magnitude is capped to one or two lines based on viewport height.

requirement: SubagentCatalogPane SHALL place its catalog inside accent/left/right block padding, render a neutral empty placeholder when no entries exist, and prepare/render the configured ListPane for nonempty entries.
contract: content_area SHALL shift x by HorizontalLayout::ACCENT + block_pad_left, preserve y/height, and saturating-subtract left plus block_pad_right from width. render SHALL render `No bundled Agents.` in gray_bright only when entries are empty and the inner area has positive width and height; it SHALL return without ListPane preparation for empty/zero inner areas. For nonempty entries it SHALL call list_state.prepare_layout(entries,inner.width,inner.height), build ListPane::new(entries), apply focused and list_style, and render into inner.
scenarios: Empty positive area
entries empty and padded inner area has dimensions
gray_bright No bundled Agents. is painted at inner origin.
Empty zero area
entries empty but inner width or height is zero
no placeholder is written and render returns safely.
Nonempty render
entries exist
layout is prepared with inner dimensions and ListPane renders with focus/style.
Padding
layout config has accent/left/right pads
content x and width account for those pads with saturating width.
Focused state
focused varies
the same value is passed to ListPane::focused.

requirement: The catalog pane SHALL project already loaded BundleState agent names without discovery, persistence, activation, copy side effects, or model mutation; callers own modal admission and agent switching.
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: sync_from_bundle only reads has_cache/agents and current Theme, rebuilds local entries, and does not discover or mutate BundleState. selected_entry returns a display tuple only; key/paste/mouse/scroll delegate to ListPaneState but this file does not translate selection into agent activation or viewer actions. Overlay visibility is read through OverlayState and list rendering is delegated to ListPane. The one inline test proves one cached agent projects and can be selected, but not no-cache/empty/height/render/input/duplicate-name behavior.
scenarios: Read-only bundle
a BundleState is supplied
catalog reflects current names without changing the bundle.
Selection handoff
an agent row is selected
caller receives ("agent",label) and decides what action to take.
Modal owner
overlay is hidden or shown
the pane reports/maintains visibility state but does not open/close the global modal.
Audit boundary
source is read with one inline test
only cached single-agent projection is runtime-tested; all other behavior remains source evidence.

requirement: Eighth-resolution progress glyph tables and legacy ConHost fallback
contract: The progress bar SHALL represent cell fill with a shared index domain 0..=8, using LEFT-fractional BLOCKS for normal terminals and the same-length SHADES table on legacy Windows ConHost. Index 0 SHALL be empty, index 8 SHALL be a full block, and partial_blocks SHALL select the table from crate::glyphs::is_legacy_windows_console so callers do not branch on host type.
scenarios: Normal terminal glyphs
is_legacy_windows_console returns false
partial cells use BLOCKS entries (▏▎▍▌▋▊▉) and full cells use █.
Legacy ConHost glyphs
is_legacy_windows_console returns true
partial cells use SHADES entries (░▒▓) while the empty and full endpoints remain compatible.
Shared index domain
the two glyph tables are selected by partial_blocks
both tables have nine entries with the same empty index and full-block index.

requirement: Clamped and rounded fill decomposition at eighth-cell resolution
contract: cell_breakdown SHALL clamp the input fraction to 0.0..=1.0, convert width multiplied by the fraction into eighths, round to the nearest eighth, and return (whole_cells, remainder_eighths) with whole_cells bounded by width and remainder_eighths in 0..=7. A full value SHALL consume the requested width and an out-of-range high value SHALL behave as full rather than adding cells.
scenarios: Whole-cell fill
width is 4 and value is 0.5
cell_breakdown returns two full cells and zero remainder.
Partial-cell fill
width is 4 and value is 0.125
cell_breakdown returns zero full cells and four eighths for the first partial cell.
Nearest eighth
width is 5 and value is 0.03
the 1.2-eighth result rounds to one eighth instead of lighting a full cell.
Out-of-range value
value is greater than 1.0
the fraction is clamped and width 4 produces four full cells with no remainder.

requirement: Shared per-cell sequence and styled span contract
contract: bar_cells SHALL be the single cell sequence used by both public renderers, yielding exactly width items in left-to-right order: full glyphs for whole cells, at most one partial glyph at the first remainder cell, and spaces thereafter. progress_bar_spans SHALL return one static span per cell, applying fg plus bg to filled symbols and bg-only style to empty spaces, while preserving the selected host glyph table.
scenarios: Empty bar
width is 5 and value is 0.0
the sequence contains five empty-space cells.
Full bar
width is 5 and value is 1.0
the sequence contains five full-block cells.
Mixed fill
width is 4 and value is 0.5
the first two cells are full and the remaining cells are empty.
Partial fill
width is 4 and value is 0.125
the first cell is the half-block glyph and the next cells are spaces.
Span styling
progress_bar_spans is called with fg and bg colors
filled spans carry both colors and empty spans carry only the track background.

requirement: Bounded ratatui buffer rendering with track and fill styles
contract: render_progress_bar SHALL paint at most width horizontal cells beginning at (x,y), using the same bar_cells output and the same filled/empty styles as progress_bar_spans. Filled cells SHALL use fg on bg, empty cells SHALL use bg-only style, and a coordinate outside the supplied Buffer SHALL be skipped without panicking.
scenarios: Paint within buffer
the requested row and width fit in the Buffer
each target cell receives the corresponding glyph and style.
Horizontal offset
x or y is nonzero
painting begins at the supplied coordinate and retains left-to-right cell order.
Clamped fill in buffer
value is outside 0.0..=1.0
the Buffer reflects the clamped cell breakdown rather than an over-wide write.
Out-of-bounds target
x+i,y is outside the Buffer area
that cell is skipped and rendering continues without a panic.

requirement: Context usage hover bar composition through the shared progress renderer
contract: When context usage data is available, context_bar_line_for_session SHALL pass the percentage fraction to progress_bar_spans for the hover bar, use the quantized urgency color as fill foreground and theme.bg_highlight as track background, append one base-background gap and a five-character secondary-colored percentage, and keep the resulting hover Line width equal to the default compact token line.
scenarios: Hover progress composition
hovered is true with used and positive total token counts
the line contains the shared progress spans followed by one gap and a fixed-width percentage.
Width invariant
the same token pair is rendered hovered and non-hovered
both Lines have the same display width, including the minimum-width 0 / 9 case.
Bar scaling
compact token strings have different natural widths
the progress bar width grows with the default token string length.
Unavailable or gateway data
token inputs are missing/zero or gateway_chat is true
no context line is produced and progress_bar_spans is not used.

requirement: Runtime facts and stable diagnostic identity
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: RuntimeFact<T> represents Available(T), NoReply, or Unavailable and derives clone/debug/equality semantics. DiagnosticId stores static domain and item strings, DiagnosticId::new is a const constructor, and Display formats the identifier as `domain.item`; the identifier also derives Hash for map/set use. The model defines stable crate-local IDs for notification protocol fallback, focus tracking unavailable, sandbox profile conflict, clipboard delivery unverified/unavailable, newline fallback, iTerm2 clipboard permission, and VS Code SSH non-ASCII caveats.
scenarios: Runtime response available
a probe produced a value
the value can be represented as RuntimeFact::Available(value).
Runtime response missing
a probe did not answer or cannot run
the model distinguishes RuntimeFact::NoReply from RuntimeFact::Unavailable.
Stable identifier formatting
a DiagnosticId has domain `terminal` and item `ssh-wrap`
Display yields `terminal.ssh-wrap`, while equality and hashing use both fields.

requirement: Diagnostic report counting and finding disposition
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: DiagnosticReport groups DiagnosticFacts, DiagnosticFinding values, and ProbeNote values. issue_count counts findings whose disposition is Issue and adds one implicit issue when ClipboardFacts::delivery is not confirmed unless a clipboard-delivery-unverified or clipboard-delivery-unavailable finding is already present. recommendation_count counts findings whose disposition is Recommendation. DiagnosticFinding carries a stable id, disposition, message, optional ManualRemediation, optional AutomaticRemediation, and optional note; FindingDisposition has Issue and Recommendation variants.
scenarios: Explicit issues
a report contains Issue findings
issue_count includes each such finding exactly once.
Unconfirmed clipboard without named finding
clipboard delivery is not confirmed and neither clipboard delivery ID appears in findings
issue_count adds one implicit clipboard issue.
Named clipboard delivery finding
clipboard delivery is not confirmed but an unverified or unavailable clipboard finding exists
issue_count does not add a second implicit issue for the same delivery condition.
Recommendations
a report contains Recommendation findings
recommendation_count equals the number of those findings.

requirement: Terminal, multiplexer, color, keyboard, and newline fact schema
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: DiagnosticFacts stores terminal identity, xtversion RuntimeFact, multiplexer and optional Byobu backend, SSH state, TmuxFacts, ColorFacts, optional KeyboardFact, optional NewlineFact, and ClipboardFacts. TmuxFacts separately records extended_keys and set_clipboard option facts, allow_passthrough support and option facts; TmuxOptionFact distinguishes Available(String), Unsupported, Unavailable, and Error, while TmuxSupportFact has Supported, Unsupported, Unavailable, and Error. ColorFacts stores a RuntimeFact<ColorLevel>, available ThemeKind values, and total theme count. KeyboardFact stores ModifierDelivery and HostOs. NewlineFact distinguishes VTE with optional version, XtermJs with terminal identity, and unavailable Kitty keyboard protocol.
scenarios: Terminal snapshot
a diagnostic snapshot is converted into facts
