the report can retain terminal, multiplexer, SSH, color, keyboard, and newline evidence in their typed fields.
Tmux option result
a tmux query returns a string, unsupported, unavailable, or error
TmuxOptionFact preserves the corresponding state and string only for Available.
Tmux passthrough capability
the support probe returns one of its four outcomes
TmuxSupportFact preserves Supported, Unsupported, Unavailable, or Error independently of the option value.
Newline fallback
the terminal cannot provide the preferred keyboard path
NewlineFact identifies VTE version evidence, xterm.js terminal evidence, or NoKittyKeyboardProtocol.

requirement: Clipboard route and environment fact schema
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: ClipboardFacts records native, tmux, OSC 52, and wrap-sink route booleans; the native tool name and NativeClipboardPreflight; Osc52Capability; DisplayServer; container-no-display state; DataControlFact; ClipboardDelivery; and an optional compatibility fix string. DataControlFact distinguishes Available, Missing, Unavailable, Error, and NotApplicable. The fix field is explicitly a compact compatibility projection while detailed policy and remediation are carried by named findings.
scenarios: Clipboard route projection
diagnostic collection determines native, tmux, OSC 52, or wrap paths
the route booleans and supporting capability fields remain available in ClipboardFacts.
Data-control result
Wayland data-control probing returns an observed, missing, unavailable, or error state, or the platform is irrelevant
DataControlFact preserves Available, Missing, Unavailable, Error, or NotApplicable.
Compatibility fix projection
legacy consumers need a compact clipboard fix value
ClipboardFacts::fix may hold an optional string while detailed remediation remains in findings.

requirement: Probe notes and live-TUI requirement classification
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: ProbeNote stores a static probe name, ProbeStatus, and optional message. ProbeStatus distinguishes Unsupported, Unavailable, and Error. probe_requires_live_tui returns true only when status is Unavailable and the probe is exactly runtime.fullscreen-active, runtime.kitty-flags-pushed, or runtime.xtversion; all other probe names and statuses return false.
scenarios: Unavailable live evidence
one of the three runtime probes is unavailable
probe_requires_live_tui returns true.
Unavailable non-live evidence
a different probe is unavailable
probe_requires_live_tui returns false.
Unsupported or error
a listed live probe has Unsupported or Error status
probe_requires_live_tui returns false even though a ProbeNote can preserve the status and optional message.

requirement: Shared overlay operations SHALL return an OverlayAction that distinguishes an ignored key from a state change and from focus transfer to scrollback or prompt.
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: OverlayAction::Ignored means no state change and an unconsumed key; Changed means the caller should redraw; FocusScrollback and FocusPrompt mean the overlay relinquishes focus to the indicated surface. OverlayAction::consumed returns false only for Ignored and true for every other variant.
scenarios: Ignored remains available to content handling
A structural router does not recognize the key
It returns None or OverlayAction::Ignored and the caller can pass the key to pane-specific handling.
State change requests redraw
A toggle, hide, escape, or fullscreen operation changes overlay state
It returns OverlayAction::Changed and the caller treats the event as consumed and redraws.
Tab transfers to scrollback
A focused overlay handles Tab
It returns FocusScrollback and consumed() is true.
Space transfers to prompt
A focused overlay handles Space
It returns FocusPrompt and consumed() is true.

requirement: Toggleable overlay panes SHALL expose explicit visible, hidden, show, and hide state operations over independent visibility, focus, and fullscreen flags.
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: OverlayState contains public visible, focused, and fullscreen booleans and derives Default, Clone, Copy, and Debug. visible() creates visible=true with focus and fullscreen false; hidden() is the all-false default. show() sets visible=true without changing focus or fullscreen. hide() clears all three flags and returns Changed, allowing external lifecycle cleanup such as session end.
scenarios: Visible but unfocused initialization
A pane should appear automatically while the prompt remains active
OverlayState::visible() yields visible=true, focused=false, fullscreen=false.
Hidden initialization
A pane starts closed
OverlayState::hidden() yields all flags false.
Auto-show preserves other state
An external caller invokes show()
visible becomes true while focused and fullscreen are left as they were.
Lifecycle cleanup hides entirely
A session-end or clear path invokes hide()
visible, focused, and fullscreen all become false and Changed is returned.

requirement: The shared overlay shortcut SHALL cycle hidden panes to visible-and-focused, visible-unfocused panes to focused, and visible-focused panes to hidden.
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: OverlayState::toggle always returns Changed. If visible is false it sets visible and focused true; if visible is true but focused is false it sets focused true; otherwise it clears visible, focused, and fullscreen. The hide branch explicitly exits fullscreen so closing a focused pane leaves no fullscreen residue.
scenarios: Open and focus hidden pane
toggle() is called while visible=false
The pane becomes visible and focused and reports Changed.
Focus already visible pane
toggle() is called while visible=true and focused=false
The pane remains visible and becomes focused.
Close focused pane
toggle() is called while visible=true and focused=true
The pane becomes hidden, unfocused, and non-fullscreen.
Repeated shortcut is consumed
Any of the three states receives its pane shortcut
toggle() always returns a consumed Changed action.

requirement: Overlay navigation SHALL provide one-level Esc/q dismissal, Tab transfer to scrollback, Space transfer to prompt, and Ctrl-F fullscreen toggling.
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: tab_out clears fullscreen and focused while retaining visible and returns FocusScrollback. escape clears only fullscreen when already fullscreen, preserving visible and focus; otherwise it hides and unfocuses the pane and returns Changed. space clears fullscreen and focus while retaining visible and returns FocusPrompt. toggle_fullscreen flips fullscreen and returns Changed without inspecting visibility or focus.
scenarios: Leave fullscreen to the overlay
escape() is called with fullscreen=true
fullscreen becomes false while visible and focused remain true.
Dismiss non-fullscreen overlay
escape() is called with fullscreen=false
visible and focused become false and Changed is returned.
Tab out
tab_out() is called from an overlay
fullscreen and focused clear, visible remains unchanged, and focus is assigned to scrollback.
Return to prompt
space() is called from an overlay
fullscreen and focused clear, visible remains true, and focus is assigned to the prompt.
Toggle fullscreen
toggle_fullscreen() is called
fullscreen flips and Changed is returned.

requirement: Focused overlay input SHALL route Ctrl-F through handle_overlay_key and route Tab, Esc, plain q, and Space through handle_overlay_nav_key, returning None for content-specific keys.
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: handle_overlay_key recognizes KeyCode::Char('f') whenever the modifiers contain CONTROL, even if additional modifiers are present, and returns the fullscreen toggle action; all other keys return None. handle_overlay_nav_key recognizes Tab and Esc regardless of modifiers, q only when modifiers are exactly NONE, and Space regardless of modifiers; each returns its corresponding OverlayState action. The caller is responsible for invoking the navigation router only when no input bar is open, as documented by the split API.
scenarios: Ctrl-F works with an input bar
handle_overlay_key receives Char('f') with CONTROL
It toggles fullscreen and consumes the key without delegating to content.
Non-structural key reaches pane content
handle_overlay_key receives an unrecognized key
It returns None and does not mutate OverlayState.
Navigation keys transfer or dismiss
handle_overlay_nav_key receives Tab, Esc, plain q, or Space
It returns the matching state action and consumes the key.
Ctrl-Q stays application-owned
handle_overlay_nav_key receives q with CONTROL
It returns None so the app-level quit shortcut remains available.
Input-bar ownership is caller-selected
An input bar is active
The caller can omit handle_overlay_nav_key while still allowing handle_overlay_key to process Ctrl-F.

requirement: Overlay routing SHALL keep the app-level Ctrl-Q quit binding available and SHALL apply the implementation's explicit modifier rules for fullscreen and prompt-transfer keys.
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: q is accepted only with KeyModifiers::NONE, preventing Ctrl-Q from being consumed by an overlay. Ctrl-F uses contains(KeyModifiers::CONTROL), so additional modifier bits do not prevent fullscreen handling. Space matches by key code without a modifier guard, so modified Space is also routed to FocusPrompt. Tab and Esc likewise match by key code alone. These are source-level routing rules and do not assert terminal key normalization.
scenarios: Plain q closes
q arrives with no modifiers
handle_overlay_nav_key calls escape().
Modified q is delegated
q arrives with any modifier such as CONTROL
handle_overlay_nav_key returns None.
Control-containing f toggles
f arrives with CONTROL plus optional additional modifiers
handle_overlay_key toggles fullscreen.
Modified Space follows key-code match
Space arrives with a modifier
handle_overlay_nav_key still calls space().

requirement: Pager dashboard module façade and public ownership boundary
contract: The dashboard façade SHALL expose the six named submodules layout, peek, peek_tail, render, row and state, and SHALL re-export the documented render entrypoints, row model/classifier/sort helpers, and state types/parsers/loaders from their owning submodules. The façade SHALL keep concrete dashboard behavior in those submodules; importing through views::dashboard provides the stable public boundary without introducing a second implementation of rendering, row construction or state persistence.
scenarios: Submodule ownership
a caller imports dashboard layout, peek, rendering, row or state functionality
the corresponding named submodule remains available through the dashboard module façade.
Render re-exports
a caller needs the dashboard widget or overlay chrome helpers
render_dashboard, DashboardOverlayChrome, HeaderPromoCta, popup_rect, render_dashboard_session_header, render_dashboard_session_overlay and render_popup_overlay are available from views::dashboard.
Row re-exports
a caller builds or classifies visible dashboard rows
DashboardRow, RowBadge, build_rows, build_rows_with_roster, classify_subagent, classify_top_level, roster_activity_to_state and sort_rows resolve through the façade.
State re-exports
a caller manipulates dashboard identity, filter, grouping, persisted state or parsing
the documented DashboardState, row/filter/grouping/location/pending-dispatch types plus load_persisted, parse_filter and parse_row_state_token resolve through the façade.

requirement: Dashboard feature flag precedence and default behavior
contract: dashboard_enabled SHALL return false when the process environment contains GROW_AGENT_DASHBOARD exactly equal to the string `0`, before consulting persistence. Otherwise it SHALL return the persisted [dashboard].enabled value from state::load_persisted_enabled, and SHALL default to true when that loader returns None. Other environment values SHALL not disable the dashboard through this override.
scenarios: Environment disable
GROW_AGENT_DASHBOARD is exactly `0`
dashboard_enabled returns false without relying on persisted configuration.
Persisted disable
the environment override is absent or has another value and persisted enabled is false
dashboard_enabled returns false from the persisted setting.
Default enabled
the environment does not equal `0` and persisted loading returns None
dashboard_enabled returns true.
Nonzero environment value
GROW_AGENT_DASHBOARD has a value other than `0`
the environment branch does not disable the feature and persistence/default resolution continues.

requirement: Session switch hint command selection by screen mode and dashboard availability
contract: session_switch_hint_command SHALL return Some(`/resume`) in minimal mode regardless of the dashboard feature flag, because the dashboard is refused there but the session picker remains available. Outside minimal mode it SHALL return Some(`/agents`) only when dashboard_enabled is true; when the dashboard is disabled it SHALL return None so session-created and fork banners fall back to a plain session-id form.
scenarios: Minimal mode
minimal is true and the dashboard environment override is disabled
the hint is `/resume` and does not advertise `/agents`.
Enabled non-minimal mode
minimal is false and dashboard_enabled is true
the hint is `/agents`.
Disabled non-minimal mode
minimal is false and dashboard_enabled is false
the helper returns None.
Banner integration
session-created or fork-marker code receives the returned option
minimal banners advertise `/resume`, enabled non-minimal banners may advertise `/agents`, and disabled banners omit the refused command.

requirement: Shared leader cluster and client attachment setup
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: The test starts LeaderCluster at DEFAULT_ROWS by DEFAULT_COLS. LeaderCluster::start creates one ContentController-backed shared home, creates a fixed `.grow/leader-e2e.sock`, and resolves the pager binary. It sets the first response to turn_sentinel(1), spawns client A with the leader socket, waits for WELCOME_SCREEN_SENTINEL within LEADER_TIMEOUT, submits PROMPT with carriage return, and waits for A to render turn 1 within STREAM_TIMEOUT. The cluster then attaches client B through the same leader with --resume and waits for B to render the replayed turn.
scenarios: Leader client startup
the shared cluster starts and client A is spawned
A uses the explicit leader socket, reaches the welcome sentinel, and completes the first prompt turn.
Shared-session attach
client B is attached through the same LeaderCluster after A has committed turn 1
B resumes the shared session and observes turn_sentinel(1).
Content fixture
the cluster content response is set before each turn
the mock server emits a deterministic turn-specific sentinel payload.

requirement: Exactly-once replay visibility for the attached client
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: After B observes the first turn, the test reads B screen_contents and requires turn_sentinel(1) to occur exactly once. The check is a visible-screen substring count and treats a duplicated replay as a failure; it does not count durable session records or inference requests.
scenarios: Single replay
B has attached and rendered the first turn
B screen_contents contains the first-turn sentinel exactly once.
Duplicated replay
the first turn is rendered more than once in B screen_contents
the exact-count assertion fails with the captured B screen.

requirement: Bidirectional live streaming across leader clients
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: The test changes the shared mock response to turn_sentinel(2), submits `again` through A using submit_turn, and waits for B to observe the second sentinel. It then changes the response to turn_sentinel(3), submits `more` through B, and waits for A to observe the third sentinel. submit_turn re-presses Enter after bounded wait attempts until the sentinel appears or STREAM_TIMEOUT expires, preventing a dropped submit from being mistaken for a streaming failure.
scenarios: Leader-to-viewer stream
A submits the second prompt after B has attached
B observes turn_sentinel(2) within STREAM_TIMEOUT.
Viewer-to-leader stream
B submits the third prompt
A observes turn_sentinel(3) within STREAM_TIMEOUT.
Dropped submit recovery
an initial Enter is dropped while clients contend
submit_turn may re-inject Enter until the requested sentinel appears, while its helper contract treats an already-sent prompt as an extra no-op.

requirement: Three-turn transcript projection and liveness checks on both panes
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: For each client A and B, the test resizes the PTY to 200 rows by DEFAULT_COLS, waits 600 ms, and repeatedly injects the SGR mouse-wheel-up sequence in up to four bursts of fifty events with increasing delays, followed by a 500 ms update. If turn 1 remains absent it sends keys::ESC twice with 200 ms updates before another wheel sequence. Within a 20-second deadline it requires each of turn_sentinel(1), turn_sentinel(2), and turn_sentinel(3) to occur exactly once, requires the process to remain running, and rejects a `panicked` marker.
scenarios: Transcript recovery to top
a client has all three turns but earlier content may be above the viewport
the resize and wheel/ESC retry loop eventually exposes all three turn sentinels or reaches the 20-second deadline.
Exactly-once transcript
all three sentinels are visible on a client screen
each sentinel occurs exactly once, rejecting dropped or duplicated turns.
Pane liveness
the client is checked after scrolling
PtyHarness::is_running is true and the visible screen does not contain `panicked`.

requirement: Leader survival after the spawning client exits
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: After both panes have the three-turn transcript, the test drops client A, pumps B for three seconds, requires B to remain running, requires B screen_contents to retain turn_sentinel(3), and then calls B quit. The test function is ignored, so these lifecycle assertions run only when explicitly selected with the documented ignored-test command.
scenarios: Spawning client exits
A is dropped while B remains attached to the shared leader
B stays alive after a three-second update and retains the third-turn sentinel.
Attached client cleanup
the survival assertion passes
B is explicitly quit through PtyHarness::quit.

requirement: The ignored leader PTY scenario SHALL start one shared LeaderCluster at the suite's default 50x120 geometry, configure a long sentinel-bearing mock response with 40 ms chunk delay, elect client A as leader, submit the shared PROMPT, and wait until the sentinel is visible while streaming before cancellation.
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: leader_reattach_cancellation_roundtrips_durable_log calls LeaderCluster::start(DEFAULT_ROWS, DEFAULT_COLS), configures ContentController::set_response with turn_sentinel(1) followed by filler repeated 40 times, and sets set_chunk_delay(Some(Duration::from_millis(40))). It spawns the leader client with spawn_leader(&[]), waits for WELCOME_SCREEN_SENTINEL within LEADER_TIMEOUT, injects PROMPT plus carriage return, and waits for turn_sentinel(1) within STREAM_TIMEOUT. The streaming sentinel closes the rewind window before Ctrl-C is sent, so the test exercises cancellation of an active turn rather than rewind handling.
scenarios: Shared cluster startup
the ignored test begins
one mock-backed leader cluster and fixed 50x120 PTY geometry are created or the test fails.
Paced long response
the test configures the content controller
the response contains the turn sentinel plus 40 repeated filler fragments and is emitted with a 40 ms chunk delay.
Leader election and prompt
client A is spawned and the welcome sentinel is visible
A submits the `go` prompt and waits for the turn sentinel.
Active streaming boundary
turn_sentinel(1) becomes visible within STREAM_TIMEOUT
the test proceeds to Ctrl-C cancellation after observing an active streamed turn.

requirement: After observing an active streamed turn, the leader PTY scenario SHALL send Ctrl-C, wait for the visible user-cancelled marker, poll the durable session log for turn_completed, and require stop_reason to equal cancelled.
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: The test injects keys::CTRL_C into client A, pumps 200 ms, waits for `Turn cancelled by user` within STREAM_TIMEOUT, then calls LeaderCluster::wait_for_turn_completed(STREAM_TIMEOUT). It asserts rec["stop_reason"] == "cancelled"; the persisted turn_completed record is the producer-side fail-before for later replay. No prompt_id or other record fields are asserted here.
scenarios: Cancel active turn
A is visibly streaming turn 1
Ctrl-C is injected while the prompt is empty and the harness pumps the leader for 200 ms.
User-facing cancellation
the cancellation path completes within STREAM_TIMEOUT
A renders `Turn cancelled by user`.
Durable terminal exists
the cluster's updates log is polled for turn_completed
wait_for_turn_completed returns a record instead of timing out.
Cancelled stop reason
the terminal record is returned
its stop_reason field is exactly `cancelled`.

requirement: Once cancellation is durably recorded, the leader scenario SHALL attach a keep-alive viewer and a fresh resume client through the same leader, and each client SHALL observe the prior turn sentinel without causing a new turn.
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: The test attaches `keep` after the cancellation, waits for turn_sentinel(1) within LEADER_TIMEOUT to establish replay and retain a second leader client, records inference_request_count, then attaches fresh client C while A is still alive and waits for the same sentinel within LEADER_TIMEOUT. The ordering intentionally avoids a cold --resume handshake racing A's teardown while still exercising durable-log replay through the shared leader.
scenarios: Keep-alive replay
turn_completed with stop_reason=cancelled has persisted
cluster.attach(&[]) creates a viewer and it sees turn_sentinel(1) within LEADER_TIMEOUT.
Fresh reattach while driver remains
keep is attached and A is still running
a new resume client C attaches to the same leader and sees turn_sentinel(1).
Same session rail
keep or C observes the sentinel
the test treats the replayed shared transcript as evidence that the clients are attached to the existing leader session.

requirement: After fresh client C has replayed the cancelled transcript, the scenario SHALL drop the original driver, allow leader disconnect processing, and require C to remain alive with the transcript visible and without active-turn or panic indicators.
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: The test drops A, pumps C for 500 ms, asserts c.is_running(), and asserts C still contains turn_sentinel(1). It invokes wait_for_labels_absent for `Waiting` and `Cancelling` with a five-second budget, then independently asserts that C's screen contains neither `panicked`, `Waiting`, nor `Cancelling`. The helper's return value is ignored; the explicit negative assertions are the final guards.
scenarios: Driver disconnect
client C has replayed turn 1
dropping A is followed by a 500 ms C update to allow leader disconnect handling.
Reattached liveness
disconnect processing settles
C remains running and still displays the cancelled transcript sentinel.
No active spinner
C's replay settles within five seconds
Waiting and Cancelling labels are absent.
No panic
the post-disconnect screen is inspected
the screen does not contain the `panicked` marker.

requirement: The fresh reattach SHALL be proven to replay from the durable log by preserving the mock inference request count from before C attaches through the post-disconnect assertions.
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: Immediately before creating C, the test records inference_request_count(cluster.content()). After C has replayed the sentinel, A has exited, and spinner/panic guards have run, it requires inference_request_count(cluster.content()) to equal the saved value. The helper counts only chat completions, Responses, or messages paths and intentionally ignores incidental GET requests such as models/settings.
scenarios: Capture pre-reattach count
keep has replayed the cancelled transcript and before C attaches
the current inference request count is saved.
Replay with no re-drive
C attaches and renders the prior sentinel
the final inference request count equals the saved count.
Incidental HTTP excluded
the helper evaluates recorded content-controller requests
non-inference GETs do not invalidate the no-new-turn assertion.

requirement: Padded wrapper construction and standard inset contract
contract: Padded::new SHALL retain a borrowed inner renderable and the supplied left/right column counts with no background by default. Padded::standard SHALL be equivalent to left=2 and right=1. with_bg SHALL be a chainable value builder that preserves the inner and padding values while setting the optional background color for the wrapper render.
scenarios: Custom padding
Padded::new receives an inner renderable and explicit left/right widths
the wrapper retains those dimensions and starts without a background override.
Standard padding
Padded::standard receives an inner renderable
the wrapper uses two left columns and one right column.
Background builder
with_bg is chained with a Color
the same wrapper is returned with that color selected for background filling.

requirement: Padded Renderable height projection
contract: The Padded Renderable implementation SHALL subtract left and right padding from the requested width with saturating subtraction, pass the resulting content width to inner.desired_height, and return the inner height unchanged. Padding therefore affects width available to content but does not add or remove rows.
scenarios: Normal width
requested width is greater than left plus right padding
the inner renderable receives exactly the remaining content width.
Standard height delegation
Padded::standard wraps a one-row inner renderable
desired_height returns one row while reserving three horizontal columns.
Width below padding budget
requested width is smaller than the nominal left plus right padding
the width passed to the inner renderable is clamped to zero rather than underflowing.
Composed wrappers
Padded wraps another Renderable decorator
height calculation continues through the inner wrapper without adding a vertical row.

requirement: Padded horizontal layout and inner content rendering
contract: For a positive render area, Padded::render SHALL divide the area horizontally into [left padding, a flexible content region, right padding] using Length(left), Min(0), and Length(right), and SHALL invoke inner.render only when the computed content region has positive width. The inner render receives the full content-region height and begins after the left padding, so content does not paint over the reserved columns.
scenarios: Offset content
a positive area has left padding and a content width
inner content starts at area.x plus the left padding and retains the area row range.
Right reservation
a positive area has both left and right padding
the flexible content region ends before the right padding reservation.
Insufficient content width
the horizontal layout produces a zero-width content region
the inner render is skipped.
Empty render area
area.width or area.height is zero
Padded returns before layout or inner rendering.

requirement: Padded background fill and content overwrite order
contract: When with_bg has selected a color, Padded::render SHALL apply a background-only Style to every addressable cell in the supplied area before rendering the inner content, thereby covering both padding and untouched content cells while allowing inner rendering to overwrite its own symbols/styles. Without a background option it SHALL leave existing buffer styles untouched until the inner render runs.
scenarios: Background across wrapper area
with_bg is set and the area is positive
all addressable cells in the area receive the selected background, including left/right padding and content cells.
Inner overwrite order
with_bg is set and inner.render paints content
the background is established first and inner content is rendered afterward in the content region.
No background override
with_bg was not called
Padded does not prepaint a background and delegates directly to the inner content after layout.
Buffer cell unavailable
the supplied Rect extends beyond the actual Buffer
the wrapper's background loop skips a missing cell through Buffer::cell_mut instead of dereferencing it.

requirement: Scalable shared-leader fan-out fixture
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: The ignored Tokio PTY test sets VIEWERS to two, starts one LeaderCluster at DEFAULT_ROWS by DEFAULT_COLS, and sets the shared mock response to turn_sentinel(1). LeaderCluster::start provides one ContentController-backed home and explicit leader socket; the local worker-thread and viewer count comments require increasing worker_threads together with VIEWERS if the fan-out is scaled.
scenarios: Viewer fan-out size
the test starts with VIEWERS = 2
one driver plus two viewer clients are exercised.
Shared fixture
the cluster starts and the first response is configured
all clients use the same mock-backed shared leader/session environment and turn-specific sentinel payload.
Scaling boundary
a maintainer increases VIEWERS
the source comment requires increasing the Tokio worker-thread budget and the per-viewer survival pump assumptions together.

requirement: Driver turn and exactly-once replay for every viewer
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: The driver spawns the leader with LeaderCluster::spawn_leader, waits for WELCOME_SCREEN_SENTINEL within LEADER_TIMEOUT, submits PROMPT, and waits for turn_sentinel(1) within STREAM_TIMEOUT. For each of the VIEWERS clients, LeaderCluster::attach creates a --resume client through the same leader; the test waits for turn_sentinel(1), pumps 500 ms so later replay batches are observed, and requires the viewer screen to contain the first-turn sentinel exactly once before storing the viewer.
scenarios: Driver first turn
the driver reaches the welcome screen and submits PROMPT
the driver renders turn_sentinel(1) within the streaming timeout.
Viewer replay
a viewer attaches through the shared leader after turn 1
the viewer renders the driver transcript and its visible first-turn sentinel occurs exactly once.
Empty or duplicate replay
a viewer screen lacks the sentinel or contains it more than once after the settle pump
the corresponding assertion fails with the viewer screen.

requirement: Driver-to-all-viewers live stream fan-out
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: After replay setup, the test changes the shared response to turn_sentinel(2), injects `again` plus carriage return into the driver, and waits for the driver to render turn 2. It then waits for every viewer to render the same sentinel, pumps each viewer for 500 ms to catch delayed duplicate frames, and requires exactly one visible occurrence in each viewer screen.
scenarios: Driver live turn
the shared response is set to turn 2 and the driver submits `again`
the driver observes turn_sentinel(2) within STREAM_TIMEOUT.
All-viewer fan-out
each attached viewer is waiting for turn 2
every viewer observes turn_sentinel(2) from the driver-driven stream.
Duplicate live frame
a viewer screen contains multiple turn-2 sentinels after settling
the exactly-once assertion fails for that viewer.

requirement: Viewer survival after driver exit and cleanup
contract: The implementation SHALL satisfy the following tested behavior: The test drops the spawning driver after turn 2, updates each viewer for three seconds, requires every viewer to remain running, rejects `panicked` on each viewer screen, and requires every viewer to retain turn_sentinel(2). It then consumes the viewer vector and calls PtyHarness::quit for each attached client. The local test is ignored and therefore these lifecycle assertions run only when the documented ignored-test command is selected.
scenarios: Driver exit
the driver is dropped while two viewers remain attached
each viewer remains running after a three-second pump and retains the turn-2 sentinel.
Viewer liveness
a viewer is checked after driver exit
its visible screen does not contain `panicked`.
Viewer cleanup
all survival checks pass
each viewer is explicitly quit through PtyHarness::quit.

requirement: The ignored leader PTY scenario SHALL start one shared LeaderCluster at the default 50x120 geometry, configure a sentinel-bearing completed response, elect client A as leader, submit the shared PROMPT, and observe the turn sentinel before attaching another client.

scenarios: Shared cluster startup
the ignored test begins

Completed response fixture

Leader election and prompt
A reaches the welcome sentinel

Turn rendered

It asserts rec["stop_reason"] equals end_turn and rec["prompt_id"] is a non-empty string. The record is treated as the producer-side fail-before for durable replay; no other fields or exact envelope are asserted.

requirement: The leader scenario SHALL preserve the leader across the original driver's exit with a keep-alive viewer, then attach a fresh resume client after A exits and require that C replays the completed transcript through the surviving leader.

It drops A before calling cluster.attach(&[]) for fresh client C; C must observe turn_sentinel(1) within LEADER_TIMEOUT. This ordering specifically tests reattach after the original driver exits while relying on the keep viewer to hold the leader up.

Shared durable rail

Waiting absence is documented as a regression guard because a finished turn clears the leader prompt slot and a fresh reattach should land Idle; it is not the durable-record fail-before.
scenarios: Replay settle
C has observed turn_sentinel(1)
wait_for_labels_absent pumps C until Waiting is absent or its five-second budget expires.
Client liveness
the settled screen is checked
C remains running.
No panic

C contains no `panicked` marker.
Idle presentation
the settled screen is checked

requirement: The fresh reattach SHALL preserve the mock inference request count and SHALL display the completed turn sentinel exactly once after an additional repaint window.

The helper counts only chat completions, Responses, or messages requests, ignoring incidental models/settings GETs.
scenarios: Capture pre-reattach count

the current inference request count is saved.
No inference re-drive

the final inference count equals the saved count.
Late replay batch window

the screen is sampled after a bounded extra repaint interval.
Exactly-once sentinel
the final screen snapshot is captured

requirement: Minimal PTY flush-left fixture and readiness contract
contract: The ignored Tokio PTY test SHALL start an isolated ContentController, set a deterministic MOCK_RESPONSE_SENTINEL response, spawn the pager through spawn_minimal with the minimal/no-leader fixture at DEFAULT_ROWS by DEFAULT_COLS, and enable terminal query responses through the helper. It SHALL wait for MINIMAL_IDLE_SENTINEL before asserting layout so the test observes the native minimal path rather than a cold-start or downgraded screen.

contract: After minimal readiness, and again after a completed prompt turn, the test SHALL verify that the first screen line containing each selected live or committed needle has zero leading ASCII spaces. The idle status `minimal · /help`, submitted user line `❯ go`, MOCK_RESPONSE_SENTINEL response and post-turn idle status SHALL therefore be flush-left at column zero, preserving the edge-to-edge minimal layout without the former block padding gutter.

the committed `❯ go` row, response row and live idle status each have zero leading ASCII spaces.
Response visibility

Leading spaces

the helper fails and reports the measured lead and line.

the helper accepts it as column-zero alignment.

requirement: Minimal parked-plan fixture and tool-call setup

The main test starts ContentController, sets a first response, spawns minimal at 20 rows by 100 columns with query responses enabled, waits for minimal readiness, submits a first `go` turn, waits up to 40 seconds for MOCK_RESPONSE_SENTINEL in full_text, and locates the session directory.

requirement: The ignored minimal PTY test SHALL start an isolated ContentController, configure a short MOCK_RESPONSE_SENTINEL response, spawn the default minimal fixture at DEFAULT_ROWS by DEFAULT_COLS, wait for minimal readiness, submit PROMPT, and wait for the response sentinel before layout assertions.

It then enumerates screen_contents lines, selects the last line whose trim is non-empty, defaults to row 0 if none exists, and requires last_non_blank < DEFAULT_ROWS - 10, which is <40.
